Standard abilities are reliable trained applications; Signature abilities are defining techniques with stronger effects and meaningful costs; each character may develop one Ultimate with scaled power, substantial costs, strong limitations, and a long cooldown or once-per-encounter/scene restriction. Do not grant an Ultimate automatically. Abilities that cost 0 points are valid freely available foundational techniques when explicitly granted by a power, trait, NPC, quest, or authored progression; they do not consume starting ability points and should remain limited by the ability's description, resources, cooldown, range, risk, and established power constraints.

generateAbilities.custom: Not a Voyage task: see generateLearnedAbilities (Created Abilities, Ability Stat Block, Improving and Team-Ups).

Chikara Tokyo.name: Chikara Tokyo
Chikara Tokyo.basicInfo: A unified, modern Tokyo realm of colorful districts, hero agencies, ordinary neighborhoods, criminal networks, apartments, workplaces, and waterfront operations, with Chikara Academy and its student life as one part of the city.

Chikara Tokyo.name: Chikara Tokyo
Chikara Tokyo.basicInfo: The unified Tokyo region, home to Chikara Academy and student neighborhoods, hero institutions and agencies, everyday businesses, criminal routes, apartments, and waterfront operations.
Chikara Tokyo.hiddenInfo: Walking and rail travel connect the city. Flight, swinging, portals, and teleportation provide alternate routes only when the character's abilities, range, anchors, and access permit them.

Chikara Academy.name: Chikara Academy
Chikara Academy.basicInfo: A prestigious superhero university in Tokyo combining rigorous academics, power training, rescue simulations, student life, supervised hero development, and coed dormitory living.

campus-footbridge.description: Raised pedestrian bridge connecting the academy to surrounding campus paths, with city lights and passing trains below. Suitable for brief meetings and farewells.

classroom-3c.description: Homeroom of Class 3C: rows of desks under tall windows, a scuffed lectern, and a power-control practice corner at the back where instructors run drills between lessons.

classroom-4d.description: Homeroom of Class 4D: a warm, slightly cluttered classroom with snack boxes on the teacher's desk, student artwork on the back wall, and the homeroom teacher's attendance sheets forever one drawer away.

classroom-5a.description: Homeroom of Class 5A: a bright upper-year classroom with lab benches along one side, a projector wall, and a quiet study nook the senior students treat as their own.

main-hall.description: Central hall with hero memorials, class rosters, schedules, Pulse kiosks, club notices, and Battle Test announcements.

north-rooftop-overlook.description: Accessible rooftop overlook with safety lighting, benches, and a wide view over Chikara District. Useful for late-night conversations, recovery, stargazing, and difficult decisions.

student-courtyard.description: Open paved courtyard between academic wings, with benches, shade trees, noticeboards, and room for casual conversations.

vending-machine-nook.description: Covered seating beside vending machines. Bright, public, and open late for casual meals, phone calls, awkward encounters, and nighttime scenes.

west-service-alley.description: Visible service alley along the academy wall for deliveries, maintenance carts, and quieter travel. It is not hidden.

Chikara Academy.hiddenInfo: A sealed sublevel beneath the academy contains records about early Ultra Force operations and may connect to the player's family history. This is hidden information and restricted access within the globally visible academy, not a hidden map location.

Old Tokyo Shrine Road.name: Old Tokyo Shrine Road
Old Tokyo Shrine Road.basicInfo: Historic shrine district with traditional restaurants, tea houses, antiques, tunnels, shops, and a preserved station.

heritage-store.description: Antique, charm, book, and traditional craft store.

lantern-restaurant.description: Traditional restaurant serving seasonal dishes near the shrine.

old-tokyo-station.description: Historic station connecting old and modern Tokyo.

tea-house.description: Restaurant and tea house for dates and negotiations.

Ultra Force Headquarters.name: Ultra Force Headquarters
Ultra Force Headquarters.basicInfo: Secure hero complex with operations, archives, training, medicine, stores, dining, communal barracks facilities, and a credentialed station. The barracks are reserved for Blacklisted recruits and provisional operatives whose story explicitly assigns them there. Everyday Zero's civilian dispatch coordinator remains based at Apartment 68; visiting Ultra Force Headquarters for work does not change the player's home or residence. Resolve "go home" using the player's established residence, not the barracks, unless a story explicitly establishes otherwise.

barracks.description: Monitored shared sleeping quarters for Blacklisted recruits and provisional operatives. These quarters are not assigned to ordinary civilian dispatch staff or Everyday Zero players. Only a story that explicitly places the player in Blacklisted recruitment or provisional housing may make the barracks their home. The random roommate shares the sleeping space, while privacy is limited and movement is logged.

command-mess.description: Hero cafeteria and restaurant for staff meals and briefings.

communal-bathroom.description: Shared barracks bathroom with communal showers, bath facilities, lockers, and strict schedules. Use only privacy-respecting, nonsexual comedy such as queue disputes, missing toiletries, plumbing problems, or harmless power accidents.

dispatch-floor.description: The dedicated Ultra Force dispatch floor: a wall of live incident boards, call consoles, response maps, agency status panels, secure phone lines, staffed routing desks, and a posted Ultra Force Dispatch Reference Guide. Dispatch coordinators assess callers, verify locations, check hero availability, route small local threats and practical paid-service cases to Hero for Hire responders, send specialized cases to the appropriate faction, escalate emergencies, and record follow-up reports. The floor includes adult civilian operations staff, pro heroes, supervised Blacklisted personnel, and coworkers; it is a workplace, not a student area.

hero-supply-store.description: Authorized store for costumes, support gear, field supplies, and recovery products.

operations-floor.description: Mission dispatch and monitoring floor where civilian calls, agency requests, police referrals, supernatural alerts, and hero availability are assessed. Dispatch staff triage each case, record details, choose an appropriate response, and route ordinary incidents to the faction or hero organization best suited to handle them.

Old Tokyo Lantern Quarter.name: Old Tokyo Lantern Quarter
Old Tokyo Lantern Quarter.basicInfo: Preserved neighborhood of lantern-lit alleys, craft workshops, seasonal food, and cultural events.

craft-row.description: Workshops selling ceramics, paper goods, charms, and crafts.

festival-court.description: Courtyard for performances, dances, and seasonal celebrations.

lantern-alley.description: Historic alley lined with lanterns, galleries, and food stalls.

seasonal-restaurant.description: Traditional dining room serving regional dishes and tea.

Old Tokyo Tea Market Street.name: Old Tokyo Tea Market Street
Old Tokyo Tea Market Street.basicInfo: Historic shopping street with groceries, tea merchants, gifts, and traditional restaurants.

grocery-stalls.description: Produce, preserved foods, spices, and ingredients.

Central Tokyo Station.name: Central Tokyo Station
Central Tokyo Station.basicInfo: Major public rail interchange with ticket counters, express platforms, route boards, and connections across Tokyo. When the player enters, a station attendant approaches to offer route and ticket help.

concourse.description: Large central concourse with maps, ticket machines, staffed counters, and departure boards. You can buy a train ticket here before boarding.

platforms.description: Platforms for Academy District, Old Tokyo, Tokyo Bay, Shadow District, and Ultra Force Headquarters. Boarding requires a valid ticket or approved access.

station-retail.description: Shops, cafés, lockers, and passenger services.

ticket-counter.description: Ticket office and automated machines. The game should tell the player they can buy a ticket here, select a destination, and pay the listed fare.

Imperial Palace East Gardens.name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
Imperial Palace East Gardens.basicInfo: Historic gardens and preserved palace grounds with stone walls, seasonal landscaping, paths, and civic landmarks.

garden-paths.description: Stone walls, lawns, seasonal trees, and historic foundations.

moat-walk.description: Scenic outer path beside water and fortified walls.

public-gate.description: Public entrance with visitor information and security guidance.

Chiyoda Civic Offices.name: Chiyoda Civic Offices
Chiyoda Civic Offices.basicInfo: Municipal offices handling permits, records, public services, neighborhood administration, and civic complaints.

public-counter.description: Public service counters for forms, permits, and resident questions.

waiting-hall.description: Seating and information boards for visitors.

Marunouchi Business Avenue.name: Marunouchi Business Avenue
Marunouchi Business Avenue.basicInfo: A polished office corridor of corporate towers, underground passages, restaurants, hotels, and weekday commuter traffic.

avenue.description: Wide office avenue with plazas, taxis, and business crowds.

tower-lobby.description: Corporate reception areas and visitor security desks.

underground-mall.description: Restaurants, cafés, shops, and connected pedestrian passages.

Tokyo Skytree Tower Complex.name: Tokyo Skytree Tower Complex
Tokyo Skytree Tower Complex.basicInfo: A landmark tower and commercial complex with observation decks, shops, restaurants, and broad views across Tokyo.

observation-deck.description: High viewing decks above the city.

tower-plaza.description: Public plaza beneath the tower with shops and event spaces.

Nakano Residential Arcade.name: Nakano Residential Arcade
Nakano Residential Arcade.basicInfo: A neighborhood shopping arcade serving apartment residents with groceries, bakeries, clinics, laundries, and family restaurants.

grocery-row.description: Markets, bakeries, pharmacies, and daily services.

Gearshift Support.name: Gearshift Support
Gearshift Support.basicInfo: Compact support-technology workshop where students help repair approved hero equipment, sort parts, and assist customers.

parts-counter.description: Components, diagnostic tools, and customer intake.

staff-office.description: Schedules, job records, and safety approvals.

workshop-floor.description: Repair benches and supervised prototype stations.

Page Turner Books.name: Page Turner Books
Page Turner Books.basicInfo: Independent bookstore with study tables, hero biographies, and a quiet inventory room.

stockroom.description: Inventory shelves and staff work area. A curious viper fang pendant rests in a forgotten storage crate.

Game Start Arcade.name: Game Start Arcade
Game Start Arcade.basicInfo: Colorful student arcade with competitive games, prize machines, after-school shifts, and a lively social scene.

arcade-floor.description: Cabinets, rhythm games, and prize machines.

prize-counter.description: Prize redemption and customer service desk.

staff-room.description: Break area, supplies, and shift board.

Crepe Expectations.name: Crepe Expectations
Crepe Expectations.basicInfo: Friendly crepe café with a compact kitchen, counter service, and student shifts.

Rescue Volunteer Desk.name: Rescue Volunteer Desk
Rescue Volunteer Desk.basicInfo: Public service desk connecting volunteers with approved welfare checks, visitor assistance, and community support.

help-desk.description: Reception for requests, directions, and volunteer intake.

quiet-room.description: Calm waiting room for visitors needing support.

records-room.description: Schedules, supplies, and supervised case files.

Uniform & Co..name: Uniform & Co.
Uniform & Co..basicInfo: Academy District clothing shop selling school uniforms, casual clothes, costume alterations, and practical accessories for students.

alterations-counter.description: Tailoring desk for repairs, adjustments, and costume-safe alterations.

back-workroom.description: Staff workroom with sewing machines and fabric supplies.

fitting-rooms.description: Private fitting stalls for uniforms and casual clothing.

sales-floor.description: Uniform racks, everyday clothing, bags, and approved accessories.

Hero Hobby Shop.name: Hero Hobby Shop
Hero Hobby Shop.basicInfo: A hobby store filled with hero collectibles, model kits, training memorabilia, craft supplies, and novelty power-themed merchandise.

checkout.description: Register, preorder desk, and raffle display.

craft-corner.description: Tables for painting models, assembling kits, and sharing hobby advice.

display-gallery.description: Rotating displays of famous heroes, academy memorabilia, and local artists.

main-floor.description: Shelves of figures, model kits, cards, comics, and hero merchandise.

Neon Karaoke.name: Neon Karaoke
Neon Karaoke.basicInfo: A colorful karaoke venue with private rooms where students celebrate, vent, practice songs, and build friendships after dark.

hallway.description: Neon-lit corridor leading to private karaoke rooms.

karaoke-room.description: Soundproof room for singing, conversations, challenges, and group scenes.

reception.description: Front desk with room bookings, song catalogs, and time packages.

snack-bar.description: Counter serving drinks and quick food to guests.

Midnight Diner.name: Midnight Diner
Midnight Diner.basicInfo: An all-night American-style diner in Chikara Tokyo, serving affordable comfort food twenty-four hours a day to students, workers, travelers, night-shift staff, and anyone who needs a booth and a quiet place to talk. The menu combines familiar American diner staples with a few practical Tokyo touches.

booths.description: Rows of private red-vinyl booths for families, dates, students, tired workers, and late-night conversations.

counter.description: Long counter with swivel stools, a coffee station, napkin holders, condiment caddies, and a view of the open kitchen. Regulars and night-shift workers often sit here.

dining-room.description: Warm all-night dining room with red vinyl booths, chrome-edged tables, counter seats, laminated menus, pie display, coffee refills, and large front windows showing the street outside.

kitchen.description: Open diner kitchen preparing burgers, cheeseburgers, fries, pancakes, waffles, eggs, bacon, grilled cheese, chicken sandwiches, milkshakes, coffee, pie, and rotating specials. A few rice bowls or other Tokyo-friendly options are available without changing the restaurant's American-diner identity.

Pulse Printworks.name: Pulse Printworks
Pulse Printworks.basicInfo: A small print and copy shop producing flyers, posters, club materials, event banners, and local campaign notices for the academy district.

design-booth.description: Computer station for layouts, posters, club flyers, and campaign materials.

front-counter.description: Order desk for printing, copying, binding, and design requests.

print-floor.description: Printers, cutters, binding machines, paper stock, and finished orders.

supply-room.description: Paper, ink, packaging, and staff storage.

Power Practice Studio.name: Power Practice Studio
Power Practice Studio.basicInfo: A supervised neighborhood studio offering safe power-control lessons, civilian exercises, and beginner sessions for students and residents.

equipment-room.description: Storage for protective gear, targets, and calibration tools.

observation-room.description: Viewing area for guardians, instructors, and controlled demonstrations.

practice-floor.description: Padded training space with adjustable barriers and safety monitors.

reception.description: Booking desk with lesson schedules, waivers, and instructor information.

Student Clinic.name: Student Clinic
Student Clinic.basicInfo: A walk-in neighborhood clinic serving academy students, residents, and workers with routine care, minor injuries, and referrals.

exam-room.description: Private room for routine examinations and minor injuries.

pharmacy-window.description: Dispensing window for approved prescriptions and care instructions.

reception.description: Check-in desk, seating, appointment board, and intake forms.

treatment-room.description: Treatment space for first aid, observation, and power-related precautions.

Riverside Food Market.name: Riverside Food Market
Riverside Food Market.basicInfo: A lively market near the river with produce stalls, prepared food, household basics, and inexpensive groceries for students and residents.

food-stalls.description: Quick meals, desserts, and rotating local vendors.

fresh-counter.description: Produce, prepared meals, and refrigerated goods.

market-exit.description: Street-facing exit beside delivery lanes and pedestrian paths.

market-hall.description: Covered market aisle with produce, pantry goods, and household supplies.

Open-Air Performance Stage.name: Open-Air Performance Stage
Open-Air Performance Stage.basicInfo: A public stage for school events, local musicians, Pulse broadcasts, festivals, speeches, and spontaneous student performances.

audience-plaza.description: Open public space with benches, food carts, and room for crowds.

backstage.description: Restricted preparation area for performers, staff, and equipment.

park-walkway.description: Path connecting the stage to nearby park and market routes.

stage.description: Raised performance platform with lighting, sound equipment, and event access.

Tokyo Tower.name: Tokyo Tower
Tokyo Tower.basicInfo: Iconic red communications tower and Central Tokyo landmark with observation decks, public event spaces, broadcast infrastructure, and a commanding view over the city.

broadcast-level.description: Communications equipment and broadcast infrastructure hidden above the public spaces.

main-observation-deck.description: Panoramic observation deck overlooking Tokyo and the surrounding districts.

observation-lobby.description: Visitor lobby and elevator access for the public observation decks.

service-access.description: Restricted maintenance and broadcast access used by authorized staff and emergency crews.

tower-foot.description: Landmark plaza with visitors, food stands, ticket booths, and public gatherings.

upper-deck.description: Higher observation level with exhibits, dramatic views, and special-event access.

Hero Agency Row.name: Hero Agency Row
Hero Agency Row.basicInfo: A Central Tokyo avenue lined with professional hero agencies, licensing offices, public relations firms, and internship opportunities.

agency-cafe.description: Café where assistants, interns, reporters, and heroes meet between appointments.

agency-street.description: Busy avenue of agency entrances, hero billboards, and professional support services.

public-relations-office.description: Media coordination and reputation-management offices serving hero agencies.

reception-lobby.description: Shared lobby for agency appointments, deliveries, and internship inquiries.

Pulse Media Tower.name: Pulse Media Tower
Pulse Media Tower.basicInfo: Central Tokyo broadcasting and news tower where hero coverage, interviews, public statements, and Fame-shaping stories are produced.

broadcast-lobby.description: Public lobby with news screens, visitor passes, and rotating hero coverage.

newsroom.description: Editors and reporters track incidents, academy news, hero performances, and public reaction. An old props drawer holds a plain metal band inscribed with unfamiliar letters.

press-room.description: Press briefing room for agency statements and major public events.

studio-floor.description: Television and streaming studios for interviews, debates, announcements, and live segments.

Tokyo Hero Plaza.name: Tokyo Hero Plaza
Tokyo Hero Plaza.basicInfo: A large public square honoring professional heroes through memorials, statues, event stages, demonstrations, and civic gatherings.

event-square.description: Open plaza for ceremonies, festivals, demonstrations, protests, and public hero appearances.

food-kiosks.description: Public food stalls and souvenir stands serving visitors and office workers.

hero-gallery.description: Indoor exhibit space displaying equipment, records, and licensed hero history.

memorial-walk.description: Path of hero statues, plaques, memorials, and historical displays.

Professional Hero Hospital.name: Professional Hero Hospital
Professional Hero Hospital.basicInfo: Specialized Central Tokyo hospital treating professional heroes, power-related injuries, emergency responders, and civilians affected by incidents.

emergency-entrance.description: Protected emergency intake for urgent injuries and incident victims.

outpatient-wing.description: Clinics for follow-up care, rehabilitation, and power-related assessments.

reception.description: Main desk handling appointments, visitors, records, and referrals.

rehabilitation-gym.description: Supervised recovery space for mobility, conditioning, and safe power rehabilitation.

trauma-ward.description: Secure treatment area for serious injuries and emergency observation.

visitor-lounge.description: Waiting area for families, agency staff, students, and authorized visitors.

Hero Licensing Bureau.name: Hero Licensing Bureau
Hero Licensing Bureau.basicInfo: Official Central Tokyo office handling hero licenses, permits, examinations, records, and regulated professional activity.

examination-wing.description: Testing rooms for written, practical, and renewal examinations.

public-lobby.description: Reception, information screens, forms, and visitor guidance.

records-counter.description: Secure counter for licenses, permits, identity checks, and official records.

staff-office.description: Restricted offices where examiners and administrators review applications.

Tokyo Metropolitan Government Office.basicInfo: Major civic office complex where public policy, emergency coordination, permits, city planning, and official hero oversight are handled.

council-wing.description: Meeting rooms and offices for metropolitan policy and public hearings.

emergency-coordination.description: Operations room coordinating city services during major incidents.

public-hall.description: Public service counters, notices, visitor screening, and city information.

restricted-briefing.description: Secure briefing room for authorized emergency and hero officials.

Executive Dining Tower.name: Executive Dining Tower
Executive Dining Tower.basicInfo: Upscale Central Tokyo dining venue where agency leaders, executives, officials, and ambitious professionals hold private meals and negotiations.

lobby.description: Elegant reception with reservations, security, and skyline elevators.

main-dining-room.description: High-end restaurant floor for formal meals and public networking.

private-suites.description: Reserved rooms for confidential meetings, negotiations, and celebrations.

skyline-terrace.description: Outdoor terrace with a sweeping view of Central Tokyo.

Hero Equipment Exchange.name: Hero Equipment Exchange
Hero Equipment Exchange.basicInfo: Licensed Central Tokyo marketplace for approved support gear, refurbished equipment, protective clothing, and regulated trade-ins.

fitting-bay.description: Supervised testing area for checking fit, mobility, and basic function.

secured-storage.description: Restricted storage for regulated equipment and high-value orders.

service-counter.description: Appraisals, repairs, trade-ins, and purchase paperwork.

showroom.description: Displays of approved support tools, protective equipment, and refurbished gear.

Metropolitan Police Headquarters.name: Metropolitan Police Headquarters
Metropolitan Police Headquarters.basicInfo: Major police headquarters coordinating investigations, emergency response, public safety, and official cooperation with licensed heroes. evidence-room.description: Restricted evidence storage and forensic intake.

investigations-wing.description: Case offices and interview rooms for authorized investigations.

locker-room.description: Officer lockers, changing benches, equipment checklists, and secure preparation space before or after a shift.

operations-center.description: Command floor coordinating citywide incidents and emergency response.

public-entrance.description: Visitor screening, public information, and report guidance.

secure-briefing.description: Controlled room for police, officials, and licensed hero briefings.

staff-cafeteria.description: A bright, functional cafeteria serving shift meals, coffee, vending-machine snacks, and informal conversation between officers, dispatchers, investigators, and support staff.

Fights in the fighting-ring and arena-floor must use context-appropriate opponents: powered villains, unlicensed vigilantes, mercenaries, criminal fighters, dangerous contractors, cursed or supernatural combatants, or other explicitly authored participants connected to the Crucible. prayer-hall.description: Quiet prayer hall for ceremonies, offerings, and respectful conversations.

temple-gate.description: Traditional gate opening onto the temple grounds and visitor path.

Hibiki House.name: Hibiki House
Hibiki House.basicInfo: A neighborhood music house preserving shamisen, taiko, flute, and folk-song traditions through lessons, rehearsals, and intimate performances.

instrument-room.description: Care and storage space for traditional instruments and costumes.

rehearsal-room.description: Practice room for ensembles, lessons, and seasonal performances.

small-stage.description: Intimate stage for recitals, folk music, and community events.

Inkstone Academy.name: Inkstone Academy
Inkstone Academy.basicInfo: A quiet school teaching brush calligraphy, seal carving, traditional composition, and disciplined artistic practice.

gallery-hall.description: Display corridor for scrolls, seals, competition pieces, and seasonal exhibits.

practice-room.description: Tatami room with low desks, brushes, ink, and paper for lessons.

school-entrance.description: Reception with class notices, student work, and registration information.

Lanternworks Storehouse.name: Lanternworks Storehouse
Lanternworks Storehouse.basicInfo: Community storage house for festival floats, masks, lanterns, banners, costumes, and ceremonial equipment used throughout the old district.

costume-room.description: Wardrobe room for festival clothing, masks, and performance accessories.

main-storage.description: Tall shelves and covered bays holding lanterns, masks, banners, and floats.

planning-room.description: Tables covered with route maps, schedules, and festival preparations.

storehouse-yard.description: Loading yard where volunteers inspect floats, carts, and festival equipment.

Sazanami Tea House.name: Sazanami Tea House
Sazanami Tea House.basicInfo: A serene tea house offering formal tea ceremonies, seasonal sweets, etiquette lessons, and carefully maintained garden rooms.

garden-gate.description: Simple gate leading into a quiet tea garden and waiting path.

garden-path.description: Stone path through the tea garden with a water basin and shaded plants.

tea-room.description: Tatami room for formal tea preparation, ceremonies, and conversation.

waiting-room.description: Shoes-off waiting room with seasonal scrolls and flower arrangements.

The Memory Vault.name: The Memory Vault
The Memory Vault.basicInfo: Public archive preserving maps, photographs, family records, hero history, local artifacts, and clues to events hidden beneath the old district.

catalog-desk.description: Archivist desk for requests, research guidance, and restricted-record applications.

exhibit-room.description: Rotating exhibits of local artifacts, historic tools, costumes, and neighborhood history.

reading-room.description: Quiet tables where visitors study maps, newspapers, photographs, and public records.

records-vault.description: Restricted storage for fragile documents, sealed files, and sensitive family histories.

Blueglass Aquarium.name: Blueglass Aquarium
Blueglass Aquarium.basicInfo: Public aquarium featuring local marine life, educational exhibits, conservation programs, and broad views of the bay.

coastal-gallery.description: Exhibits focused on Tokyo Bay habitats, shore life, and conservation.

deep-ocean-hall.description: Large tanks displaying deep-water species and dramatic underwater environments.

education-center.description: Classroom and workshop space for marine science and environmental programs.

main-entrance.description: Ticketing, visitor information, exhibits map, and daily program schedules.

Harborline Port.name: Harborline Port
Harborline Port.basicInfo: Working harbor handling ferries, cargo, patrol boats, fishing vessels, and everyday maritime traffic along the bay.

cargo-dock.description: Working dock for freight deliveries, fishing boats, and harbor supplies.

ferry-terminal.description: Passenger ferry boarding area connecting waterfront routes and nearby districts.

harbor-gate.description: Main entrance with berth schedules, access notices, and waterfront traffic information.

harbor-office.description: Administrative office handling permits, berth assignments, manifests, and local harbor coordination.

passenger-pier.description: Open pier for ferries, sightseeing boats, and scheduled harbor crossings.

warehouse-yard.description: Storage and loading area for maritime goods and maintenance supplies.

Rescuewake Pier.name: Rescuewake Pier
Rescuewake Pier.basicInfo: Waterfront launch point for hero boats, emergency transports, patrol craft, and authorized harbor operations.

launch-platform.description: Boarding platform for authorized hero transport and rapid waterfront deployment.

operations-dock.description: Restricted dock for patrol craft, supply boats, and emergency response vessels.

pier-entrance.description: Public gate with schedules, access notices, and harbor safety information.

rescue-slip.description: Protected slip for rescue launches and emergency medical transfers.

Tideway Market.name: Tideway Market
Tideway Market.basicInfo: Busy waterfront market with seafood vendors, prepared food stalls, local crafts, and everyday harbor commerce.

craft-row.description: Small shops selling nautical goods, souvenirs, and local handmade products.

food-stalls.description: Casual stalls serving hot meals, snacks, drinks, and seasonal specialties.

market-gate.description: Main entrance with vendor signs, daily specials, and harbor traffic.

seafood-hall.description: Fresh seafood counters, auction displays, and local fishmongers.

Baywatch Terrace.name: Baywatch Terrace
Baywatch Terrace.basicInfo: Elevated waterfront viewpoint offering skyline views, harbor watching, public events, and quiet evening scenes above the bay.

event-platform.description: Small platform for festivals, public announcements, and seasonal gatherings.

lower-terrace.description: Accessible terrace with benches, signs, and views across the harbor.

upper-deck.description: Highest viewing level with panoramic skyline and water views.

Lifeline Harbor.name: Lifeline Harbor
Lifeline Harbor.basicInfo: Coastal emergency facility supporting maritime rescue, disaster response, evacuation drills, and harbor safety operations.

command-room.description: Dispatch and coordination room for harbor incidents and rescue operations.

harbor-gate.description: Controlled entrance with response notices, safety briefings, and visitor clearance.

training-yard.description: Open area for water rescue practice, evacuation drills, and equipment exercises.

Seabreeze Station.name: Seabreeze Station
Seabreeze Station.basicInfo: Waterfront rail station serving the harbor, with ticket counters, bay-line platforms, route boards, and ferry connections nearby. When the player enters, a station attendant approaches to offer route and ticket help.

concourse.description: Waterfront concourse with maps, ticket machines, and passenger services. You can buy a train ticket here before boarding.

ferry-link.description: Walkway toward harbor ferries and rescue docks.

platforms.description: Bay-line platforms for Central Tokyo. Boarding requires a valid ticket.

ticket-counter.description: Bay-line ticket office and machines. The game should tell the player they can buy a train ticket here, choose Central Tokyo, and pay the listed fare.

Campus Corner Mart.name: Campus Corner Mart
Campus Corner Mart.basicInfo: Convenience store near the student quarter, open late for snacks, supplies, errands, and casual encounters.

counter.description: Checkout counter and quick conversations with staff.

store-floor.description: Food, drinks, toiletries, stationery, and seasonal goods.

Common Ground.name: Common Ground
Common Ground.basicInfo: Neighborhood center with clubs, tutoring, workshops, and public services.

club-hall.description: Rooms for student clubs and meetings.

community-cafe.description: Affordable café for locals and students.

Student Commons.name: Student Commons
Student Commons.basicInfo: A student-friendly plaza with shops, cafés, parks, dates, and a neighborhood train station.

rooftop-diner.description: Casual restaurant with student meals, booths, and evening date seating.

shopping-street.description: Student stores, clothing, gifts, and convenience shops.

student-market.description: Affordable stores for school supplies, accessories, gifts, and necessities.

Koban Corner.name: Koban Corner
Koban Corner.basicInfo: A small neighborhood police box handling lost property, directions, minor incidents, and local safety reports near the academy district station.

back-office.description: Secure records and equipment room for officers on duty.

front-desk.description: Public counter for reports, directions, and lost-property claims.

waiting-bench.description: Small public waiting area for visitors and witnesses.

Riverside Green.name: Riverside Green
Riverside Green.basicInfo: Riverside green space with walking paths, practice lawns, food trucks, and quiet conversation spots.

food-truck-lane.description: Rotating food vendors serving casual meals and desserts.

practice-lawns.description: Open fields for harmless movement drills and club activities.

quiet-grove.description: Tree-covered benches for private talks and reading.

riverside-bridge.description: Pedestrian bridge overlooking the academy district.

riverwalk.description: Waterfront promenade for dates, jogging, and evening walks.

Academy Gate Station.name: Academy Gate Station
Academy Gate Station.basicInfo: Public rail station serving the Academy District, with ticket counters, route boards, platforms, and student-friendly transit services. When the player enters, a station attendant approaches to offer route and ticket help.

concourse.description: Main concourse with route maps, ticket machines, staffed counters, and information screens. You can buy a train ticket here before boarding.

platforms.description: Platforms for trains to Chikara Academy Campus and Central Tokyo. Boarding requires a valid ticket or approved access.

station-retail.description: Cafés, convenience shops, and student services.

ticket-counter.description: Staffed ticket booth and machines. The game should tell the player they can buy a ticket here, choose a destination, and pay the listed fare.

The Student Quarter.name: The Student Quarter
The Student Quarter.basicInfo: Student apartments, study lounges, convenience stores, and courtyards surrounding the academy neighborhood.

convenience-row.description: Small shops selling snacks, stationery, toiletries, and gifts.

residential-courtyard.description: Apartment courtyards where students relax and meet after class.

student-bus-stop.description: Local transit stop connecting the quarter to the plaza and academy.

study-lounge.description: Shared study space with tutoring tables and vending machines.

Support Street.name: Support Street
Support Street.basicInfo: Small support companies and costume repair shops serving academy students.

supply-cafe.description: Café popular with technicians and students.

Night Owl Mart.name: Night Owl Mart
Night Owl Mart.basicInfo: A brightly lit convenience store between Chikara Academy Station and the student apartments, open late for snacks, school supplies, toiletries, quick meals, and chance encounters.

counter.description: Checkout counter with hot snacks, ticketed promotions, and casual conversations.

stockroom.description: Delivery area and employee-only storage for supplies and late-night restocking.

store-floor.description: Aisles of drinks, prepared meals, stationery, toiletries, and emergency supplies.

Clubhouse Row.name: Clubhouse Row
Clubhouse Row.basicInfo: Student clubhouses for hobbies, rehearsals, cooking, gaming, and social events.

club-cafe.description: Small café run by student clubs.

cooking-club.description: Practice kitchen for optional cooking activities.

game-room.description: Casual room for games and friendship scenes.

Chikara Student Residences.name: Chikara Student Residences
Chikara Student Residences.basicInfo: Anime-style student apartments where characters live, rest, study, cook, and host relationship scenes. Each student has a private one-person room on the same residential floor with shared facilities: a communal kitchen, laundry room, separate shared bathrooms, lounges, and outdoor common areas. Dormitory rooms 4-01 through 4-19 are authored residence areas; Dormitory 4-18 remains reserved for the player in classroom story starts.

residence-front-step.description: Covered front step and entry plaza.

shared-girls-bathroom.description: Shared girls' bathroom with private toilet and shower stalls. Preserve privacy and appropriate access.

shared-kitchen.description: Communal kitchen for meals, cooking, and casual residence scenes.

study-lounge.description: Shared room for homework, quiet conversations, and residence notices.

Campus Fresh Market.name: Campus Fresh Market
Campus Fresh Market.basicInfo: Campus grocery store supplying ingredients, snacks, toiletries, and daily necessities.

checkout-cafe.description: Counter for coffee, sandwiches, and gossip.

fresh-food-aisle.description: Produce, dairy, eggs, and chilled ingredients.

market-entrance.description: Entrance with specials and student discounts.

pantry-aisle.description: Rice, noodles, spices, drinks, and snacks.

Academy Walk.name: Academy Walk
Academy Walk.basicInfo: Covered arcade with clothing, gifts, electronics, school supplies, and support accessories.

uniform-shop.description: Uniforms, casual clothes, shoes, and alterations.

The Commons Table.name: The Commons Table
The Commons Table.basicInfo: Affordable restaurant where students eat, work part-time, and build relationships.

dining-room.description: Casual room with booths and group tables.

private-booths.description: Quiet booths for dates and difficult talks.

Chikara Gate Station.name: Chikara Gate Station
Chikara Gate Station.basicInfo: Secure campus station where enrolled students and authorized visitors can buy tickets and board trains to Tokyo districts. When the player enters, a station attendant approaches to offer route, ticket, and academy-permission help.

concourse.description: Academy transit hall with route boards, student access checks, ticket machines, and staff assistance. You can buy a train ticket here before boarding.

platforms.description: Platforms for Academy District and approved connections through Central Tokyo. Boarding requires a valid ticket and any required academy authorization.

ticket-counter.description: Campus ticket counter and student transit desk. The game should tell the player they can buy a ticket here, choose a destination, and pay the listed fare; school-hour permission may still be required.

Hero Field Complex.name: Hero Field Complex
Hero Field Complex.basicInfo: Outdoor training zone for rescue drills, mobility practice, controlled sparring, and team exercises.

field-complex.description: Training fields with adjustable terrain and safety barriers.

flood-course.description: Water-and-current course for aquatic rescue practice.

mobility-track.description: Walls, ramps, platforms, and timed traversal routes.

observation-tower.description: Instructor tower for reviewing team tactics.

rescue-village.description: Mock neighborhood for evacuation and disaster-response drills.

Pixel Riot Arcade.name: Pixel Riot Arcade
Pixel Riot Arcade.basicInfo: Arcade hiring students for cabinet maintenance assistance, prize counter service, floor monitoring, and evening customer support.

front-desk.description: Entry desk handling tokens, memberships, questions, and customer issues.

game-floor.description: Arcade floor needing monitoring, cleanup, and basic player assistance.

prize-counter.description: Prize exchange and inventory station for tickets and merchandise.

staff-room.description: Small staff area for breaks, schedules, and shift instructions.

Gearshift Support Shop.name: Gearshift Support Shop
Gearshift Support Shop.basicInfo: Support-equipment retailer offering part-time work in customer service, inventory, repairs, demonstrations, and hero gear organization.

inventory-room.description: Storage area for stock, deliveries, labels, and equipment records.

repair-counter.description: Work area for intake, basic maintenance, testing, and customer requests.

showroom.description: Display floor for approved support items, costumes, tools, and training accessories.

WorkLink Exchange.name: WorkLink Exchange
WorkLink Exchange.basicInfo: Central job board connecting students and residents with legal part-time shifts, pay details, schedules, and employer instructions.

job-board.description: Notice wall and digital board listing shifts, pay, hours, and requirements.

Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters.name: Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters
Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters.basicInfo: A fortified supervillain agency headquarters occupying a sealed forty-eight-story skyscraper above an abandoned financial district. The agency presents itself as a legitimate security consultancy while coordinating criminal contracts, covert weapons, protected metahuman operations, mercenary deployments, and assassination work. Most floors are offices, storage, residences, laboratories, security infrastructure, or restricted operational space.

containment-lab.description: A hidden laboratory where the agency tests suppressants and amplifiers on captured powered people. Researchers, automated defenses, unstable subjects, and a power-suppressing specialist create a rescue-or-pursuit encounter.

evidence-office.description: A records room containing contracts, political protection payments, target intelligence, assassination dossiers, and proof that official reports were altered. An archivist, security detail, and timed data purge force an investigation under pressure.

executive-floor.description: A restricted upper floor protected by powered lieutenants, invisible hunters, regeneration specialists, armored bodyguards, and an emergency response team. Rival agents, assassination clients, and captured witnesses may alter the route to the target.

ground-elevators.description: A bank of reinforced elevators and biometric access gates connecting the lobby to the tower's forty-eight floors. Security staff can lock individual cars, redirect them, or trap passengers between checkpoints.

loading-bay.description: An underground cargo entrance for contraband, power-enhancing drugs, weapons, prisoners, armored vehicles, and mercenary teams. An armored convoy, explosive haulers, drug-enhanced bruisers, drone swarms, and a security lieutenant defend it.

operations-floor.description: A fortified mid-tower operations level where criminal contracts are assigned, mercenary teams are briefed, powered assets are tracked, and extraction routes are coordinated. The floor can become a command center, an ambush site, or a contested objective.

public-lobby.description: A polished reception hall hiding criminal operations behind a legal front. Guards, shielded enforcers, combat drones, a disguised powered bodyguard, frightened staff, and a staged hostage scene confront intruders.

rooftop.description: The exposed roof of the forty-eight-story skyscraper: rain-dark concrete, antenna masts, maintenance structures, helipad markings, service access, and a panoramic view over the abandoned financial district. It is a lonely insertion and extraction point, covered by floodlights, cameras, sniper nests, powered sentries, and rapid-response routes from the upper floors. A contractor may sit here alone before an operation while a handler speaks through an ordinary Bluetooth earbud; once the alarm begins, the roof becomes a lethal kill zone.

security-control.description: The surveillance and communications hub controlling cameras, doors, elevators, alarms, drones, and turrets. Tactical operators, a lockdown team, a handler with armed escorts, and falsified mission records defend it.

street-approach.description: Rain-slick perimeter streets beneath the tower. Patrols, snipers, armored response vans, powered scouts, cameras, and civilians trapped behind a security cordon create the first encounter.

target-suite.description: A hardened private suite containing a protected supervillain target, personal superpowered guards, defensive constructs, and possible reinforcements. A contract may demand assassination, but the encounter must allow killing, restraint, capture, rescue, negotiation, or abandoning the objective. One Blacklisted member faces the mission's fatal turning point here or during the approach.

warehouse-floor.description: A concealed storage level with drug shipments, restraints, evidence lockers, unstable powered test subjects, containment beasts, turret nests, coerced workers, and an elite warehouse commander.

Tokyo Curse Squad Headquarters.name: Tokyo Curse Squad Headquarters
Tokyo Curse Squad Headquarters.basicInfo: A concealed headquarters beneath a restored shrine compound in Old Tokyo. The Tokyo Curse Squad gathers here to shelter cursed-item wielders, magical practitioners, and supernatural power users; negotiate with spirits; research dangerous artifacts; and protect the surrounding neighborhood.

archive-vault.description: A warded archive containing cursed objects, magical texts, family records, spirit contracts, and containment cases. Every item is catalogued because careless handling can awaken it.

containment-ward.description: A reinforced medical and holding area for cursed artifacts, possessed objects, injured supernatural members, and entities that cannot safely return to the streets.

mission-room.description: A map room displaying Old Tokyo wards, spirit routes, artifact sightings, missing-person reports, and requests for discreet supernatural assistance. Members receive rescue, containment, investigation, negotiation, and escort assignments here.

reception-hall.description: A hidden meeting hall where new members, heroes, spirits, and neighborhood elders negotiate access, protection, and supernatural disputes.

ritual-chamber.description: A circular chamber for spellwork, pact renewal, exorcism, magical training, and controlled experiments. Protective seals fail if a practitioner ignores the agreed limits.

shrine-courtyard.description: A quiet restored shrine courtyard with protective ropes, paper charms, and a sealed entrance beneath the main altar. Locals visit without knowing the headquarters lies below.

tea-room.description: A calm traditional room used for meals, confidential conversations, mediation, and negotiations with Kurokawa contacts or skeptical hero officials.

training-yard.description: An enclosed underground courtyard for practicing supernatural abilities, cursed-item control, close combat, and nonlethal restraint without exposing Old Tokyo.

Tokyo Curse Squad Headquarters.hiddenInfo: The headquarters predates modern hero licensing. Beneath the archive is an older sealed chamber whose pact may protect Old Tokyo—or bind the entire Tokyo Curse Squad to an unknown supernatural power.

Pulse Afterdark.name: Pulse Afterdark
Pulse Afterdark.basicInfo: A stylish all-ages-by-time nightlife venue in Central Tokyo with music, dancing, performances, private booths, and a late-night café. Its programming changes by hour, allowing ordinary social scenes alongside celebrity events, Spark dates, and discreet meetings.

backstage.description: Performer preparation area and service corridor where artists, staff, guests, and suspicious activity may intersect.

entrance-lobby.description: Neon-lit entrance with coat check, ticketing, event checks, and a visible code of conduct.

late-night-cafe.description: A calmer café section serving food and non-alcoholic drinks, suitable for conversations, recovery, Spark dates, and unexpected meetings.

main-floor.description: Dance floor and stage for DJs, live music, hero-themed performances, student showcases, and crowded social encounters.

private-booths.description: Reserved seating for dates, group conversations, negotiations, and quieter scenes away from the music.

Pulse Afterdark.hiddenInfo: The club's owner quietly bans predatory behavior and cooperates with trusted staff, medics, and security contacts when a guest is in danger. A locked service room contains old event ledgers that may connect performers, heroes, villains, and supernatural visitors.

The Hero's Afterparty.name: The Hero's Afterparty
The Hero's Afterparty.basicInfo: A supervised campus-adjacent nightlife venue for adult Chikara Academy students and approved guests, with music, dancing, performances, karaoke, Spark dates, and late-night social scenes.

entrance-lobby.description: Secure entrance with event check-in, coat storage, accessibility support, and a visible consent and power-safety code.

nightclub-floor.description: Dance floor with student DJs, themed nights, safe lighting, and carefully monitored power effects.

performance-stage.description: Small stage for student bands, hero-brand showcases, karaoke, club fundraisers, and comedy nights.

student-lounge.description: Quiet seating and café area for conversation, group gatherings, Spark dates, and cooling down after performances.

The Hero's Afterparty.hiddenInfo: The venue is independent from the academy but maintains a conduct agreement with campus staff. Security quietly contacts faculty, medics, or trusted heroes when a guest is in danger. Its event book contains connections between students, performers, agencies, villains, and supernatural visitors.

Nightshade Exchange Relay.name: Nightshade Exchange Relay
Nightshade Exchange Relay.basicInfo: A discreet Tokyo contact point for the global Nightshade Exchange. New operators can begin through the Nightshade app without visiting in person, while the relay handles identity checks, equipment, payments, emergency extraction, and higher-risk contracts, including optional assassination listings.

contract-room.description: A secured room with encrypted terminals, paper files, payment terms, and rotating job listings from Nightshade Exchange cells around the world. Some listings involve assassination, while others offer surveillance, sabotage, extraction, protection, or information work.

exit-alley.description: A narrow service alley used for discreet arrivals, departures, dead drops, and emergency exits.

front-room.description: A plausible private office and waiting room where visitors verify an invitation, identity, or referral before receiving contract information.

Nightshade Exchange Relay.hiddenInfo: The Nightshade app is the easiest entry point for new players. It offers an onboarding profile, beginner contracts, payment previews, risk labels, anonymous messaging, and optional in-person relay access. The app never guarantees safety or legality. Contracts may involve ordinary crime, villain operations, assassination, coercion, rescue, information, or betrayal. Assassination listings must identify the requested outcome and known civilian risk, but target identity, client motives, and evidence may be unreliable. Players can investigate, refuse, negotiate, choose surveillance or extraction instead, expose the client, betray the broker, or leave the network. Distinguish suspects and jobs by evidence rather than assuming every contact is a supervillain.

Chikara Community Gym.name: Chikara Community Gym
Chikara Community Gym.basicInfo: An affordable neighborhood gym with free weights, cardio equipment, mats, lockers, and open floor space for general conditioning and supervised martial-arts practice.

locker-room.description: Lockers, showers, water stations, and a small first-aid cabinet.

main-floor.description: A busy training floor with machines, weights, mats, and enough open space for footwork and conditioning drills.

mat-room.description: A padded room for stretching, grappling drills, mobility work, and controlled partner practice.

Chikara Community Gym.hiddenInfo: Characters can train Close Quarters Combat here through regular practice, partner drills, conditioning, and instruction. Progress requires time and effort; the gym does not grant instant skill levels or assume a character has a trainer.

Redline Boxing Club.name: Redline Boxing Club
Redline Boxing Club.basicInfo: A serious boxing gym known for disciplined coaching, heavy bags, technical drills, controlled sparring, and amateur bouts.

conditioning-corner.description: Jump ropes, medicine balls, pads, and equipment for footwork, endurance, and striking drills.

reception.description: A small front desk with membership information, class schedules, and notices for supervised bouts.

ring-floor.description: A boxing ring surrounded by heavy bags, speed bags, mirrors, and coaches correcting stance, guard, timing, and combinations.

Redline Boxing Club.hiddenInfo: Redline specializes in boxing fundamentals and controlled sparring. Characters can build Close Quarters Combat through lessons, drills, and consensual practice, with injury and recovery handled realistically.

Harborline Boxing Academy.name: Harborline Boxing Academy
Harborline Boxing Academy.basicInfo: A waterfront boxing school that combines traditional boxing instruction with practical self-defense, fitness classes, and community outreach.

classroom.description: A small room for rules, fight analysis, strategy, and lessons on safe, lawful self-defense.

entrance.description: A waterfront entrance with class boards, community notices, and a view toward the harbor.

recovery-room.description: A supervised space for hydration, stretching, ice, first aid, and post-training assessment.

training-hall.description: A bright hall with two rings, padded walls, heavy bags, and coaches teaching boxing, defense, distance, and controlled takedown transitions.

Harborline Boxing Academy.hiddenInfo: This academy can support both Close Quarters Combat training and character development through mentorship, discipline, and community relationships. It does not automatically grant formal credentials or assume the character joins a faction.

The Crucible Training Ring.name: The Crucible Training Ring
The Crucible Training Ring.basicInfo: A reinforced private training ring attached to the Crucible, offering brutal practice, sparring, and combat coaching for operators willing to accept dangerous terms.

equipment-bay.description: Protective gear, wraps, training weapons, and recovery supplies available under the Crucible's rules.

observer-gallery.description: A shadowed gallery where recruiters, gamblers, instructors, and rivals watch training sessions.

training-ring.description: A reinforced ring with hard lighting, battered pads, observation balconies, and equipment chosen for punishing close-range drills.

The Crucible Training Ring.hiddenInfo: Training here can improve Close Quarters Combat through high-risk sparring and specialized coaching, but injuries, debts, reputation changes, recruitment pressure, and exposure to criminal networks are possible. Do not force a character to accept terms or participate in lethal fights.

Deadbeats Club.name: Deadbeats Club
Deadbeats Club.basicInfo: A shared four-bedroom house in Tokyo designed as an open sandbox hub for solo or multiplayer characters. For the Deadbeat Club story start, this is the player's current home and residence: phrases such as "go home" resolve here unless the player explicitly changes residence. The house supports cooperative scenes, private downtime, planning, conflict, guests, and departures into the wider city.

balcony.description: A narrow balcony overlooking Tokyo rooftops, useful for fresh air, private conversations, watching the street, or noticing unusual activity.

bathroom.description: A shared bathroom with a shower, sink, medicine cabinet, and limited privacy. Residents decide schedules, supplies, and boundaries.

bedroom-1.description: A private bedroom reserved for a player or resident chosen by the group. Its furniture, decorations, locks, and privacy rules are player-directed.

bedroom-2.description: A private bedroom reserved for a player or resident chosen by the group. Its furniture, decorations, locks, and privacy rules are player-directed.

bedroom-3.description: A private bedroom reserved for a player or resident chosen by the group. Its furniture, decorations, locks, and privacy rules are player-directed.

bedroom-4.description: A private bedroom reserved for a player or resident chosen by the group. Its furniture, decorations, locks, and privacy rules are player-directed.

common-room.description: The shared living room and kitchen form the social center of the house, with a dining table, couches, storage, and doors leading toward every bedroom. Players can plan together, cook, host guests, argue, relax, or leave for the city.

fire-escape.description: A visible fire escape reached from the balcony, overlooking neighboring rooftops. Suitable for late-night conversations and quiet observation, subject to safety and weather.

front-step.description: The house's visible front step and small entry landing, where residents wait for rides, receive deliveries, meet guests, or talk under the streetlight.

laundry-corner.description: A cramped laundry and utility corner off the common room, with cleaning supplies, a washer, and household notices. Ordinary chores and low-stakes conversations happen here.

rooftop-access.description: A shared rooftop access landing above the house, with a broad city view and enough space to sit away from the street. Visible and reachable, though building rules and weather may restrict use.

side-alley.description: A publicly visible side alley beside the house, with bins, utility pipes, and a view toward the neighborhood street. Useful for deliveries, tense conversations, and optional encounters.

Deadbeats Club.hiddenInfo: The Deadbeats Club is a neutral sandbox hub for solo or multiplayer play, not an automatic academy, faction, or romance route. For the Deadbeat Club story start, treat Deadbeats Club as the player's current residence and resolve "go home" here unless the player explicitly establishes another home. A solo player may occupy one bedroom and manage the house independently; a group may use up to four bedroom slots. Privacy, access, guests, chores, shared expenses, house rules, relationships, ownership, jobs, powers, and obligations remain player-directed. Keep legal hero work, ordinary employment, criminal offers, and other survival paths open-ended.

MealDrop Fulfillment Hub.name: MealDrop Fulfillment Hub
MealDrop Fulfillment Hub.basicInfo: A busy urban grocery and prepared-food dispatch center serving the MealDrop app, with shelves for essentials, restaurant pickup lanes, courier staging, and refrigerated storage.

cold-storage.description: Refrigerated and frozen storage for groceries, drinks, medical-safe foods, and restaurant ingredients.

courier-bay.description: A loading area where bicycle, scooter, and walking couriers collect orders for nearby deliveries.

dispatch-floor.description: Workers assemble grocery baskets and prepared-food orders beside route screens, packing stations, and insulated delivery bags.

MealDrop Fulfillment Hub.hiddenInfo: MealDrop is primarily an ordinary service location and is not automatically a quest hub. Characters may work here, collect orders, solve delivery problems, or encounter ordinary NPCs. Do not turn routine food delivery into a crisis unless player choices or current world events support it.

Tokyo Financial District Exchange.name: Tokyo Financial District Exchange
Tokyo Financial District Exchange.basicInfo: A regulated financial services center with bank branches, brokerage offices, card support desks, payment services, and public investment education.

banking-hall.description: A public banking hall for account services, transfers, card support, identity checks, and payment questions.

brokerage-lounge.description: A supervised space for market information, brokerage support, investment education, and lawful trading assistance.

service-entrance.description: A side entrance used by staff, couriers, and scheduled appointments.

Tokyo Financial District Exchange.hiddenInfo: This is an ordinary financial-services location, not a guaranteed source of money. Account approval, loans, credit, trading access, and investment outcomes depend on established identity, funds, legal status, records, and player decisions. Financial crime, fraud, market manipulation, and stolen credentials create legal and faction consequences.

Chikara Academy Campus Faculty Housing.name: Chikara Academy Campus Faculty Housing
Chikara Academy Campus Faculty Housing.basicInfo: Private one-bedroom faculty apartments on the Chikara Academy campus, with shared kitchens, common rooms, staff facilities, and quiet residential corridors for teachers and authorized faculty.

faculty-apartment-1-bedroom.description: A private one-bedroom apartment assigned to a faculty member, with a bedroom, bathroom, compact living space, desk, and kitchenette. It is the player's starting home for the new academic year.

faculty-common-room.description: A comfortable shared lounge for faculty residents, with seating, noticeboards, campus schedules, and a place for informal introductions and staff conversations.

faculty-corridor.description: A quiet residential corridor connecting private faculty apartments to the shared common room and kitchen. Staff may pass through between campus duties without being forced into social scenes.

shared-kitchen.description: A communal faculty kitchen with refrigerators, counters, tea supplies, simple cooking equipment, and a dining table used by staff residents at irregular hours.

Chikara Academy Campus Faculty Housing.hiddenInfo: Faculty members have separate private apartments. Shared spaces make casual faculty relationships possible, while private apartments preserve boundaries and personal downtime. Faculty housing is not a clinic, bar, or criminal headquarters.

Misfit Hero Agency Headquarters.name: Misfit Hero Agency Headquarters
Misfit Hero Agency Headquarters.basicInfo: A licensed but black-sheep hero agency on Hero Agency Row, assigned daily missions despite its poor reputation. The agency is underfunded, overworked, and full of improvised repairs, but the newly graduated player and dysfunctional teammates gradually turn it into a found-family home base. The player's private apartment occupies the floor directly above the agency, while the other agency members each have their own private apartment in the same converted building.

agency-street.description: The agency's entrance on Hero Agency Row, with public foot traffic, reporters, neighboring agencies, delivery workers, and occasional clients or protesters. The black-sheep agency remains licensed, but its reputation makes every daily arrival visible.

azrael-apartment.description: The agency director's private apartment in the converted building above and behind the agency offices. It includes a cramped living space, a work desk covered in licensing paperwork, controlled smoking areas, and private space to recover after managing the team.

briefing-room.description: A glass-walled briefing room with city maps, case screens, agency regulations, and a whiteboard covered in half-erased plans. Daily mission briefings, strategy, performance reviews, and arguments over agency orders happen here.

director-office.description: A small office for the agency director, evaluations, licensing paperwork, budget warnings, disciplinary conversations, and difficult decisions about the team's future. The director assigns or relays daily missions and manages the agency's black-sheep status.

equipment-bay.description: A cluttered equipment bay for costumes, support gear, spare parts, transport maintenance, and emergency repairs. Gear disputes and improvised upgrades are common after the team's daily assignments.

luna-apartment.description: A teammate's private apartment in the converted agency building. Its safety plan, grounding objects, locked equipment storage, quiet space, and carefully managed access support autonomy while reducing risk during power instability. Entry remains privacy- and consent-based except for genuine emergencies.

med-bay.description: A modest agency first-aid room for stabilization, injury checks, recovery planning, and deciding when a case requires Professional Hero Hospital. Daily missions may end here without forcing the player back into action before recovery.

player-apartment.description: A private apartment directly above the agency headquarters, assigned to the newly graduated player. It has a bedroom, bathroom, small living area, work desk, storage for hero equipment, and enough separation to decompress while remaining close enough to respond to daily dispatches.

reception-dispatch.description: A cramped reception and dispatch area with ringing phones, case folders, public complaints, client requests, and a mission board that receives new assignments every day. The team must report for daily dispatch even when the job is embarrassing, dangerous, or politically inconvenient.

shared-kitchen.description: A compact communal kitchen stocked with cheap groceries, instant meals, mismatched mugs, and notes about whose turn it is to clean. It is available for casual team scenes and practical household routines before and after daily assignments.

team-lounge.description: The agency's shared lounge with mismatched couches, a small dining table, vending machines, personal clutter, and the unofficial emotional center of the team. Arguments, meals, apologies, and found-family bonding happen here between daily missions.

tess-apartment.description: A teammate's private apartment in the converted agency building. It has practical storage, recovery space, spare blankets, meal supplies, and room to step away from caretaking duties when needed.

training-room.description: A reinforced but imperfect training room with padded flooring, repair patches, target equipment, and a damage report clipboard. The team drills, argues about technique, and learns to cover one another's weaknesses between daily missions.

Misfit Hero Agency Headquarters.hiddenInfo: The agency's poor reputation is partly inherited from failed leadership, but its case records contain evidence that the team was repeatedly given impossible assignments. The headquarters receives daily work because senior agencies use it as a pressure valve for politically awkward, low-prestige, or high-risk cases. The converted building's private apartments allow agency members and the player to live near one another without erasing privacy or consent. Shared meals, drinking nights, arguments, and unexpected support gradually create found-family bonds.

Apartment 68.name: Apartment 68
Apartment 68.basicInfo: A modest rented apartment assigned to the player near the police district. It is private, ordinary, and practical: a bedroom, small living area, kitchenette, bathroom, secure storage for duty equipment, and a place to decompress after patrols and investigations.

apartment-entry.description: The apartment entrance and short shared hallway, with a lockable front door, mail slot, utility panel, and access toward the building stairwell. Neighbors may be heard nearby, but entry remains private and consent-based.

apartment-interior.description: The main private living space, with a small sofa, work surface, kitchenette, dining counter, ordinary storage, and room for quiet conversations or decompression after a shift.

bathroom.description: A private bathroom with a shower, sink, mirror, and medicine cabinet for ordinary hygiene and recovery routines.

bedroom.description: A private bedroom with a bed, wardrobe, bedside table, and enough quiet for sleep, recovery, and personal routines between police shifts.

building-entry.description: The building's public entrance and mail area, with intercoms, notices, parcel shelves, and a view of the street. A practical starting point for patrols and visitors.

building-stairwell.description: The visible shared stairwell outside Apartment 68, connecting the apartment floor to the building entrance. It supports neighbor encounters, deliveries, and brief conversations.

duty-storage.description: A lockable storage closet for legally issued duty equipment, uniforms, case materials, and secured personal items. It is not a police evidence locker and should not store unauthorized evidence.

kitchenette.description: A compact kitchenette with a refrigerator, microwave, sink, limited counter space, and basic cooking supplies. It supports ordinary meals rather than professional food preparation.

street-side-alley.description: A visible side alley beside the apartment building, lit by security lamps and used by residents, deliveries, and pedestrians. Suitable for discreet but not hidden conversations.

window-seat.description: A narrow window seat overlooking the police district, useful for reviewing notes, decompressing after patrol, watching rain, or having a quiet late-night conversation.

Apartment 68.hiddenInfo: Apartment 68 is close enough to the police district for practical commuting but is not automatically a police safehouse. It is visible and available only within the On the Beat playthrough, not a general-world location for unrelated story starts. The player controls who enters and what personal routines happen here, subject to ordinary law and building rules.

Kurokawa District.name: Kurokawa District
Kurokawa District.basicInfo: A dense backstreet district of aging apartments, shuttered businesses, service alleys, rooftop routes, and overlooked residents. The area is a natural operating ground for vigilantes, gangs, couriers, and anyone trying to stay outside the official spotlight.

apartment-block.description: A worn residential building overlooking the district. Residents share thin walls, unreliable elevators, and a constant awareness of who controls the street below. Fire escapes and maintenance stairs create routes between the street and roof.

backstreet-crossroads.description: A cramped intersection beneath tangled utility lines, lined with convenience stores, worn apartment entrances, and narrow alleys that make surveillance difficult.

gang-hideout.description: An abandoned neighborhood storefront with a reinforced rear room and access to a maintenance roof. Its occupants change, but gang crews use it for meetings, storage, intimidation, and holding people who cannot safely go to the police.

night-bars.description: A row of cramped bars, karaoke rooms, and half-hidden entrances beneath apartment buildings. Information moves quickly here, but so do rumors, debts, and unwanted attention.

ramen-row.description: A short stretch of late-night ramen shops, vending machines, and covered stools. It is one of the few places where residents, couriers, vigilantes, and exhausted workers can share space without asking too many questions.

rooftop-access.description: A fire-escape landing and locked stairwell provide access to connected rooftops. From here, a watcher can observe several blocks without standing in the street.

rooftop-route.description: A broken but traversable chain of rooftops, water tanks, maintenance bridges, and laundry lines. It is useful for couriers and surveillance but dangerous in bad weather or a hurried pursuit.

service-alley.description: A narrow rear lane behind restaurants, workshops, and abandoned units. Deliveries, discarded equipment, gang lookouts, and quiet meetings sometimes pass through here.

Kurokawa District.hiddenInfo: Several buildings have unofficial rooftop access routes known to local couriers and vigilantes. The safest paths depend on weather, lighting, patrols, and which residents are awake.

Central Tokyo.name: Central Tokyo
Central Tokyo.basicInfo: A dense central district of business towers, transit corridors, polished public spaces, nightlife, rooftops, and hidden service routes. Official heroes, media, executives, students, criminals, and ordinary workers overlap here, making it useful for investigations, social scenes, emergencies, and high-visibility missions.

arcade-quarter.description: A lively strip of arcades, karaoke rooms, casual restaurants, and late-night shops beneath the central towers. It is a social hub and a useful place to follow rumors without looking like an investigator.

business-avenue.description: A canyon of office towers, convenience stores, cafés, banks, and corporate entrances. Security cameras and polished sidewalks conceal service doors and private conflicts.

media-plaza.description: A bright public square surrounded by screens, broadcast studios, hero advertising, cafés, and event stages. A small incident here can become citywide news within minutes.

rooftop-gardens.description: Elevated gardens and accessible tower roofs offering views across Central Tokyo. Some are public retreats; others are restricted maintenance spaces used for surveillance or clandestine meetings.

service-level.description: A maze of loading bays, utility corridors, parking access, and staff-only doors beneath the polished central district. It is useful for covert movement but easy to become disoriented in.

station-concourse.description: A crowded transit concourse where commuters, couriers, tourists, and suspicious watchers pass beneath electronic signs and constant announcements.

taxi-stand.description: A busy curbside pickup zone where taxis, rideshares, delivery vehicles, and private cars compete for space. Drivers and dispatchers notice who is moving through the city and when.

Central Tokyo.hiddenInfo: Corporate security, media crews, and official heroes monitor the central district closely. Rooftops and service levels provide alternate routes, but access rules and cameras change frequently.

Old Tokyo.name: Old Tokyo
Old Tokyo.basicInfo: A historic district of shrine roads, lantern streets, traditional shops, theaters, tea houses, aging apartments, and preserved buildings surrounded by modern Tokyo. It is a strong setting for cultural events, secrets, personal histories, quiet investigations, and conflicts hidden behind tradition.

heritage-gardens.description: A preserved garden and museum edge with ponds, footbridges, stone lanterns, and secluded corners. It offers calm routes, ceremonial gatherings, and places where someone can disappear into a crowd.

lantern-quarter.description: A narrow historic street of lanterns, small restaurants, craft shops, and old façades. Crowds gather during festivals, while residents know which doors are welcoming and which are not.

old-apartments.description: Aging residences above workshops and family businesses. Tenants rely on personal trust, informal favors, and neighbors who remember events the official records forgot.

old-station.description: A historic station preserved beside modern transit infrastructure. Its platforms, pedestrian bridges, and storage corridors connect the district to the rest of Tokyo.

shrine-road.description: A winding approach lined with gates, stone walls, small shrines, and quiet side paths. Visitors come for blessings, rumors, memorials, and private conversations away from the main streets.

tea-market.description: A covered market of tea merchants, sweets, antique goods, and family-run stalls. Bargaining, gossip, and long-standing obligations shape who receives help here.

theater-row.description: A cluster of historic theaters, rehearsal halls, dressing rooms, and small performance venues. Public culture and private rivalries share the same narrow corridors.

Old Tokyo.hiddenInfo: Old Tokyo's strongest information network is social memory: shopkeepers, caretakers, performers, and residents notice disruptions long before official systems do.

Tokyo Bay.name: Tokyo Bay
Tokyo Bay.basicInfo: A broad waterfront district of piers, marinas, logistics yards, aquarium attractions, promenades, storm barriers, and industrial back channels. It supports rescue missions, smuggling investigations, faction operations, quiet meetings, and dangerous weather-driven events.

aquarium-front.description: A family-oriented aquarium and attraction district that becomes quieter after closing. Service entrances, staff corridors, and waterfront access create opportunities for rescue or infiltration scenes.

ferry-pier.description: A working passenger pier shared by commuters, tourists, service crews, and small cargo operators. Departures, delays, and tide conditions shape movement through the waterfront.

logistics-yards.description: A maze of containers, cranes, warehouses, loading lanes, and restricted gates. Shipments can be legitimate, stolen, or deliberately misdeclared, and visibility changes with weather and shift changes.

marina.description: A mixed-use marina with private boats, repair slips, floating walkways, and small waterfront restaurants. Boat owners, mechanics, and dock workers form an informal information network.

storm-barrier.description: A long flood-control structure with maintenance stairs and restricted service platforms. It is a dramatic lookout but becomes hazardous during high winds, heavy rain, or emergency closures.

warehouse-row.description: A line of old warehouses and converted storage buildings along the industrial edge. Some are legitimate businesses; others are temporary bases, smuggling points, or places where people are held.

waterfront-promenade.description: A public walkway beside the bay with food stalls, benches, observation points, and sudden views of ships, bridges, and storm fronts.

Tokyo Bay.hiddenInfo: The bay's public spaces and industrial routes operate on different schedules. Weather, tides, port shifts, security closures, and ferry service can change available paths and mission difficulty.

Academy District Hub.name: Academy District Hub
Academy District Hub.basicInfo: A lively student-centered point of interest near the academy district, combining public gathering spaces, transit access, food, study areas, shops, residences, and useful mission routes.
