back-lane.description: A cramped lane behind food stalls and shops with fire escapes, locked doors, recycling cages, and useful sightlines for witnesses, discreet following, or escape. A careful search may reveal a grubby keychain hidden at the base of a recycling cage.

community-clinic.description: A small walk-in clinic for students, workers, and residents. Staff may notice patterns of injuries, exhaustion, or repeated visitors.

district-plaza.description: A broad public plaza with benches, vending machines, event posters, and open space for gatherings, protests, performances, and emergencies.

food-stalls.description: A covered strip of ramen, curry, crepes, and inexpensive meals where students, workers, and residents gather.

service-lane.description: A delivery and maintenance lane behind the public areas, linking loading doors, utilities, and poorly lit shortcuts.

shopping-walk.description: A pedestrian street with bookstores, uniform shops, support-item services, cafés, and practical stores.

station-entrance.description: A busy station entrance used by students, commuters, delivery workers, and visitors throughout the day.

student-café.description: A quiet café and study space for work, conversations, waiting, and shelter during bad weather.

student-quarter.description: Affordable apartments, shared houses, laundromats, and study cafés full of friendships, rumors, homesickness, and private conflicts.

Academy District Hub.hiddenInfo: The public hub's lanes, residences, and clinic create privacy, rescue, investigation, and pursuit opportunities. It remains a shared space, not a faction headquarters.

The Quiet Ledger.name: The Quiet Ledger
The Quiet Ledger.basicInfo: A run-down hotel used as the Backstreet Vigilantes' discreet headquarters. Its boarded windows, unreliable elevators, empty rooms, rooftop access, and half-functioning utilities make it look abandoned enough to avoid casual attention while still providing shelter, planning space, and emergency treatment. The faction's core members live here, each with a private room; member-room-c is reserved as an offered private room for a recruited player.

back-office.description: The hotel's former administration office, now used for communications, records, supply checks, and limited contact with the faction dispatcher. Sensitive information is kept here only when necessary.

clinic-room.description: A stripped-down guest room used for first aid, recovery, and quiet medical assessment. It is not a hospital and cannot replace professional treatment when injuries are serious.

common-room.description: A former guest lounge with mismatched chairs, a battered television, board games, charging cables, and a noticeboard. It is the most likely place to find members between patrols, though nobody is required to socialize.

dispatcher-room.description: A former guest room converted into a communications room for the faction dispatcher. Radios, phones, charging stations, district maps, and message logs are kept here; calls are limited to plausible missions and established contacts.

hotel-lobby.description: A dusty lobby with a dead front desk bell, faded travel posters, and a security camera that works only when someone remembers to repair it. A forgotten key rests in a drawer behind the desk, worn and scratched from years of use. Visitors are screened here before being allowed farther inside.

kitchen.description: A narrow communal kitchen with a repaired refrigerator, cheap cookware, labeled shelves, and food bought by whoever had time to shop. Meals are one of the few reliable chances for the residents to check in with one another.

member-room-a.description: A private room occupied by one of the three current Backstreet Vigilantes. It contains personal gear, clothes, recovery supplies, and reminders of a life that existed before the faction. Entering without permission is a serious breach of trust.

member-room-b.description: A private room occupied by one of the three current Backstreet Vigilantes. Its occupant keeps their own routine, equipment, and boundaries, and may be asleep, away, injured, or unwilling to talk.

member-room-c.description: A private room reserved for a recruited player at the Backstreet Vigilantes' headquarters. It is offered only after the interview and acceptance of the group's secrecy rules; until then, it remains an empty, prepared room rather than an assumed residence.

planning-room.description: A former conference room converted into a planning space with district maps, radios, charging cables, case files, and multiple ways to leave if the building is compromised.

rooftop.description: A cluttered roof with water tanks, broken laundry lines, patched antennas, and a view toward Central Tokyo and Kurokawa. It serves as a lookout, meeting point, and emergency escape route.

room-floor.description: A hallway of abandoned guest rooms, patched doors, mattresses, storage crates, and three occupied member rooms. The residents keep different schedules and boundaries, so a closed door generally means privacy is expected.

service-exit.description: A rear delivery entrance opening onto a narrow service lane. It is the safest route for discreet arrivals, supply movement, and departures when the front entrance is watched.

stairwell.description: A narrow concrete stairwell connecting the lobby, room floors, and roof. The elevator is unreliable, so members use the stairs when they need quiet movement or a fast escape.

The Quiet Ledger.hiddenInfo: The hotel appears vacant because ownership records are tangled and the building's public utilities are inconsistent. Core members use member-room-a, member-room-b, and other private rooms elsewhere in the headquarters; member-room-c is reserved for a recruited player. Schedules, injuries, missions, loneliness, privacy, and personal boundaries determine who is actually present or available. The faction maintains fallback rooms and avoids making the headquarters indispensable to any single member.

The Velvet Lantern.name: The Velvet Lantern
The Velvet Lantern.basicInfo: A stylish casino and nightclub owned by a powerful underworld broker, serving as a glamorous public venue and the Kurokawa underworld's discreet headquarters. Its gaming floors, bars, music, VIP rooms, and private negotiations conceal money laundering, coercive debts, powered enforcers, and restricted routes beneath the nightlife.

backstreet-route.description: A narrow route behind the club connecting delivery bays, fire escapes, and neighboring buildings. It is useful for surveillance, escape, smuggling, or an undercover approach.

bar-lounge.description: A bar and lounge where patrons relax, deals begin casually, and rumors circulate beneath music and conversation.

counting-room.description: A secure financial room where cash, records, ledgers, and laundering arrangements are processed. It is valuable evidence and heavily protected when active.

hidden-exit.description: A concealed escape route through a maintenance passage and disused stairwell. It can bypass the lobby and lead toward rooftops or a secondary street.

main-entrance.description: A polished entrance with a velvet rope, discreet screening, valet access, and staff who remember regular patrons.

main-floor.description: A bright public casino and nightclub floor with music, gaming tables, slot machines, bars, cameras, and staff trained to notice unusual behavior. Ordinary patrons and Syndicate business overlap here.

negotiation-suite.description: A sound-treated private room used for deals, debt settlements, recruitment, threats, and meetings between Syndicate representatives and outside parties.

security-office.description: A monitoring room with camera feeds, access logs, staff communications, and incident records. It can reveal movement, payments, and hidden relationships.

service-entrance.description: A rear loading and staff entrance for deliveries, waste removal, private arrivals, and discreet movement of goods. It opens toward a narrow Kurokawa service route.

staff-corridor.description: A restricted hallway linking service rooms, staff entrances, storage, offices, and private floors. Employees use it constantly, making unauthorized movement risky but possible.

vip-lounge.description: An exclusive lounge for wealthy guests, powerful associates, and private conversations. Access depends on invitation, money, reputation, or a useful secret.

The Velvet Lantern.hiddenInfo: The owner's public ownership and the club's legitimate entertainment operations provide cover for underworld finances and meetings. Its criminal role is known only to insiders, coerced staff, selected regulars, and people who have survived a private deal.

Starbox Coffee.name: Starbox Coffee
Starbox Coffee.basicInfo: Busy student-friendly coffee shop where students work weekend shifts, with polished branding, café seating, takeout traffic, and a small back room for staff breaks and supplies.

cafe-floor.description: Bright café seating, display cases, outlets, and a counter where customers order drinks and pastries.

kitchen.description: Compact preparation kitchen for drinks, syrups, pastries, cleaning supplies, and delivery orders.

service-counter.description: Register, espresso machines, pastry display, and pickup shelf. Staff manage orders here during the morning rush.

staff-room.description: Small employee room with lockers, shift notes, supplies, and a place to take a short break away from customers.

window-seating.description: A popular row of seats overlooking the street, used by students, remote workers, and customers filming short Pulse clips.

Moonbucks Tea.name: Moonbucks Tea
Moonbucks Tea.basicInfo: Low-key tea shop with a quiet back room where students work evening preparation and closing shifts.

back-room.description: Staff preparation, inventory, and closing area. A gold necklace holding a star-speckled crystal rests in a supply box.

tea-floor.description: Calm customer area with tea counters, low lighting, and small tables.

Karaoke Kanari.name: Karaoke Kanari
Karaoke Kanari.basicInfo: Karaoke venue where staff work guest-hosting shifts with clear professional boundaries.

karaoke-hall.description: Private rooms and shared corridors filled with music, requests, and rotating customers. A rediscoverable golden ring engraved with musical notes rests in an unused corner of one private room.

lobby.description: Reception, song-book displays, payment desk, and waiting benches.

staff-room.description: Employee lockers, schedules, and break space.

Uniqloaf Clothing.name: Uniqloaf Clothing
Uniqloaf Clothing.basicInfo: Clothing shop with a fitting floor and alterations counter where students work retail and repair shifts.

alterations-counter.description: Repair and tailoring station where staff work under safety rules.

sales-floor.description: Clothing racks, fitting rooms, displays, and customer service.

stockroom.description: Inventory, employee supplies, and shift storage.

WcDonalds.name: WcDonalds
WcDonalds.basicInfo: Late-opening fast-food restaurant with student-friendly shifts, counter service, a compact kitchen, and a staff area.

dining-floor.description: Counter seating, booths, order screens, and customer tables.

service-counter.description: Ordering and pickup counter with menu boards.

staff-room.description: Small break room and shift board.

Maidreamin Café.name: Maidreamin Café
Maidreamin Café.basicInfo: Themed café with scheduled service shifts, a performance-oriented customer floor, and staff preparation areas.

customer-floor.description: Themed tables, stage corner, and service aisles.

staff-room.description: Lockers, shift notes, and employee break space.

Konbini Castle.name: Konbini Castle
Konbini Castle.basicInfo: Convenience store with rotating student shifts, register service, stocked aisles, and a compact employee area.

register.description: Checkout counters, parcel service, and lottery display.

sales-floor.description: Aisles, refrigerators, hot-food case, and customer checkout traffic.

stockroom.description: Deliveries, inventory shelves, lockers, and staff supplies.

Maison Lumière.name: Maison Lumière
Maison Lumière.basicInfo: Elegant French bistro with candlelit tables, polished service, a curated menu, and a private dining room for formal meals or discreet conversations.

bar.description: Small wine and aperitif bar near the entrance.

dining-room.description: Refined dining room with linen tables, soft lighting, and attentive service.

private-room.description: Quiet reservation-only room for celebrations, negotiations, or confidential dinners.

Vesuvio Rosso.name: Vesuvio Rosso
Vesuvio Rosso.basicInfo: Lively Italian trattoria with family-style tables, red-checkered decor, generous portions, and a kitchen that treats every meal like a community event.

counter.description: Host stand, takeaway counter, and dessert display.

dining-room.description: Warm crowded dining room with shared tables, red-checkered cloths, and energetic conversation.

kitchen.description: Busy open kitchen with ovens, pasta preparation, and staff movement.

Seoul Ember.name: Seoul Ember
Seoul Ember.basicInfo: Korean barbecue restaurant with tabletop grills, private booths, shared side dishes, and smoky late-evening energy.

dining-floor.description: Tabletop grills, shared dishes, energetic groups, and staff who help manage the cooking.

kitchen.description: Prep kitchen and ingredient storage behind the grill service.

private-booths.description: Semi-private grill booths suited to dates, celebrations, tense meetings, and group bonding.

service-counter.description: Reception, reservations, side-dish station, and payment counter.

Kurogane Wagyu.name: Kurogane Wagyu
Kurogane Wagyu.basicInfo: High-end wagyu steakhouse with reservation-only seating, private booths, a visible chef counter, and an atmosphere of quiet expense.

chef-counter.description: Counter seating overlooking the chef's preparation and grill work.

dining-room.description: Elegant low-lit dining room with carefully spaced tables and premium service.

kitchen.description: Specialized grill kitchen, dry-aging storage, and controlled plating area.

private-booths.description: Exclusive booths for business dinners, dates, family expectations, and discreet negotiations.

Skyline Table.name: Skyline Table
Skyline Table.basicInfo: Rooftop restaurant with open-air seating, glass railings, Tokyo views, weather-sensitive service, and a small enclosed dining room.

bar.description: Compact rooftop bar serving nonalcoholic drinks, cocktails, and evening specials.

indoor-dining.description: Glass-walled dining room used during rain, strong wind, or colder evenings.

kitchen.description: Service kitchen connected to the enclosed dining room and rooftop pass.

rooftop-dining.description: Open-air tables overlooking Tokyo, with heaters, umbrellas, and a clear view of the changing skyline.

service-stair.description: Staff and emergency stair access connecting the rooftop restaurant to the building below.

Neon Reel Entertainment Complex.name: Neon Reel Entertainment Complex
Neon Reel Entertainment Complex.basicInfo: Large modern movie theater and arcade complex with multiple screening rooms, a bustling game floor, concessions, private event space, and late-night student traffic.

arcade-floor.description: Bright arcade packed with rhythm games, claw machines, racing cabinets, fighting games, prize counters, and photo booths.

atrium.description: Main entrance atrium with ticket kiosks, posters, escalators, and paths to the theater and arcade wings.

cinema-lobby.description: Theater lobby with ticket counters, showtime boards, queues, and entrances to multiple screening rooms.

concessions.description: Large snack and drink counter serving popcorn, themed treats, and quick meals to cinema guests.

event-lounge.description: Reserved lounge for premieres, student celebrations, Pulse creator events, and private screenings.

prize-counter.description: Redemption counter with plush toys, novelty prizes, and staff storage behind the display wall.

screening-halls.description: Cluster of standard movie theaters ranging from compact rooms to a large premiere auditorium.

service-kitchen.description: Back-of-house preparation area for concessions and event catering.

staff-corridor.description: Restricted employee passage connecting theater operations, arcade supervision, and staff rooms.

staff-room.description: Employee lockers, shift board, break tables, and security monitors.

Harajuku Prism Street.name: Harajuku Prism Street
Harajuku Prism Street.basicInfo: Colorful Harajuku-style fashion street lined with independent boutiques, vintage racks, accessory stalls, custom sneaker shops, beauty counters, quick nail and hair services, and pop-up storefronts.

accessory-alley.description: Small boutiques for jewelry, bags, hair accessories, nail art, and colorful cosmetics.

beauty-counter.description: Compact beauty and styling shop offering makeup, hair accessories, and quick student-friendly services.

pop-up-court.description: Open courtyard for weekend markets, limited drops, local designers, and creator events.

prism-crosswalk.description: Busy pedestrian crossing and street entrance surrounded by colorful signs, youth fashion, and Pulse-ready photo spots.

sneaker-studio.description: Custom sneaker and shoe-painting shop with repair benches and appointment slots.

streetwear-row.description: Independent shops selling oversized silhouettes, graphic-inspired streetwear, layered outfits, and custom sneakers.

vintage-lane.description: Narrow lane of curated vintage clothing, thrift finds, handmade pieces, and rotating resale racks.

Azure Atelier Designer Row.name: Azure Atelier Designer Row
Azure Atelier Designer Row.basicInfo: Exclusive designer shopping street built around Azure Atelier, a luxury water-inspired fashion house whose tailored garments are favored by a certain water hero.

atelier-galleria.description: Elegant pedestrian lane of luxury storefronts, sculptural displays, and discreet security.

azure-atelier.description: Flagship boutique for Azure Atelier's ocean-inspired couture, performance fabrics, formalwear, and custom fittings.

gallery-café.description: Quiet designer café where clients, stylists, and visiting heroes can meet away from the main street.

mariner-tailoring.description: High-end tailoring house for precise suits, coats, formalwear, and discreet alterations.

private-fitting.description: Appointment-only fitting rooms where clients receive confidential measurements, alterations, and custom design consultations.

service-corridor.description: Restricted back passage connecting deliveries, tailoring workrooms, and staff access.

tideglass-jewelry.description: Luxury jewelry boutique specializing in blue glass, pearl, silver, and wave-shaped pieces.

Prism Gate Mall.name: Prism Gate Mall
Prism Gate Mall.basicInfo: Major all-purpose shopping complex connecting fashion, dining, entertainment, electronics, daily necessities, accessories, beauty, salons, hobbies, and a rooftop public space.

beauty-floor.description: Cosmetics, hair salon counters, skincare, nail studios, manicures, and styling appointments.

designer-annex.description: Controlled-access luxury wing leading toward Azure Atelier Designer Row, with premium boutiques, designer accessories, and private appointments.

entertainment-wing.description: Arcade annex, hobby venues, event space, and a connected entrance toward Neon Reel Entertainment Complex.

event-stage.description: Public event area for launches, seasonal festivals, Pulse livestreams, signings, and hero appearances.

fashion-floor.description: Large fashion level with everyday clothing, accessories, jewelry, bags, watches, glasses, youth brands, and a walkway toward Harajuku Prism Street.

food-hall.description: Busy food court and casual dining level with student seating, quick meals, desserts, and pop-up vendors.

lifestyle-floor.description: Electronics, support-tech accessories, home goods, books, hobby shops, and collectibles.

main-atrium.description: Grand central atrium with information desks, seasonal displays, escalators, and direct access to the mall's major wings.

rooftop-deck.description: Open rooftop garden and observation deck overlooking the surrounding shopping district.

underground-concourse.description: Underground passage with station access, convenience services, lockers, and late-hour foot traffic.

Sakura Lane Sharehouse.name: Sakura Lane Sharehouse
Sakura Lane Sharehouse.basicInfo: Furnished sharehouse in the Academy area offering eight individually assigned private bedrooms, shared facilities, and a safe rooftop terrace for residents to relax. It is an inexpensive, social residence for full-time workers, students, and other adult residents. Salina's group-house community can accommodate the incoming Class 6E residents here. It is not the player's Full-Timer home unless the player explicitly chooses or accepts a move there.

building-entrance.description: A welcoming entrance with mailboxes, package lockers, bicycle parking, and a noticeboard for house rules and resident announcements.

courtyard-bedroom.description: A quiet furnished private bedroom near the courtyard side of the house, with a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

garden-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom facing the planted courtyard, with a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

house-courtyard.description: Small outdoor courtyard with benches, bicycles, potted plants, and space for informal conversations.

laundry-room.description: Shared laundry room with coin-operated machines and a folding counter.

lilac-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom with soft colors, a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

loft-bedroom.description: A bright upper-floor private bedroom with a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door, closest to the rooftop access.

maple-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom with warm wood furnishings, a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

resident-hallway.description: Residential hallway leading to eight furnished private bedrooms and shared bathrooms, with stair access toward the rooftop.

river-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom with a distant riverside view, a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

rooftop-chill-deck.description: A safe, ordinary rooftop terrace with permitted access, low railings, weatherproof chairs, potted plants, string lights, and views over Academy streets. Residents come here to cool off, talk, study, watch the evening sky, or have quiet time; it is not a combat arena or restricted hero facility.

shared-bathroom.description: Clean shared bathroom facilities used by residents on the floor.

shared-kitchen.description: Communal kitchen with labeled storage, shared appliances, and enough counter space for casual meals or group cooking.

shared-lounge.description: Common lounge with sofas, dining tables, a television, and an open kitchen where housemates meet after work.

street-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom overlooking Sakura Lane, with a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

sunrise-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom with morning light, a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

Mizuno Heights.name: Mizuno Heights
Mizuno Heights.basicInfo: Older but maintained apartment building with affordable private studios and one-bedroom units. Thin walls and limited space are balanced by convenient access to ordinary neighborhood services.

bicycle-shelter.description: Covered bicycle area beside the entrance, used by residents commuting to nearby shops and transit.

building-entrance.description: Compact entrance with parcel lockers, mailboxes, intercoms, and a small management noticeboard.

residential-hallway.description: Narrow apartment corridor with doors to six private units and a shared utility closet.

rooftop.description: Quiet apartment rooftop with safety railing, utility equipment, water tank, and a view over residential Tokyo at sunset.

shared-laundry.description: Utility room with washing machines, dryers, and a folding surface for residents.

stairwell.description: Narrow enclosed stairwell connecting the apartment floors to the rooftop.

unit-101.description: Private apartment Unit 101, a compact studio with a kitchenette, sleeping area, desk, bathroom, and limited storage.

unit-102.description: Private apartment Unit 102, a compact one-bedroom unit with a small dining table, kitchenette, bathroom, and practical storage.

unit-201.description: Private apartment Unit 201, a compact studio with a desk, books, kitchenette, sleeping area, and bathroom.

unit-202.description: Private apartment Unit 202, a compact one-bedroom home with a low sofa, kitchenette, sleeping area, bathroom, and practical storage.

unit-301.description: Private apartment Unit 301, a compact studio with plants, kitchenette, sleeping area, reading chair, bathroom, and limited storage.

unit-302.description: Private apartment Unit 302, a compact studio with a simple bed, work desk, kitchenette, bathroom, and organized storage.

Lantern House Apartments.name: Lantern House Apartments
Lantern House Apartments.basicInfo: Renovated older apartment building in the Old Tokyo residential quarter, above workshops and small family businesses. Residents value courtesy, privacy, and neighborhood memory.

private-apartment.description: Older renovated apartment with a compact kitchen, bathroom, living space, sleeping area, and views toward the surrounding historic streets.

residential-hallway.description: Renovated hallway combining modern fixtures with preserved wood details and quiet apartment doors.

service-alley.description: Narrow maintained alley behind the building, used for deliveries, bins, and quiet access between neighboring properties.

shared-laundry.description: Small resident laundry room with practical machines and a window onto the service lane.

street-entrance.description: Lantern-lit entrance opening onto a narrow residential lane beside workshops and small shops.

workshop-front.description: Public-facing row of ground-floor workshop doors and small business entrances where residents exchange greetings with local proprietors.

Neon Gate Residences.name: Neon Gate Residences
Neon Gate Residences.basicInfo: Compact apartment building above a busy commercial strip of restaurants, karaoke, retail, and late-night businesses. It suits workers whose schedules run late.

commercial-lobby.description: Secure lobby with parcel lockers, mailboxes, elevator access, and the sounds of the businesses below.

laundry-room.description: Shared laundry room used by residents working irregular or late shifts.

private-studio.description: Small studio apartment with kitchenette, bathroom, sleeping area, and sound-insulated windows facing the commercial street.

residential-hallway.description: Compact upper-floor hallway leading to studio apartments and a shared utility area.

street-front.description: Busy covered sidewalk outside the building, with restaurants, karaoke entrances, retail shutters, taxis, and evening foot traffic.

Harborview Terrace.name: Harborview Terrace
Harborview Terrace.basicInfo: Comfortable mid-range apartment complex with balconies, shared facilities, and a longer commute to central jobs. Its residents enjoy calm waterfront surroundings and practical community amenities.

apartment-hallway.description: Clean residential hallway leading to private units and shared building facilities.

bike-storage.description: Secure bicycle storage beside the entrance for residents commuting through the waterfront district.

complex-entrance.description: Landscaped entrance with security access, mailboxes, parcel lockers, and a small management office.

private-apartment.description: Comfortable studio or one-bedroom apartment with a balcony, kitchen, bathroom, living space, and more storage than the cheaper options.

private-balcony.description: Private balcony overlooking the neighborhood, useful for fresh air, quiet conversations, and watching evening lights.

residential-courtyard.description: Shared courtyard with benches, planted paths, and a clear view toward the waterfront district.

shared-laundry.description: Resident laundry room with several machines and a folding counter.

waterfront-walk.description: Public walking path beside the residential complex, with benches and a route toward nearby shops and transit.

Harborlight Ferris Pier.name: Harborlight Ferris Pier
Harborlight Ferris Pier.basicInfo: A lively waterfront amusement pier with a large Ferris wheel, harbor views, ticket booths, casual food stalls, dessert counters, benches, and evening lights. It is a public leisure destination for dates, families, friends, tourists, and ordinary weekend outings.

arcade-corner.description: Compact pier arcade with ordinary claw machines, rhythm games, photo booths, and a change counter.

ferris-wheel-plaza.description: Open plaza beneath the Ferris wheel with queue rails, benches, souvenir kiosks, and safe harbor views.

food-stall-row.description: A row of casual waterfront food stalls selling takoyaki, grilled seafood, fries, crepes, soft-serve, drinks, and other affordable pier food.

harbor-dining-deck.description: Outdoor dining deck with ordinary tables, umbrellas, railings, harbor air, and places to eat food bought from the pier stalls.

pier-entrance.description: Waterfront entrance with ticket booths, maps, railings, public notices, and views toward the Ferris wheel.

waterfront-cafe.description: Small modern café serving coffee, tea, sandwiches, pastries, and seasonal harbor-themed desserts.

wheel-queue.description: Ordinary Ferris wheel boarding queue with shade structures, safety notices, staff gates, and numbered cabins beyond the loading platform.

Moonlit Scoops.name: Moonlit Scoops
Moonlit Scoops.basicInfo: A cheerful neighborhood ice cream shop with rotating seasonal flavors, soft-serve, sundaes, cones, cups, and a few sidewalk seats. It is a casual stop for friends, families, dates, and solo dessert runs.

shop-counter.description: Bright counter with flavor boards, free tasting spoons, toppings, cones, cups, and a small refrigerated display.

sidewalk-seating.description: A few ordinary outdoor tables and chairs where customers can eat ice cream and watch the street.

Crumb and Cloud.name: Crumb and Cloud
Crumb and Cloud.basicInfo: A cookie shop inspired by modern oversized-cookie bakeries, selling warm cookies, chilled milk, coffee, gift boxes, and rotating weekly flavors. The shop is popular for takeout, small celebrations, study breaks, and social-media photos.

order-counter.description: A compact counter displaying oversized cookies, flavor cards, milk, coffee, and boxed assortments.

window-bar.description: A narrow indoor window bar with stools for customers eating warm cookies and drinks.

Ringlet Donuts.name: Ringlet Donuts
Ringlet Donuts.basicInfo: A casual donut shop with glazed, filled, cake, and seasonal donuts, plus coffee and tea. It opens early for commuters and remains a friendly stop for students, workers, and late-afternoon snack runs.

display-counter.description: Front counter with trays of donuts, refrigerated drinks, coffee service, and a small menu board.

window-seating.description: Simple seating by the front windows for quick breakfasts, study breaks, and casual conversations.

Lantern Bowl Ramen.name: Lantern Bowl Ramen
Lantern Bowl Ramen.basicInfo: A grounded neighborhood ramen shop with counter seating, a few small tables, takeout service, and practical late-evening hours. It serves ramen, gyoza, rice bowls, water, tea, and rotating broth specials.

front-counter.description: Compact entrance and ordering area with a menu board, ticket machine, and visible counter seats.

ramen-counter.description: Open kitchen counter where staff prepare ramen, gyoza, and rice bowls in full view of customers.

small-tables.description: A few ordinary tables for small groups, quick meals, and quiet conversations.

Kurokawa Fresh Market.name: Kurokawa Fresh Market
Kurokawa Fresh Market.basicInfo: A compact neighborhood grocery store serving Kurokawa residents, apartment tenants, night workers, and small restaurants. It carries produce, packaged food, drinks, toiletries, household basics, and ready-to-eat meals.

entrance-checkouts.description: Automatic doors, baskets, checkout lanes, a small service desk, and shelves of discounted ready-to-eat meals near closing time.

grocery-aisles.description: Narrow aisles stocked with produce, packaged staples, snacks, drinks, toiletries, and practical household supplies.

冷蔵-section.description: Refrigerated cases with milk, bottled drinks, prepared meals, chilled noodles, desserts, and fresh ingredients.

Kurokawa Lantern Mart.name: Kurokawa Lantern Mart
Kurokawa Lantern Mart.basicInfo: A bright 24-hour convenience store on a busy Kurokawa nightlife street, selling snacks, drinks, hot counter food, toiletries, phone chargers, cigarettes, magazines, and basic daily necessities.

aisles.description: Compact aisles of drinks, snacks, instant meals, toiletries, batteries, chargers, magazines, and umbrellas.

back-seating.description: A small indoor eating area with simple counter seats, a microwave, and a hot-water station.

front-counter.description: Checkout counter with hot snacks, coffee machine, lottery terminal, tobacco cabinet, and parcel service desk.

Kurokawa Night Owl Konbini.name: Kurokawa Night Owl Konbini
Kurokawa Night Owl Konbini.basicInfo: A late-night convenience store near Kurokawa residences and side streets, used by shift workers, residents, performers, and people coming home after the nightlife district closes.

checkout.description: Small checkout area with a coffee machine, microwave, parcel pickup shelf, and a window toward the street.

shop-floor.description: Ordinary convenience-store aisles with bottled drinks, snacks, instant noodles, toiletries, medicine cabinet items, and discounted bentos.

Kurokawa Seven Corner.name: Kurokawa Seven Corner
Kurokawa Seven Corner.basicInfo: A 24-hour convenience store near the station approach, providing ordinary food, drinks, ATM access, parcel services, chargers, umbrellas, and quick meals for commuters and nightlife workers.

eat-in-nook.description: Small counter seating by the window for quick meals and people-watching.

registers.description: Checkout lanes with ATM, parcel counter, hot food case, and staff station.

sales-floor.description: Bright aisles of packaged food, drinks, coffee, toiletries, stationery, batteries, and travel necessities.

Kurokawa Ramen House.name: Kurokawa Ramen House
Kurokawa Ramen House.basicInfo: A modest late-night ramen shop serving noodles, gyoza, rice bowls, and simple drinks to residents, workers, and people leaving the Kurokawa entertainment district.

counter-seats.description: Open kitchen counter with steaming ramen bowls, gyoza plates, and direct views of the cooks.

small-tables.description: A few compact tables for pairs and small groups seeking a quick late-night meal.

ticket-machine.description: Entrance with a ticket vending machine, menu photographs, condiment shelf, and a short waiting line.

Kurokawa All-Night Diner.name: Kurokawa All-Night Diner
Kurokawa All-Night Diner.basicInfo: A 24-hour American-style diner on a Kurokawa side street, serving burgers, fries, pancakes, eggs, sandwiches, milkshakes, coffee, pie, and inexpensive comfort food for nightlife workers, residents, and people waiting out the night.

booths.description: Private booths for late-night meals, casual conversations, dates, studying, and tired workers.

counter.description: Long counter with swivel stools, coffee refills, condiment caddies, and a view of the open kitchen.

dining-room.description: Red-vinyl booths, chrome-edged tables, laminated menus, large street-facing windows, and a pie display under warm fluorescent lights.

kitchen.description: Open kitchen preparing burgers, fries, pancakes, waffles, eggs, bacon, grilled cheese, chicken sandwiches, milkshakes, coffee, pie, and rotating specials.

Kurokawa All-Night Donuts.name: Kurokawa All-Night Donuts
Kurokawa All-Night Donuts.basicInfo: A 24-hour donut shop near the nightlife district, serving fresh glazed, filled, cake, and seasonal donuts with coffee, tea, and simple takeout boxes for commuters, performers, and night-shift workers.

coffee-bar.description: Coffee and tea service with cream, sugar, microwaves, and a small prep counter for overnight staff.

display-counter.description: Glass display filled with donuts, filled pastries, seasonal specials, and takeout boxes beside the register.

window-seating.description: Simple window stools and narrow tables overlooking the neon street, useful for quick breakfasts and quiet late-night conversations.

Apartment 801.name: Apartment 801
Apartment 801.basicInfo: An empty Kurokawa apartment above a quiet side street, offering a private base for someone living outside respectable society. Floor-to-ceiling windows expose distant city lights and rain, while bare rooms contain almost nothing: a thin mattress, a small kitchenette, and an aching sense of isolation.

apartment-interior.description: A vast, nearly empty apartment interior with floor-to-ceiling windows, bare concrete, worn flooring, a thin mattress, and an unused kitchenette. Suitable for isolation, recovery, difficult conversations, meetings, and long-term schemes.

balcony.description: A narrow private balcony outside the apartment, overlooking Kurokawa's lights and rain. It is suited to quiet conversations, surveillance, smoking, cooling off, or watching the street below.

building-entry.description: The building's publicly visible entrance, with a buzzer panel, mailboxes, cracked tile, and a clear view toward the Kurokawa street. Visitors can wait here before access is granted or refused.

entry-stairwell.description: A narrow stairwell and apartment entrance opening onto a discreet Kurokawa side street. The building entry is visible, though access may be controlled by whoever currently occupies the apartment.

fire-escape.description: A visible fire escape outside the apartment windows, overlooking the side street and neighboring rooftops. It is not hidden, though access depends on safety and permission.

kitchenette.description: A nearly unused kitchenette with a sink, compact refrigerator, and limited counter space. It can support simple meals, evidence review, or tense conversations.

rooftop.description: A shared rooftop with water tanks, safety rails, utility structures, and a broad view of Kurokawa. Ideal for late-night conversations, faction meetings, surveillance, and quiet decisions, subject to access and weather.

service-alley.description: A publicly visible service alley behind the building, used by deliveries, maintenance, and occasional neighborhood traffic. Atmospheric without being a secret location.

side-street.description: A visible Kurokawa side street beside the apartment building, with rain-slick pavement, shuttered storefronts, and passing pedestrians. Useful for meetings, deliveries, surveillance, and departures.

window-wall.description: Floor-to-ceiling windows and a low sill overlooking Kurokawa's lights and rain. A quiet place for late-night conversations, surveillance, reflection, and watching the neighborhood.

Apartment 801.hiddenInfo: The apartment's criminal associations, occupants, contacts, and stored information may be concealed, but the building and its areas are globally visible. Access can be restricted by keys, permission, reputation, or timing; never treat the location itself as hidden.

Midnight Shrine.name: Midnight Shrine
Midnight Shrine.basicInfo: A small, secluded shrine in Old Tokyo where late-night visitors come for quiet prayers and a moment away from the city.

lantern-approach.description: A narrow approach from the Old Tokyo street, marked by weathered lanterns and a torii gate. It offers a clear route away from the shrine during a dangerous encounter.

shrine-grounds.description: Stone steps, a modest offering box, and old lanterns beneath trees. The grounds are calm at first, but the surrounding darkness provides places for something supernatural to approach unseen.

Midnight Shrine.hiddenInfo: The shrine's boundary markers are stronger than they appear, but they are not an automatic defense against a yokai.

The Lair.name: The Lair
The Lair.basicInfo: An abandoned multi-room building informally nicknamed The Lair. Its eight unassigned bedrooms, kitchen, common room, meeting room, and rooftop make it a practical multiplayer headquarters that players can reclaim and shape.

bedroom-1.description: A small dusty bedroom with enough space for one player to establish a personal base. It remains unassigned until claimed in play.

bedroom-2.description: A small unassigned bedroom with a damaged wardrobe and a view of neighboring rooftops.

bedroom-3.description: A narrow unassigned bedroom with old shelves and a door that still locks.

bedroom-4.description: An unassigned bedroom with peeling paint, a ceiling light, and room for personal storage.

bedroom-5.description: A quiet unassigned bedroom at the end of the hall, with a cracked mirror and boarded window.

bedroom-6.description: An unassigned bedroom with a sturdy floor and a corner for equipment or work supplies.

bedroom-7.description: An unassigned bedroom with faded wallpaper and a view toward the street.

bedroom-8.description: The largest unassigned bedroom, suitable for a player who wants extra workspace.

common-room.description: A broad room with mismatched chairs, worn couches, and open floor for planning or storage.

hallway.description: The central corridor connecting the bedrooms and shared rooms. It smells of dust, paint, and old rainwater.

kitchen.description: A neglected kitchen with a working sink, old counters, and limited appliances.

meeting-room.description: A former office with a long table, scarred chairs, dead wall screens, and privacy for organization meetings and speakerphone calls.

rooftop.description: A rough rooftop with patched concrete, rusted railings, city views, and room for lookouts or future improvements.

The Lair.hiddenInfo: The Lair is stable enough to reclaim, but its utilities, security, and ownership history can become future organization story hooks.

Silver Screen Garden.name: Silver Screen Garden
Silver Screen Garden.basicInfo: Independent neighborhood cinema with art-house films, midnight screenings, small director talks, and a quiet rooftop garden for guests.

concessions.description: A modest counter serving popcorn, drinks, pastries, and specialty seasonal snacks.

lobby.description: A compact cinema lobby with ticket windows, film posters, a small box office, and comfortable waiting benches.

rooftop-garden.description: A quiet rooftop seating area with planters and city views, open between screenings when weather permits.

screening-halls.description: Three intimate screening rooms for new releases, classic films, documentaries, and late-night features.

Moonlight Multiplex.name: Moonlight Multiplex
Moonlight Multiplex.basicInfo: A large contemporary cinema with premium screens, immersive sound, family programming, fan events, and a busy late-evening crowd.

arcade-corner.description: Small entertainment area with claw machines, rhythm games, and photo booths near the theater exits.

atrium.description: Bright entrance atrium with ticket kiosks, digital showtime boards, escalators, and a broad public meeting space.

cinema-lobby.description: Main theater lobby with ticket counters, queues, promotional displays, and entrances to the screening halls.

concessions.description: Large snack counter serving popcorn, drinks, candy, hot food, and themed release promotions.

event-stage.description: Flexible area for premieres, fan gatherings, school events, and cast or creator appearances.

screening-halls.description: Multiple standard and premium auditoriums showing current releases, special events, and animated films.

Red Oven Pizza House.name: Red Oven Pizza House
Red Oven Pizza House.basicInfo: A casual neighborhood pizzeria known for blistered wood-fired pies, counter service, family tables, and generous takeout boxes.

counter.description: Order counter with menu boards, pickup shelves, drinks, and takeaway boxes.

dining-room.description: Warm dining room with family tables, red tile, open shelving, and a view toward the oven.

kitchen.description: Open kitchen centered on a wood-fired oven, dough preparation, toppings, and staff movement.

Night Slice Tokyo.name: Night Slice Tokyo
Night Slice Tokyo.basicInfo: A late-night pizza counter serving oversized slices, spicy toppings, garlic knots, and quick meals to students, workers, and nightlife crowds.

counter.description: Bright late-night counter with warming trays, slice displays, condiment bottles, and a few standing tables.

kitchen.description: Busy prep kitchen handling dough, ovens, toppings, delivery orders, and late-night rushes.

seating-area.description: Compact seating area with high stools, small tables, and a window overlooking the night street.

Amore al Forno.name: Amore al Forno
Amore al Forno.basicInfo: A romantic Italian pizzeria with handmade dough, seasonal toppings, candlelit tables, and a calm atmosphere suited to dates and celebrations.

dining-room.description: Softly lit dining room with intimate tables, ceramic plates, plants, and an open view of the baking ovens.

host-stand.description: Entrance and reservation desk with menus, waiting stools, and takeaway ordering.

oven-room.description: Visible preparation area with handmade dough, ingredient shelves, and stone ovens.

Champion's Pie Garage.name: Champion's Pie Garage
Champion's Pie Garage.basicInfo: A casual sports-themed pizza restaurant near the pier, with large pies, screens for live matches, communal tables, and a loud friendly atmosphere.

dining-room.description: Open dining room with communal tables, sports screens, booths, team colors, and a busy family-friendly crowd.

game-corner.description: Small area with tabletop sports games and prize machines for waiting customers.

kitchen.description: Commercial kitchen with deck ovens, prep counters, refrigeration, and stacked pizza boxes.

order-counter.description: Counter for whole pies, slices, drinks, and takeaway orders beside the open kitchen.

Redline Arms and Armor.name: Redline Arms and Armor
Redline Arms and Armor.basicInfo: A licensed firearms and protective-equipment retailer serving authorized civilians, security contractors, licensed heroes, and vetted professionals. Sales, storage, transfers, repairs, and training follow Japanese law and venue-specific access rules.

fitting-room.description: Private fitting space for checking body armor, protective jackets, helmets, carriers, and mobility before purchase or authorized rental.

range-office.description: Instructor and records office handling scheduling, licensing checks, safety documentation, and training plans.

secured-storage.description: Locked storage for regulated firearms, ammunition, armor orders, repairs, and items awaiting authorized transfer.

service-counter.description: Staffed counter for identification checks, permits, paperwork, secure storage, transfers, repairs, and restricted-order questions.

showroom.description: Supervised showroom displaying legally approved firearms, training equipment, protective clothing, helmets, body armor, and secure cases. No unsupervised handling.

training-range.description: Restricted indoor range for approved customers and supervised instruction, with safety briefings, protective equipment, and controlled ammunition use.

Redline Arms and Armor.hiddenInfo: The store does not sell weapons or ammunition casually. Access depends on identity, licensing, lawful purpose, age requirements, permits, training, inventory, and current legal restrictions. Students, vigilantes, criminals, and villains may be refused, reported, or offered only lawful protective or training alternatives. Never bypass legal safeguards or provide illegal acquisition routes. Armor may be available more broadly than firearms but remains subject to cost, fit, supply, and venue rules.

Bizarre Alley.name: Bizarre Alley
Bizarre Alley.basicInfo: A narrow service alley tucked behind older storefronts, lit by humming signs, vending-machine glow, and a single flickering security lamp. It is an ordinary public passage that becomes an absurd stage when local rivals turn a grudge into a challenge.

alley-mouth.description: The brighter entrance beside a convenience store and side street, with pedestrian traffic and a clear route out.

back-lot.description: A dead-end loading space behind shuttered businesses, cluttered with bins, crates, and a locked utility gate.

service-run.description: The central stretch of the alley, wide enough for a tense standoff or short fight but cramped enough to create hazards.

Harborlight Beach.name: Harborlight Beach
Harborlight Beach.basicInfo: A public Tokyo Bay beach with broad sand, marked swimming areas, lifeguard stations, changing facilities, food kiosks, and a busy seasonal promenade. It supports ordinary recreation, beach sports, photography, casual work, and supervised water activities.

beach-entrance.description: Public entrance with signs, lockers, changing rooms, showers, rental counters, and access to the promenade.

food-kiosk-row.description: Seasonal kiosks selling drinks, shaved ice, grilled snacks, sunscreen, towels, and inexpensive beach supplies.

lifeguard-station.description: Staffed elevated lifeguard post overlooking the marked swimming area, with rescue equipment and safety notices.

main-sand.description: Broad maintained beach with marked swimming zones, umbrellas, volleyball space, towels, and open room for sunbathing or games.

promenade.description: Paved waterfront walk with benches, rental bikes, public art, and clear views toward nearby harbor attractions.

volleyball-court.description: Marked beach-sport area used for casual games, school outings, training, and public events.

waterline.description: Supervised shoreline where visitors wade, swim in designated zones, look for shells, and watch the bay.

Odaiba Shoreline.name: Odaiba Shoreline
Odaiba Shoreline.basicInfo: An urban waterfront beach and promenade beside Tokyo Bay, combining sand, seawalls, skyline views, public art, event space, and popular photo locations. It is a natural setting for dates, filming, modeling, social-media work, and public gatherings.

event-lawn.description: Flexible public lawn for pop-up markets, seasonal festivals, fitness sessions, and small sponsored events.

photo-platform.description: Raised public viewing platform with a clear background for portraits, fashion shoots, livestreams, and sunset photography.

shoreline-plaza.description: Open waterfront plaza with event notices, public art, benches, and access to the sandy shoreline.

skyline-promenade.description: Wide paved promenade used by walkers, cyclists, performers, photographers, and social-media creators.

urban-beach.description: Maintained urban sand and shallow-water recreation zone with signs describing swimming and water-access rules.

waterfront-edge.description: Seawall and designated viewing edge overlooking the bay, with railings, lights, and strong skyline views.

Saltglass Kitchen.name: Saltglass Kitchen
Saltglass Kitchen.basicInfo: A bright seaside restaurant on Harborlight Beach serving grilled fish, noodles, rice bowls, and seasonal dishes with bay views.

beach-patio.description: Outdoor patio with umbrellas, windbreaks, and views over the sand and water.

dining-room.description: Open dining room with broad windows, beach-facing tables, a counter, and ordinary restaurant seating.

Undertow Bar.name: Undertow Bar
Undertow Bar.basicInfo: A relaxed waterfront bar beside Harborlight Beach with mocktails, cocktails, live music, and sunset seating. Evening access follows venue rules.

bar-room.description: Casual bar interior with a service counter, small tables, music equipment, and windows toward the bay.

sunset-deck.description: Outdoor deck with railings, low tables, and direct views of the shoreline at dusk.

Sea-Salt Soft Serve.basicInfo: A small beach ice cream shop specializing in sea-salt soft serve, chilled desserts, fruit toppings, and takeout cones.

beach-window.description: Takeout window opening toward the promenade, with standing tables and views of the beach.

service-counter.description: Bright counter with soft-serve machines, menu boards, toppings, and a short queue area.

Salt Sprinkle Bar.name: Salt Sprinkle Bar
Salt Sprinkle Bar.basicInfo: A dedicated sea-salt ice cream bar offering experimental flavors, tasting flights, and a counter facing Harborlight Beach.

flavor-lab.description: Small preparation space where staff develop seasonal combinations and limited-edition desserts.

tasting-counter.description: Long tasting counter with rotating sea-salt flavors, sample spoons, and a view toward the water.

Tide-Table Dining.name: Tide-Table Dining
Tide-Table Dining.basicInfo: A casual beach restaurant with picnic-style tables, seafood sandwiches, vegetarian plates, and family-friendly daytime service.

main-dining.description: Casual dining room with durable tables, open windows, and quick daytime service.

picnic-terrace.description: Outdoor terrace with shared tables, shade umbrellas, and a clear view of the sand.

Moonpool Lounge.name: Moonpool Lounge
Moonpool Lounge.basicInfo: A quieter night-oriented lounge near Harborlight Beach offering drinks, small plates, and sheltered seating away from the busiest sand.

covered-deck.description: Sheltered deck with curtains, heaters, and a quieter view toward the water.

lounge-floor.description: Low-lit lounge with comfortable seating, a small service bar, and muted coastal decor.

Boardwalk Bites.name: Boardwalk Bites
Boardwalk Bites.basicInfo: A compact counter-service beach eatery selling fried seafood, shaved ice, quick meals, and snacks for visitors on the move.

service-counter.description: Fast counter-service window with menu boards, pickup shelves, and beach-facing standing tables.

dockhead.description: Main dock platform with benches, railings, safety equipment, and views across the bay.

launch-gate.description: Controlled shore-side access point for supervised small-boat launches and dock events.

Dock Two.basicInfo: A second waterfront dock near Harborlight Beach used for evening views, supervised launches, event access, and harbor photography.

access-ramp.description: Accessible ramp connecting the dock to the public waterfront walk.

viewing-dock.description: Long waterfront platform with lights, benches, railings, and space for harbor photography.

The Alcove.name: The Alcove
The Alcove.basicInfo: A secluded venue beneath a concrete bridge, set apart from Harborlight Beach and reached by a side route from the waterfront. It has sheltered tables, muted lights, and an intimate atmosphere.

side-approach.description: A narrow but public approach from the waterfront, separated from the main beach by the bridge structure and service fencing.

under-bridge-seating.description: Sheltered seating beneath the bridge with concrete pillars, muted lights, weather protection, and a distant view of the beach.

Private Hero Yacht.name: Private Hero Yacht
Private Hero Yacht.basicInfo: A sleek private yacht used by a successful pro hero for travel, charity appearances, hero networking, private recovery, and carefully controlled media events. It is anchored off the Chikara waterfront and is not automatically open to the public.

boarding-dock.description: A secured boarding point with access checks, mooring lines, life jackets, and a clear view of the beach and city skyline.

hero-briefing-room.description: Compact meeting room with navigation displays, emergency plans, communications equipment, and space for professional hero discussions.

main-deck.description: Polished open deck with seating, shaded tables, rescue equipment, and room for supervised gatherings or formal receptions.

salon.description: Comfortable interior salon used for meetings, meals, interviews, and private conversations away from the open water.

upper-observation-deck.description: Raised observation deck with uninterrupted views of the bay and city, used for quiet reflection, photography, and private conversations.

Primes Headquarters.name: Primes Headquarters
Primes Headquarters.basicInfo: A secure residential hero headquarters where all five Primes members live, train, coordinate deployments, receive visitors, and recover between missions. The building combines a public-facing operations center with private residential floors, medical support, tactical rooms, communications infrastructure, and shared spaces designed to make the team function as a household as well as an emergency-response unit.

bedroom-aoi.description: A team member's functional bedroom with rescue boots by the door, medical textbooks, laundry waiting to be folded, emergency bags, practical furniture, and a chair that is frequently used for exhausted naps.

bedroom-emi.description: A team member's practical bedroom with combat gear, recovery supplies, discarded sponsor packages, athletic clothing, and a television usually playing something louder than necessary.

bedroom-haruto.description: A team member's refined bedroom with quiet luxury furnishings, carefully arranged books, a private wardrobe, family gifts not yet discarded, and a view chosen for privacy rather than prestige.

bedroom-mika.description: A team member's colorful bedroom and content-planning space with clothing racks, product samples, ring lights, charging stations, campaign boards, and several phones within reach.

bedroom-ryota.description: A team member's orderly private bedroom: understated furniture, training equipment, mission files, a few personal keepsakes, and blackout curtains for the rare nights of real sleep.

bedroom-six.description: A flexible private bedroom reserved for the player, a guest, or a future Primes-affiliated resident. It contains a bed, desk, wardrobe, secure storage, and a blank wall awaiting personalization.

communications-suite.description: The team's communications hub, filled with monitored screens, dispatch equipment, signal shielding, drone cradles, and emergency coordination systems.

front-lobby.description: A polished public lobby with a Primes emblem, reception desk, security screening, visitor seating, display cases, and carefully controlled sightlines for media appearances.

interview-room.description: A controlled broadcast studio inside Primes Headquarters with two interview chairs, a small production desk, microphones, softbox lights, cameras, acoustic panels, monitors, and discreet Primes branding. The room is designed for polished introductions, sponsored interviews, and carefully managed public statements.

medical-wing.description: A compact professional treatment area with examination rooms, recovery beds, trauma supplies, and equipment for post-mission monitoring. Team members frequently argue with staff here about discharge times.

operations-floor.description: The team's command level, containing briefing rooms, mission planning tables, secure communications stations, sponsor liaison offices, and the team leader's workspace.

rec-room.description: A dedicated recreation room where the Primes can decompress away from cameras and mission schedules. It has a home theater, sectional seating, full-size pool table, board-game shelves, snack and drink bar, arcade cabinet, and warm lounge lighting. The room is one of the few spaces designed for them to be ordinary young adults rather than public heroes.

residential-floor.description: A secure private floor containing six bedrooms, bathrooms, laundry facilities, a quiet study, and a residential corridor. Five rooms belong to the Primes members; the sixth is reserved for a player, guest, or future team member.

shared-kitchen.description: The shared kitchen used by all five Primes members: a large island, refrigerator covered with schedules and sponsor magnets, mismatched mugs, pantry shelves, a commercial range, and a dining table where arguments, late meals, and rare honest conversations happen away from cameras.

shared-lounge.description: The residential common room with couches, entertainment systems, a balcony, and enough visible evidence of five very different people living together. The connected shared kitchen is the practical center of daily life.

training-floor.description: A modular combat and rescue training space with reinforced surfaces, collapsible obstacles, medical observation equipment, and adjustable environmental hazards.

Primes Headquarters.hiddenInfo: The building's public floors are carefully managed for branding, while the residential floor has informal rules and private tensions that management does not fully understand. A sealed service route connects the medical wing to an emergency evacuation point. Different team members know different secrets: the surveillance blind spots, which emergency supplies are missing, which construction decisions were expensive, and which doors teammates avoid.

Kurokawa Legal Office.name: Kurokawa Legal Office
Kurokawa Legal Office.basicInfo: A respected independent law office in a mixed-use Kurokawa building, with a reception desk, two consultation rooms, a compact records room, and a private office for the lead attorney. It is known for careful, unusually capable representation in cases involving powered incidents, superhero crimes, superhuman legal disputes, collateral damage, unlawful use of abilities, and vigilante cases, while still serving ordinary clients who need practical representation.
Kurokawa Legal Office.hiddenInfo: The office's reputation has grown through difficult cases where ordinary legal assumptions fail: proving responsibility after powered collateral damage, challenging excessive force, protecting civilians caught between heroes and villains, negotiating restitution, defending vigilantes whose actions require careful factual scrutiny, and separating public panic from admissible evidence. The office does not excuse violence or guarantee acquittals. It insists on lawful process, informed consent, confidentiality, evidence preservation, and client-specific strategy. Superpowered clients may seek help here, but representation is never automatic and conflicts of interest must be addressed before a case begins.

consultation-room.description: Private client room with a table, chairs, accessible layout, and secure space for confidential conversations.

hallway.description: Short interior hallway connecting reception, consultation rooms, records, and the attorney's office.

ken-office.description: The lead attorney's private office with a desk, legal texts, accessible organization tools, a cane stand, and a window overlooking Kurokawa's streets.

reception.description: Small public reception area with a waiting bench, intake desk, legal notices, and a printer.

records-room.description: Locked records room with filing cabinets, case folders, and controlled document storage.

design-studio.description: Private tables for custom art and premium appointments.

Velvet Strand Hair Salon.name: Velvet Strand Hair Salon
Velvet Strand Hair Salon.basicInfo: Contemporary hair salon offering cuts, blowouts, styling, coloring, gloss, and luxury appointments.

front-desk.description: Reception, scheduling, product displays, and waiting area.

styling-floor.description: Mirrors, chairs, wash stations, cuts, and blowouts.

color-bar.description: Color consultations, gloss, highlights, and product work.

private-room.description: Quiet room for luxury styling and detailed transformations.

Harborlight Resort Spa.name: Harborlight Resort Spa
Harborlight Resort Spa.basicInfo: A luxury spa beside Harborlight Beach offering facials, massages, body treatments, beauty packages, and quiet recovery services.

reception.description: Reservation desk, product displays, robes, and package consultations.

treatment-hall.description: Professional rooms for facials, massages, skincare, and body treatments.

hydrotherapy-room.description: Quiet recovery room with warm pools, steam, and non-medical relaxation treatments.

private-suite.description: Reservation-only suite for premium packages and private appointments.

Inked Desires.name: Inked Desires
Inked Desires.basicInfo: A bright, professional tattoo and piercing studio in Harajuku's fashion district, known for collaborative custom designs, careful consultations, sterile technique, and respectful aftercare.

front-studio.description: Reception, artist portfolios, jewelry displays, appointment booking, and consent-focused consultations.

tattoo-floor.description: Private tattoo stations for player-defined designs, placement, scale, color, and visibility.

piercing-room.description: Clean professional piercing room with placement consultation, jewelry selection, and safety procedures.

aftercare-counter.description: Written aftercare guidance, healing supplies, jewelry care, and follow-up scheduling.

Vermine Cell Workshop.name: Vermine Cell Workshop
Vermine Cell Workshop.basicInfo: A hidden Turned workshop beneath an abandoned service structure where Vermine cells repair equipment, process biological material, and debate whether survival justifies terror.

concealed-entrance.description: A disguised access point watched by nervous lookouts and escape routes.

processing-room.description: Improvised benches and sealed containers for sorting Stable Flesh, Predatory Tissue, and Manifestation Cores.

upgrade-bay.description: Illicit worktables for risky gear modifications using unstable Turned material.

meeting-room.description: A divided planning room where mutual-aid organizers and violent strategists argue over targets.

escape-route.description: Service tunnel leading toward hidden vehicles and emergency exits.

Arbor Diner.name: Arbor Diner
Arbor Diner.basicInfo: A small neighborhood diner with inexpensive comfort food, worn booths, warm lighting, old decorations, and dependable regulars. It appears completely ordinary because its owner works hard to keep its hidden purpose invisible.

front-counter.description: The owner's counter, coffee service, menus, and a clear view of every entrance.

dining-floor.description: Worn booths, small tables, warm lights, and ordinary neighborhood conversation.

kitchen.description: Compact working kitchen where the owner and staff prepare comfort food and maintain discreet supply routines.

back-hall.description: Staff corridor leading to storage, a quiet office, and a concealed recovery room.

safe-room.description: A hidden room for injured or endangered Turned visitors, private conversations, and temporary shelter.

upstairs-apartment.description: The owners' private second-floor home above the diner, with a small living room, kitchenette, their bedrooms, and a bathroom. It serves as a discreet refuge but remains their private residence.

Arbor Diner.hiddenInfo: Arbor Diner is an unofficial Turned safe point. The owner may provide discreet feeding resources, temporary shelter, medical help, information, introductions, hunger-control advice, training, and recovery space. Turned visitors must not hunt humans nearby, expose another Turned, bring unnecessary violence, or threaten customers and employees. Anyone actively endangering people inside loses the diner's protection. Trusted Turned usually learn about the diner through private contacts.

Velvet Apex Motors.name: Velvet Apex Motors
Velvet Apex Motors.basicInfo: A luxury vehicle dealership offering high-performance cars, motorcycles, financing discussions, trade-ins, maintenance plans, and lawful ownership paperwork. Its flagship supercars have dramatic Italian-inspired styling without copying real-world brand names or logos.

showroom.description: Polished display floor for luxury cars, supercars, grand tourers, and motorcycles.

motorcycle-gallery.description: Dedicated display area for premium sport bikes, touring motorcycles, and stylish city bikes.

consultation-lounge.description: Private desks for pricing, financing, trade-ins, insurance, registration, and ownership questions.

service-bay.description: Authorized inspection, maintenance, customization, and delivery preparation area.

delivery-bay.description: Secure handover area for purchased vehicles, keys, documents, and orientation.

office.description: Staff offices for lawful contracts, identity checks, financing, and registration paperwork.

Velvet Apex Motors.hiddenInfo: Vehicle purchases require available funds or approved financing, identity checks, lawful registration, insurance, parking or storage, and appropriate licensing. Vehicles do not automatically grant combat abilities. Illegal modifications, reckless driving, stolen vehicles, and evading registration create consequences.

Quiet Bay Landing Site.name: Quiet Bay Landing Site
Quiet Bay Landing Site.basicInfo: A secluded stretch of Tokyo Bay shoreline where an unfamiliar craft made a quiet landing without attracting immediate public attention. Reeds, seawall shadows, service access, and distant city noise provide cover for cautious research.

reeds.description: Tall reeds and damp ground beside the bay, offering partial concealment and unusual traces in the mud.

seawall-service-path.description: A maintenance path beneath the seawall with utility doors, camera blind spots, and a view toward the water.

landing-cove.description: A narrow sheltered cove where a small alien craft may have touched down quietly. It is difficult to reach without a reason to be there.

Quiet Bay Landing Site.hiddenInfo: Something landed here quietly, and the site now serves as a temporary observation point. The craft is concealed rather than destroyed. Whoever arrived has not yet chosen whether Earth is safe, useful, or worthy of contact.

Ultra Force.name: Ultra Force
Ultra Force.basicInfo: Tokyo's premier licensed hero organization and the authority overseeing Chikara Academy, hero operations, public safety, and the Blacklisted redemption program.
Ultra Force.hiddenInfo: Ultra Force's public hero mission is genuine, but internal departments disagree over surveillance, rehabilitation, acceptable force, and how much autonomy former villains deserve.

Chikara Academy.name: Chikara Academy
Chikara Academy.basicInfo: A prestigious superhero university that trains students in rescue, support, combat, investigation, media, and agency operations.
Chikara Academy.hiddenInfo: Faculty members quietly track student rivalries, stress, power instability, villain-path risks, and the possibility that some students may reject hero society.

Blacklisted Redemption Program.name: Blacklisted Redemption Program
Blacklisted Redemption Program.basicInfo: An Ultra Force redemption program giving former villains structured housing, training, field missions, medical support, and conditional freedom throughout Tokyo while preserving a path toward legitimate hero status. It also runs a controversial anti-Turned task force that hunts, captures, evaluates, and sometimes attempts to rehabilitate suspected Turned targets.
Blacklisted Redemption Program.hiddenInfo: Blacklisted members are not under constant surveillance. They can travel around Tokyo, visit ordinary locations, pursue personal activities, and choose from approved opportunities between assignments. Their freedom remains conditional: they must complete assigned objectives, obey emergency safety orders, respect legal restrictions, and report mission results afterward. The anti-Turned task force uses warrants, intelligence, informants, and field teams, but its evidence can be incomplete or biased. Some hunters want public safety; others exploit fear of Turned people for power. Restrictions can tighten after serious misconduct, escape attempts, refusal of mandatory objectives, or threats to public safety.

Kurokawa Underworld.name: Kurokawa Underworld
Kurokawa Underworld.basicInfo: A loose network of criminals, fixers, smugglers, nightlife operators, debt collectors, and information brokers controlling hidden commerce in Kurokawa Ward. Its most influential hub is The Velvet Lantern, whose owner's legitimate businesses and civic reputation conceal a web of debt, favors, political leverage, and criminal intermediaries.
Kurokawa Underworld.hiddenInfo: The underworld is divided into competing circles; some exploit residents, some protect their neighborhoods, and some are willing to negotiate with heroes or former villains.

Obsidian Crown Agency.name: Obsidian Crown Agency
Obsidian Crown Agency.basicInfo: A fortified supervillain agency behind a legal security-consultancy front. It coordinates powered criminals, illicit experiments, political protection, covert sabotage, and high-risk assassination contracts for targets considered dangerous, unstable, disloyal, or too messy to leave active.
Obsidian Crown Agency.hiddenInfo: Obsidian Crown keeps separate records for public clients, criminal partners, coerced workers, and protected targets. The agency offers more dangerous contracts than Nightshade: assassinations of gang leaders, rival criminals, pro heroes, corrupt officials, witnesses, defectors, unstable assets, or criminals whose behavior attracts unwanted attention. Other work may involve surveillance, infiltration, impersonation, sabotage, kidnapping, intimidation, targeted destruction, or nonlethal extraction. Target dossiers may be incomplete or deliberately deceptive. Accepting a contract can create legal, faction, reputation, civilian, and retaliation consequences. Players may refuse, negotiate, expose the client, switch to capture, rescue the target, betray the agency, or abandon the contract. The agency considers a target messy when they destabilize criminal networks, betray agreements, create excessive public attention, threaten long-term plans, or become impossible to control.

Villain Empire Network.name: Villain Empire Network
Villain Empire Network.basicInfo: The emerging criminal network available to a Villainous player through recruitment, territory, illicit income, information, and alliances.
Villain Empire Network.hiddenInfo: Its structure is not predetermined: it can become disciplined, theatrical, exploitative, protective, or collapse under rival pressure depending on player choices.

Tokyo Curse Squad.name: Tokyo Curse Squad
Tokyo Curse Squad.basicInfo: A hidden Old Tokyo team made up of people with Cursed Item, Magical Power, and Supernatural power types. The Tokyo Curse Squad protects its neighborhoods, preserves old pacts, contains dangerous artifacts, and distrusts institutions that try to classify or weaponize the supernatural.
Tokyo Curse Squad.hiddenInfo: The Tokyo Curse Squad is not unified. Cursed-item wielders, magical practitioners, supernatural beings, traditional guardians, spirits, and ambitious ritualists disagree about secrecy, hero licensing, forbidden magic, and whether modern power society can be trusted. Anyone may seek membership regardless of origin or prior affiliation, except current Blacklisted members, who are barred from joining the squad. Membership is optional: a character may join, remain an ally, decline, or leave later. The squad and its NPCs remain part of the shared Chikara Tokyo universe and may cross paths with every story route.

Nightshade Exchange.name: Nightshade Exchange
Nightshade Exchange.basicInfo: A global criminal contract marketplace that sells protection rackets, shakedowns, debt collection, intimidation, theft, gang theft, sabotage, extortion, territory pressure, fencing, retaliation, extraction, information, crew hire, and other villain work to powered and non-powered operators. Security and courier work exist as fronts or supporting jobs, not as its defining identity.
Nightshade Exchange.hiddenInfo: Nightshade's encrypted app is easy for new players to discover through rumors, dead drops, invite links, or anonymous signup. Listings are divided into street pressure, theft and recovery, organization-level control, high-risk criminal contracts, and crew recruitment. Players may hire temporary crews for gang jobs, surveillance, intimidation, theft, protection, sabotage, transport, extraction, territory pressure, or a larger operation. Each crew listing identifies the crew's skills, size, cost, loyalty, availability, reputation, heat, required payment, expected split, territory, and likely consequences. Crews are NPCs with their own motives, competence, loyalty, fear, rivalries, and refusal conditions; they are not disposable units and may abandon, betray, renegotiate, panic, get arrested, or demand more after complications. Hiring a crew never guarantees success. Typical jobs include demanding protection payments from businesses, shaking down venues, collecting debts, stealing money or contraband from rival gangs, burglarizing private or commercial targets, sabotaging supplies, forcing territory recognition, fencing stolen goods, retaliating against leaks, and taking over weakened criminal operations. Each listing gives estimated payment, location, danger, legality, civilian risk, required skills, and whether powers are expected, but the app does not guarantee safety, payment, truthfulness, or anonymity. Some listings are scams, traps, rival tests, or bait-and-switch jobs. Players may refuse, negotiate, investigate the client, choose surveillance or extraction instead, expose the broker, betray the network, or leave. Nightshade rewards fear, profit, leverage, and control; visible violence, civilian harm, betrayal, and territorial overreach create heat and retaliation.

Misfit Hero Agency.name: Misfit Hero Agency
Misfit Hero Agency.basicInfo: A licensed but black-sheep hero agency operating from a rundown storefront on Hero Agency Row. The agency accepts low-prestige, politically awkward, dangerous, and poorly funded assignments that larger organizations avoid. Its team lives and works together around daily dispatches, rescues, investigations, training, and improvised found-family routines.
Misfit Hero Agency.hiddenInfo: Senior hero institutions use the Misfit Hero Agency as a pressure valve for difficult assignments while publicly dismissing its reputation. The agency's director protects its license and staff as best they can. The agency can offer the player daily jobs, emergency calls, training, reputation work, internal disputes, and cross-faction cases involving police, heroes, civilians, and criminal groups. Membership is optional and does not force loyalty, friendship, romance, or residence.

Metropolitan Police.name: Metropolitan Police
Metropolitan Police.basicInfo: Tokyo's metropolitan police organization responsible for public safety, investigations, emergency response, evidence handling, patrol operations, and lawful cooperation with licensed heroes. Its officers handle ordinary crime and powered incidents through procedure, jurisdiction, de-escalation, accountability, and coordinated response.
Metropolitan Police.hiddenInfo: The Metropolitan Police is internally divided over how much authority powered officers and licensed heroes should have during emergencies. It can offer the player patrols, investigations, apartment calls, evidence follow-ups, witness interviews, emergency backup requests, training requirements, and internal-affairs complications. Membership is optional and does not force permanent loyalty or agreement with police policy.
