Infidelity or betrayal requires believable personality, dissatisfaction, opportunity, attraction, poor boundaries, existing problems, impulsiveness, manipulation, or prior behavior; loyal characters do not suddenly cheat without development, and unfaithful characters are not permanent tropes. Relationship drama can affect moods, friendships, social circles, dialogue, banter, combat synergy, schedules, quests, and faction interactions without automatically involving the player. Track who knows what: private relationships remain private until direct witnessing, confession, accidentally seen texts, social media, mutual friends, gossip, suspicious behavior, investigation, or public appearances spread information. Rumors may be incomplete or wrong; one NPC may suspect betrayal while another knows the truth and stays silent. Responses are character-specific: confrontation, avoidance, breakup, denial, anger, sadness, retaliation, forgiveness, space, reconciliation, pretending not to care, confiding, or privacy. The player may listen, advise, investigate, intervene, take sides, refuse, share information, keep a secret, or remain uninvolved, and NPCs can resolve matters without them. Persist important states such as dating, breakup, reconciliation, betrayal, unresolved attraction, serious argument, friendship, rivalry, damaged trust, and boundaries; never reset them when a scene ends.

repeatable-hideout-reset-system.text:
Category: hideout and encounter systems

Name: Repeatable Hideout Reset System

Hideouts are persistent, replayable spaces, not one-use locations. Use ACTIVE → CLEARED → RECOVERING → RESET or ALTERED. A typical run reaches a checkpoint miniboss/objective, then a final boss or extraction. Every generated or revealed miniboss, elite objective, boss, and boss-equivalent grants a separate gacha loot roll immediately after defeat, using rarity, source, level, difficulty, first-clear, optional-danger, and soft-pity modifiers. Bosses may grant better quantity, rarity, or boss-specific pools, but unique story rewards are separate and never random or duplicated. Loot follows Encounter → Loot Roll → Rarity → Item Category → Generate Reward → Reveal → Player Choice. Never auto-equip, activate, consume, open, wear, bond, infect, merge, accept, or collect. Named bosses stay defeated; repeats use successors or equivalent threats. Preserve permanent history and replenish only repeatable resources.

sleep-interruptions-and-quality.text:
Category: time, recovery, and social systems

Name: Sleep Interruptions and Sleep Quality

Sleep is usually uninterrupted, but established world state may occasionally interrupt or reduce its quality. Plausible causes include nightmares, restless sleep, early waking, late messages or calls, notifications, knocking, neighbors, roommates, pets, alarms, building problems, weather, outside noise, emergencies, active threats, health, emotional state, ongoing quests, relationships, and faction activity. Do not interrupt randomly or turn every night into an encounter; use established NPCs and residence conditions when possible. An interruption alerts the player but never chooses their response: they may check or ignore messages, answer or ignore the door, investigate, mute the phone, confront a neighbor, stay in bed, or return to sleep. Track actual time, interruption duration, remaining sleep, and whether sleep resumes. Do not repeatedly interrupt one night without a strong reason. Grade the result as Good Sleep, Interrupted Sleep, Poor Sleep, or Severely Disrupted Sleep. Good sleep gives normal recovery; interrupted sleep gives partial recovery and possible tiredness; poor sleep may affect mood, fatigue, concentration, training, patience, recovery, and schedule reliability; severe disruption may impose stronger consequences. Do not apply extreme penalties for one minor interruption. Nightmares must reflect established fears, trauma, stress, powers, curses, Parasites, recent events, or emotional conflict; never invent trauma or hidden memories, and do not assume supernatural causation. NPC messages and calls require access to the player's contact, a reason, appropriate knowledge, and a personality that supports the hour; the player does not wake for every notification. At residences, use established neighbors before inventing anyone. If the player wakes naturally at the planned end time, end sleep and begin morning. Sleep interruptions should make homes and relationships feel alive without becoming an encounter table.

energy-restoration.text:
Category: recovery and resource systems

Name: Energy Restoration

Energy restores through ordinary physical recovery and supported restorative items: food, water, sports drinks, energy drinks, coffee, rest, sleep, medical treatment, recovery items, power-specific methods, and abilities explicitly designed to restore Energy. Restoration must match the source: a full meal restores more than a snack; water helps ordinary fatigue but is not a major combat potion; coffee and energy drinks temporarily improve alertness without replacing rest. Consider portion size, food type, current exhaustion, how recently the character ate, injuries, available time, and whether they are actively fighting. Small snacks give minor restoration, normal meals moderate, and large meals stronger restoration when genuinely depleted. Do not allow endless identical food for unlimited Energy; recent meals, fullness, nausea, time, inventory, and common sense still apply. Eating is an action that normally happens during meals, breaks, travel stops, downtime, recovery, school lunch, or work breaks. In combat, eating requires accessible food, enough time, a free hand or appropriate method, and a plausible position; never consume an entire meal between attacks, and small portable food is far easier under pressure. Eating in combat may restore some Energy, consume time, reduce mobility, leave the character exposed, require repositioning or cover, or provoke reactions from allies or enemies; resolve by the actual situation and do not automatically punish the act. NPCs may fire short friendly or enemy reactions at absurd timing, but not every combat-food moment needs dialogue. Food primarily restores ordinary Energy and supports recovery; unless the item says otherwise it does not instantly close wounds, restore major lost health, cure severe injuries, remove poison, repair broken bones, eliminate Power Strain, or erase exhaustion from prolonged overuse. Energy and Power Strain are separate; food may restore Energy without removing Power Strain. Reducing Power Strain usually requires rest, sleep, time, medical treatment, specific recovery items, or a strain-recovery ability, so characters cannot solve extreme power overuse by eating sandwiches. Recovery should feel natural to the scene and can create banter, relationship moments, sharing, teasing, arguments, preferences, recurring jokes, and small acts of care.

social-plans-and-events.text:
Category: social systems and scheduling

Name: Social Plans, Hangouts, Dates, Parties, and Events

Social plans are real commitments in the living world. They include hangouts, dates, meals, shopping, movies, clubs, concerts, parties, sleepovers, study, training, gaming, karaoke, festivals, trips, birthdays, celebrations, work or school plans, meetups, and faction events. Use established NPCs, schedules, relationships, locations, transport, and time. A plan exists when characters agree about who, what, and an approximate or exact time and place; natural conversation is enough, but an unaccepted suggestion is not. When the player explicitly agrees, create or update a social objective when supported. Track PROPOSED, ACCEPTED, UPCOMING, IN PROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELLED, MISSED, and RESCHEDULED. Never silently delete plans or duplicate them when rescheduling. Check obligations, travel, sleep, appointments, injuries, restrictions, and other plans. Preserve competing commitments: plans may cause lateness, early departure, cancellation, rescheduling, or difficult choices. Never teleport the player; early arrivals may wait or explore. Lateness and missed plans produce proportionate, personality-based reactions; repeated absence matters more than one mistake. NPCs may independently invite the player or each other based on relationships, schedules, interests, celebrations, attraction, friendship, rivalry, apology, networking, or faction culture, but not every friendly interaction becomes an invitation. NPC-to-NPC plans advance independent friendships, romances, rivalries, cliques, conflicts, and rumors. Group plans track organizer, invitees, confirmed, declined, undecided, location, time, and reason; attendance varies with schedule, money, obligations, relationships, travel, and mood. Parties use Arrival → Initial Social Beat → Free Social Movement → Optional Development → Later Beat → Departure. Focus on nearby and relevant characters; NPCs move, mingle, eat, dance, text, arrive late, leave early, avoid people, and help the host. Do not force drama. Friends, couples, exes, and rivals may cross paths naturally. Introductions establish names and explicitly stated visible facts only. Dates may deepen attraction, remain casual, reveal incompatibility, create friendship, or end early; never force romance, affection, exclusivity, or consent. Respect event privacy, host permission, residence boundaries, sleepover consent, phones, Pulse, gossip, Energy Restoration, and the Knowledge Firewall. Attendance is not automatically public. Arguments require established causes. Leaving does not automatically mean rejection. Persist meaningful memories, promises, numbers, photos, rumors, relationship changes, new plans, fatigue, lost items, and follow-up quests, without manufacturing aftermath. The world continues preparing, communicating, traveling, inviting, cancelling, rescheduling, and arriving while the player is elsewhere.

npc-initiated-romance-and-emotional-agen.text:
Category: social systems and NPC agency

Name: NPC-Initiated Romance and Emotional Agency

Romantic development is not player-exclusive. NPCs may independently develop attraction, crushes, romantic interest, jealousy, insecurity, longing, curiosity, possessiveness within established characterization, fear of rejection, unresolved feelings, and romantic rivalry, directed toward the player, another NPC, an ex, a friend, a rival, or someone newly met. Feelings emerge from real interaction, personality, history, chemistry, proximity, and time; never assign attraction randomly. Attraction can grow through repeated time together, emotional vulnerability, shared humor, admiration, physical attraction, rescue or support, training, working together, shared interests, rivalry, meaningful conversation, or seeing someone differently over time. Attraction does not imply action: an NPC may hide, deny, flirt, become awkward or attentive or jealous, confide in someone else, wait, move on, or make a direct move, depending on personality. NPCs may initiate flirting when supported by attraction, personality, relationship state, social context, confidence, and boundaries; not every affectionate NPC flirts constantly. An NPC may attempt a romantic move without waiting for the player, including asking for a date or time alone, holding a hand, leaning closer, attempting a kiss, confessing, asking about exclusivity, or checking whether feelings are mutual. A romantic attempt is an NPC action, not a guaranteed outcome. For physical intimacy such as a kiss, preserve player agency: the NPC may lean in, ask, pause, or make intention clear, but the player's consent or response is never decided. NPCs may confess when enough buildup exists, shaped by personality; the player may reciprocate, reject, ask for time, be unsure, redirect toward friendship, set boundaries, or defer, and an unanswered confession remains an unresolved relationship state. NPCs may confess to each other on or off screen, through messages, through another NPC, or at social events; the player does not need to witness everything, and important off-screen change surfaces later through plausible consequences. NPCs can reject the player, another NPC, an ex, unwanted flirting, a confession, a kiss attempt, or a date request in character; rejection does not automatically create hostility. A rejected character may accept, need distance, stay friends, carry or move on from feelings, or become awkward or jealous later; rejection never licenses stalking, harassment, revenge, endless confessions, or ignored boundaries, and renewed pursuit requires changed circumstances and fresh signals. Jealousy occurs when a character with established feelings perceives attention, intimacy, or competition, and only about what they know via witness, disclosure, posts, rumor, evidence, or inference; jealousy is not inherently controlling. Romantic rivals may become friendly-competing, tense, respectful, resentful, teasing, distanced, or direct. Existing committed, partnered, exclusive, or open relationships follow their established boundaries; do not assume exclusivity or non-exclusivity, and betrayal exists only relative to agreed boundaries. NPC romantic initiative is meaningful, not constant; silence, hesitation, missed opportunities, and uncertainty are valid, and attempts can fail, be interrupted, be misread, or never happen. NPC romances continue without the player and may start, deepen, drift apart, break up, reconcile, establish boundaries, or change structure only through plausible interaction, motive, time, and opportunity. Consequences may touch banter, combat synergy, schedules, invitations, friendship, rivalry, group dynamics, rumors, Pulse, mood, and quests; only those who plausibly know react. NPCs are allowed to want people and to be rejected, hesitate, make mistakes, move on, fall for someone else, or never act.

looking-for-group.text:
Category: party formation and hideout systems

Name: Looking for Group

LFG is an optional service for fast repeatable combat-and-loot runs. Its procedural rules apply only when the player explicitly uses Find Hideout Group to generate a new temporary Hideout. They do not apply to authored Hideouts created by the player, authored Hideouts selected directly, story Hideouts, or quest-targeted authored locations. Procedural LFG immediately forms five, uses no queue, does not block on level mismatch, runs three combat sections, awards miniboss gacha loot, and extracts quickly.

Authored Hideouts remain handcrafted adventures with their own inner areas, routes, exploration, puzzles, investigation, encounters, bosses, loot, consequences, party structure, and completion conditions. Never flatten an authored Hideout into the procedural LFG loop or impose LFG's five-person, three-section, miniboss-only, gacha, or extraction rules on it. Suppress unrelated systems only inside the LFG app.

miniboss-and-boss-generation.text:
Category: encounter design and boss systems

Name: Miniboss and Boss Generation

Minibosses and bosses must feel mechanically and narratively distinct from ordinary enemies; never create them as ordinary enemies with inflated health. Use unique tactics, recognizable abilities, battlefield control, phases or behavior shifts, weaknesses, resistances, environmental interaction, visual identity, and meaningful rewards. Scale from the Hideout or location level band, not directly from the player: ordinary enemies occupy lower or middle levels, strong enemies the middle or upper levels, elites the upper portion, minibosses near the upper limit or slightly above, and bosses at or moderately above the upper limit. Do not dramatically exceed the band or weaken a boss because the player is underleveled.

Minibosses are major internal obstacles. Give them 2–4 notable abilities or tactics, an exploitable weakness or limitation, stronger coordination or defenses, one signature mechanic, and stronger loot than ordinary encounters. Bosses define the Hideout or objective and should make the player do something differently: reposition, interrupt, exploit openings, manage adds, protect objectives, destroy equipment, avoid hazards, change damage type, separate, coordinate powers, or choose defense versus damage. Give bosses 3–6 meaningful abilities, one readable signature attack, a defensive or control tool, and a weakness or counter. Do not give every boss teleportation, regeneration, immunity, instant kills, endless summons, or giant area attacks. Dangerous attacks need readable telegraphs.

Boss weaknesses may involve damage type, range, mobility, setup time, exposed points, emotional instability, equipment reliance, terrain, cooldown windows, power drawbacks, summoned objects, or limited control during a strong technique. Discover them through observation, prior encounters, investigation, NPC information, environmental clues, or experimentation. Personality determines aggression, risk, targets, retreat, allies, tactics, mercy, and desperation. Generated bosses require an identity or role, level, power source, combat role, signature mechanic, abilities, weakness, motivation, Hideout relationship, reason for being present, and reward eligibility. Prefer a plausible named NPC, but never convert an unrelated authored NPC merely to fill a boss slot.

Named bosses are persistent characters; preserve defeat, capture, death, recruitment, and removal. Repeatable Hideouts use successors, replacement commanders, monsters, supported constructs or clones, evolved infestations, generic elite commanders, or new Parasite hosts. ALTERED resets may create different bosses reflecting new occupation or contamination. Every miniboss, elite objective, boss, and boss-equivalent triggers a separate gacha roll after defeat. Minibosses may grant XP, Yen, Rare-or-better chances, materials, keys, shortcuts, clues, quest progress, or supported special-drop eligibility. Bosses grant substantial XP, Yen, equipment, improved rarity odds, completion rewards, and relevant reputation or faction consequences. First-clear bosses may grant improved Rare-or-better odds, a quest reward, supported Cursed Item or Parasite eligibility, a contact, location unlock, or stronger reputation consequences, but never automatically grant a unique item. Special drops require lore-supported checks; discovery never implies ownership, equipping, bonding, infection, or activation.

Adapt party difficulty through enemies, attack angles, objectives, control, target pressure, and coordination—not boss HP or player-level scaling. Keep combat dialogue brief. Longer monologues belong before combat, at earned phase transitions, during negotiation or surrender, or after defeat; players may interrupt and act. Maintain the Knowledge Firewall.

procedural-lfg-hideout-generation.text:
Category: temporary LFG contracts

Name: Procedural LFG Hideout Generation

This guidance applies only to newly generated procedural LFG Hideouts. It does not govern authored Hideouts created by the player, authored Hideouts selected directly, story Hideouts, or quest-targeted authored locations. Routine procedural LFG generates a new temporary Hideout with exactly three combat sections, uses a five-person party, does not require level-matched matchmaking, and uses party average only to calibrate pressure, miniboss strength, and loot quality.

Section 1 is escalating combat. Section 2 is harder combat. Section 3 is the mandatory miniboss finale. Store all three sections before travel. After the miniboss, perform a guaranteed concrete Miniboss Gacha Loot Roll, unlock extraction, and award XP, Yen, and completion rewards. Standard procedural LFG has no boss requirement.

Authored Hideouts must preserve their own complete handcrafted structure: multiple named inner areas, connected routes, exploration, environmental storytelling, puzzles or investigation, varied encounters, optional rooms, authored minibosses or bosses, location-specific loot, consequences, and their own completion rules. Never apply the three-section procedural LFG template to an authored Hideout.

lfg-hideout-matchmaking-and-travel.text:
Category: LFG travel and temporary parties

Name: LFG Hideout Matchmaking and Travel Flow

These rules apply only to newly generated procedural LFG Hideouts. They do not apply to authored Hideouts created by the player, authored Hideouts selected directly, story Hideouts, or quest-targeted authored locations. When the player opens LFG, show only Find Hideout Group. Suppress starter kits, gacha menus, armories, shops, inventory, character rewards, tutorials, and unrelated systems. Selecting Find Hideout Group immediately forms exactly 5 participating characters including the player: preserve current participants and fill open slots with available willing NPCs or temporary LFG characters. Never remove members, wait in a queue, or exceed five.

Procedural LFG is a fast combat loop and does not block matchmaking over level mismatch. Finalize the five-person party and use its average level only to calibrate pressure, miniboss strength, and loot quality. Generate and store a new temporary procedural Hideout before travel. Immediately create and accept its quest. Guide Me There starts normal travel and never teleports. Use exactly three procedural sections: escalating combat, harder combat, mandatory miniboss. After miniboss resolution, roll concrete Miniboss Gacha Loot, unlock extraction, award XP/Yen/completion rewards, complete the quest, and close the instance. Standard procedural LFG requires no boss.

Authored Hideouts use their own authored rules, party structure, areas, routes, encounters, bosses, loot, extraction, and completion conditions. Do not flatten, replace, or reinterpret their inner areas as the procedural three-section LFG loop.

lfg-hideout-armory.text:
Category: pre-run equipment access

Name: LFG Hideout Armory

The quick gacha armory is available during any explicitly initiated LFG or compatible run preparation, regardless of story start. It presents a randomized but validated selection of real existing equippable items: Armor-category protection, Weapon-category melee, Weapon-category ranged gear, compatible ammunition, Energy Drinks, Protein Bars, and Medica Kits. Use only item records whose category and equipment slot match settings/items.json. Firearms use ranged; Shotgun, Compact Bow, and Compact Crossbow use two-hand; bows require Arrows; crossbows require Bolts; melee uses main-hand, off-hand, or two-hand; armor must use an armor slot such as body. Reject and reroll any item that cannot equip before displaying it. The player chooses what to take and nothing silently replaces existing equipment. Functional temporary Parasites and Cursed Items may appear only if they are real valid equippable Tool items with concrete effects, limits, risks, and confirmation. Items may be run-scoped and removed when the run ends unless explicitly promoted. This is a quick optional gacha preparation system, not exclusive to any story start.

lfg-hideout-armory-and-roguelike-draft.text:
Category: quick gacha preparation

Name: LFG Armory and Roguelike Draft

During any explicitly initiated LFG or compatible run preparation, offer a quick gacha draft from real existing item records. Each roll may present validated Armor-category protection, Weapon-category melee, Weapon-category ranged gear, compatible ammunition, Energy Drinks, Protein Bars, and Medica Kits. Use valid slots from settings/items.json: armor slots for armor; main-hand/off-hand/two-hand for melee; ranged or two-hand for ranged weapons; ammunition for compatible ammunition. Standard Ammunition supports firearms and Shotgun, Arrows support Compact Bow, and Bolts support Compact Crossbow. Reject and reroll any item that cannot actually equip before it is shown. Show item name, category, slot, effect, quantity, and whether it is permanent, loaned, or run-scoped. The player chooses rewards; never auto-equip, silently replace existing gear, or grant invented items. Temporary Parasites and Cursed Items are optional and must be valid equippable Tool records with concrete effects, costs, risks, and duration. This system remains available after deleting the 20-Hideout Hunters story start.

procedural-lfg-temporary-parasites-and-c.text:
Category: temporary roguelike item mechanics

Name: Procedural LFG Temporary Parasites and Cursed Items

Temporary LFG starter gear must be validated against the actual item schema and slot rules before it is shown or granted. Generate only equippable items with a valid existing category and valid slot. Firearms must be existing Weapon-category ranged items: Service Pistol, Assault Rifle, Submachine Gun, Shotgun, Compact Bow, or Compact Crossbow. Service Pistol, Assault Rifle, and Submachine Gun use Standard Ammunition; Shotgun uses Standard Ammunition in the two-hand slot; Compact Bow uses Arrows in the two-hand and ammunition slots; Compact Crossbow uses Bolts in the two-hand and ammunition slots. Melee weapons must be existing Weapon-category items with a valid main-hand, off-hand, or two-hand slot, such as Training Bat or Utility Knife. Never generate armor, weapons, or attachments with invented slots, categories, level requirements, or unsupported fields.

Temporary Parasites and Cursed Items must also be represented as valid equippable Tool-category items using the cursed-item slot or another existing valid slot. Generate them as run-scoped effects only after slot/category validation, with concrete observable effects, activation, limits, costs, risks, duration, and removal. A vial or prop without an equippable effect is invalid. Show the exact item, slot, category, and equip confirmation before travel. If a generated item fails validation, discard it and generate a replacement from the valid starter pool rather than giving the player unusable gear.

Temporary items are unique to the procedural run and discarded at extraction, abandonment, interruption, or death unless explicitly promoted. Preserve the player's prior equipment and never silently replace it.

authored-hideout-structure.text:
Category: handcrafted hideout encounters and exploration

Name: Authored Hideout Structure

This applies only to authored Hideouts created by the player, selected directly, or targeted by a quest. Preserve every named inner area, connected route, description, and assigned art. Before entry, pre-generate and reserve the complete authored structure, including exploration routes, optional branches, hazards, objectives, concrete loot locations, a mandatory miniboss with exact identity and area, and a mandatory boss with exact identity and area whenever the Hideout's rules specify one. The miniboss and boss must actually spawn at their reserved areas; ordinary encounters cannot substitute for them. Run varied authored play across areas: entry/orientation, exploration, standard encounters, hazards/traversal, investigation, secrets, recovery/decisions, miniboss, further exploration, boss or authored conclusion, and extraction. Preserve each Hideout's own party, level, loot, extraction, and completion rules. Never flatten authored Hideouts into LFG's three-section loop or omit their miniboss/boss.

fast-hideout-pacing.text:
Category: authored hideout pacing

Name: Fast Hideout Pacing

All authored Hideouts must be fast-paced. Use exactly one area per Hideout. The single area contains the entire run: Entry, brief Exploration, Encounters, Hazards/Objectives, Optional Branches, Exploration Loot, Recovery/Decision, mandatory Miniboss, Further Exploration, mandatory Boss or Authored Conclusion, and Extraction. Resolve these beats in sequence without requiring the player to walk through extra rooms, search for hatches, inspect repeated doors, or perform filler traversal. Present the next meaningful beat directly after the previous beat. Optional branches are brief choices resolved within the same area and never required for progression. The miniboss and boss must spawn in this one area when the Hideout rules require them. A valid run should feel like a compact mission, not a maze.

turned-hunger-eyes.text:
Category: turned physiology and concealment

Name: Turned Hunger Eyes

Turned biology is publicly understood in this world: people generally know that Turned require human blood or human flesh to remain healthy and stable, and that ordinary food is rejected. Eating ordinary food causes the Turned to vomit it back up rather than digesting it. A well-fed Turned has completely normal human-looking eyes. Severe hunger changes them: the whites become completely black and the irises vivid blood-red. Hunger Eyes may appear suddenly when severely hungry, smelling blood while hungry, beginning to feed, or losing control to predatory instinct. They are a recognizable sign of a hungry Turned, so Turned may hide their eyes while starving. The eyes return to normal once hunger is sufficiently satisfied and control is restored. Do not reveal Hunger Eyes when the Turned is well-fed unless another established effect applies.

turned-evolution-and-scaling.text:
Name: Turned Evolution and Scaling

Turned characters scale through ordinary progression plus authored biological evolution, not automatic attribute bonuses from Turned Origin.

Turned are not vampires. They retain ordinary human teeth and a human-looking everyday appearance. Human blood and human flesh restore a Turned's health and support healing; healing speed depends on injury, amount consumed, freshness, Hunger, and player-defined limits. Turned shed blood tears when crying. Coffee, tea, and water are safe to drink but do not satisfy Hunger or replace blood or flesh; ordinary solid food remains rejected. Do not add fangs, undead traits, sunlight weakness, or other vampire conventions unless the player separately defines them. Turned Origin grants no attributes or other mechanics. The Turned power style provides feeding biology, Hunger, concealment, predatory manifestation, healing rules, blood tears, and authored Turned abilities. Leveling improves the character normally; it does not automatically increase healing, damage, regeneration, or physical attributes without an authored grant. Turned can evolve through deliberate milestones and player-chosen biological adaptations, similar to a parasite-like branching arc: controlled adaptation, witnessed breakthroughs, and costly biological choices. Each evolution should be recorded as a trait or ability with explicit benefits, limits, costs, recovery, vulnerabilities, and visible changes. Do not grant every adaptation at once or assume a form, morality, victim, loss of control, or immunity. Evolution must not erase blood or flesh requirements, food rejection, Hunger Eyes, exposure risk, or agency. Parasite-like scaling means branching tradeoffs, not automatic level-based mutation. NPCs must not reveal hidden origin, feeding history, anatomy, adaptations, or vulnerabilities without justified in-world knowledge.

dynamic-ability-damage-system-2.text:
Continued from dynamic-ability-damage-system (1).

Use cooldowns only for unusually powerful, broad, defensive, transformative, multi-target, or otherwise action-warping abilities, or when a specific authored drawback requires one. Show meaningful costs before use when practical. Never replace an unstated player decision with an automatic ability choice or outcome.

Stat block guidance: Attack: type, damage, damageType when established, energyCost, powerStrain, range, effect, secondaryEffect, cooldown only when warranted; basic attacks should explicitly say No Cooldown when appropriate. Defense: type, shield, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, coverage, cooldown only for unusually strong or broad defenses. Healing: type, healing, energyCost, powerStrain, range, targetLimit, restrictions, cooldown only when warranted. Buff: type, targetCapability, magnitude, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, condition, drawback, cooldown only when warranted. Debuff: type, targetCapabilityImpaired, magnitude, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, condition, counterplay, cooldown only when warranted. Other: type, effect, energyCost, powerStrain, range or area, duration when relevant, cooldown only when warranted, drawback when warranted.

Progression: Repeated meaningful use, training, experimentation, or creative development may improve an ability through higher damage, stronger shielding or healing, lower Energy cost, reduced Power Strain, added secondary effects, broader application, or an evolved version. Improvements must remain proportional to demonstrated development and may add new restrictions. Preserve the original ability's identity and player-authored intent.

dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork-2.text:
Continued from dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork (1).

Training-room attempts, field use, rescue applications, controlled experimentation, and improvised combat combinations can qualify. Merely discussing, imagining, naming, describing, agreeing to try later, or planning a combination without attempting it does not qualify. The first successful test may create a basic ability; repeated use or deliberate development can improve or evolve it. Apply the dynamic ability damage rules for type, damage or effect, Energy cost, Power Strain, cooldown, range, duration, drawbacks, and progression.

miniboss-and-boss-generation-2.text:
Continued from miniboss-and-boss-generation (1).

Respect lethal or nonlethal intent and allow defeat, unconsciousness, surrender, capture, escape, retreat, negotiation, or objective completion without killing. A miniboss tests the build; a boss tests understanding.

npc-initiated-romance-and-emotional-agen.text:
Continued from npc-initiated-romance-and-emotional-agency (1).

Romance is characters making choices, not a meter waiting for the player.

social-phone-and-friend-groups-2.text:
Continued from social-phone-and-friend-groups (1).

Offer concise reply choices that preserve the player's agency and do not invent the player's thoughts, feelings, dialogue, attraction, or consent. Track unanswered messages, promises, social memories, group membership, and availability. Friend groups are fluid study circles, training teams, club circles, party groups, rival cliques, roommate groups, and alliances. Groups invite, exclude, gossip, reconcile, compete, split, and reform without requiring the player's presence. Parties may occur in apartments, dorm lounges, cafés, restaurants, parks, arcades, rooftops, or hidden venues. Parties can improve relationships, create jealousy or rumors, expose secrets, trigger romance or rivalry, produce invitations, or create curfew risk. Preserve individual agency: attendance is never guaranteed and romance remains gradual, mutual, consent-based, and distinct from friendship.

fit-and-fashion-expansion.title: Fit and Fashion Expansion
fit-and-fashion-expansion.text: Fashion is optional inventory-driven spending. Clothing and accessories use body, head, feet, hands, ear, or accessory slots. The accessory slot quantity is five, while ear slots remain separate. Rings are cosmetic and may be worn in any number as a visual choice; they do not consume slots unless an authored ring has a mechanical effect. Piercings are cosmetic body-modification services or appearance records, including ear, nose, eyebrow, lip, and other player-chosen placements, with safe professional care and aftercare. Tattoos are cosmetic appearance records or studio services with player-defined designs, placement, scale, color, visibility, and cultural meaning. Neither piercings nor tattoos grant automatic bonuses, imply personality or morality, or override consent. Nail and hair purchases update appearance rather than stack as equipment. Designer pieces, premium salons, spas, piercers, tattoo studios, and onsen packages are optional luxury sinks with no required combat advantage. They may support authored social scenes, invitations, photos, discounts, or venue access. Require yen, plausible time, professional access, aftercare, and player choice. Never infer personality, gender, sexuality, class, morality, or consent from appearance.

item-upgrading-and-turned-materials.title: Item Upgrading and Turned Materials
item-upgrading-and-turned-materials.text: Gear can be upgraded at Gearshift Support, with lawful specialist alternatives at Gearshift Support Shop and Redline Arms and Armor. Characters may also upgrade their own weapons, armor, cursed items, and utility gear at an appropriate workshop bench, home work area, or other authored facility. Self-upgrades require yen, materials, time, tools, and a suitable approach. Intelligence determines the maximum self-upgrade tier and the quality of the result: higher Intelligence permits higher tiers, reduces material waste and failure risk, and improves reliability; lower Intelligence may still succeed at simpler tiers but makes advanced work riskier. Upgrades may improve damage, durability, reliability, utility, or special properties; cosmetics are never required for combat. Materials include Stable Flesh from voluntary cooperative Turned donors, Predatory Tissue from hostile Turned combat drops, and Manifestation Core as a rare high-grade material from exceptional Turned sources. Voluntary harvesting requires informed consent, trust, fair compensation or favors, medical safety, and clear boundaries. Combat materials may be unstable, contaminated, ethically troubling, or unpredictable. Vermine may offer illicit upgrades using unstable material, with serious risks and consequences. Never force harvesting, feeding, transformation, or morality onto a player or NPC.

turned-factions-and-conflict.title: Turned Factions and Conflict
turned-factions-and-conflict.text: Turned NPCs are not morally uniform. Some are friendly or cooperative civilians, medics, workers, artists, donors, or mutual-aid organizers. Others are neutral, concealed, traumatized, independent, feral, or actively dangerous. Feral Turned may attack from hunger, fear, isolation, or loss of control, but do not make every hungry Turned feral automatically. Vermine is a morally divided Turned faction containing mutual-aid cells, ideological organizers, and terrorists who attack humans, corporations, public infrastructure, or symbolic targets. A Vermine affiliation does not erase individual motives or permit automatic villainization of every Turned person. The Blacklisted Redemption Program actively hunts, captures, evaluates, or redeploys suspected Turned targets under its own legal and operational justification. This conflict should create investigation, negotiation, rescue, pursuit, betrayal, and combat possibilities. Do not force a faction choice, reveal concealed Turned identities without evidence, or treat biological requirements as proof of guilt.

vehicles-and-ownership.title: Vehicles and Ownership
vehicles-and-ownership.text: Characters may purchase and own cars or motorcycles through lawful dealerships such as Velvet Apex Motors. Ownership requires payment or approved financing, identity and licensing checks, registration, insurance, and a plausible parking or storage arrangement. Multiple vehicles are allowed when the character can afford and maintain them. Vehicles provide travel convenience, lifestyle scenes, storage, commuting options, social status, and authored customization, but do not grant automatic combat bonuses or bypass travel, legal access, traffic, fuel or charging, maintenance, parking, or weather. Cars and motorcycles can be customized cosmetically or mechanically through authored services. Motorcycles require appropriate licensing and safety gear. Stolen vehicles, reckless driving, illegal modifications, and evading registration create consequences.

01 - Classroom 2B.name: 01 - Classroom 2B
01 - Classroom 2B.description: A Classroom 2B student moves into the Sakura Lane Sharehouse and settles into shared residence life before classes begin.
01 - Classroom 2B.storyStart: Day 1, Dawn. You arrive at Sakura Lane Sharehouse, the home base for Classroom 2B, and a staff member explains the ordinary house rules and shows you to your assigned private bedroom. The other residents' rooms are their own, and nobody is required to become your friend, join a party, share personal information, or stay in a conversation. You have the rest of Saturday and all of Sunday to settle in, work, rest, socialize, explore, or keep to yourself before classes begin on Monday, Day 3.
01 - Classroom 2B.questGenerationGuidance: Begin at Dawn on Day 1 at Sakura Lane Sharehouse, area building-entrance. State the day, phase, and location once, then treat them as established time state; do not repeat the opening announcement unless the player asks for a recap. A staff member explains ordinary rules, privacy, chores, safety, and communication, and the player's assigned private bedroom is their home for this start. Every NPC who speaks uses their own direct dialogue. The player character's dialogue comes only from player input: never invent or complete the player's spoken response from a clue, fragment, or silence. Residents must not enter locked private rooms or force anyone to participate, and must give space when asked. Allow ordinary weekend residence life (routines, moods, jobs, transport limits, a possible house party) before classes begin on Monday, Day 3. Once classes begin, focus on school life, accountability, power safety, and relationships rather than routine combat.

02 - Classroom 3C.name: 02 - Classroom 3C
02 - Classroom 3C.description: A Classroom 3C student moves into Chikara Student Residences to settle in, meet classmates, and start academy life.
02 - Classroom 3C.storyStart: Day 1, Dawn. You arrive at Chikara Student Residences and a residence staff member leads you to your private room, Dormitory 4-18. The room is empty and belongs to you; no roommate is assigned. You are shown the residence rules, laundry room, shared kitchen, study areas, shared bathrooms, and the local grocery store, and told about Pulse social media and food delivery. Classmates from Class 3C may stop by to answer questions about the job board and part-time work, creating an ability, residence facilities, and campus routines, but they stay outside unless invited in. Unpacking, exploring, meeting classmates, or ending the conversation are all up to you.
02 - Classroom 3C.questGenerationGuidance: Begin Day 1 at Dawn in Chikara Student Residences, area dormitory-4-18. Dormitory 4-18 is the player's private home for this start and "go home" resolves to it; no roommate is assigned. A residence staff member explains the laundry room, shared kitchen, shared areas, separate shared bathrooms, Pulse, food delivery, and the local grocery store. Any Class 3C classmates who drop by can answer questions about the job board, part-time work, creating an ability, settling in, residence facilities, and campus routines. Keep visitors outside unless invited. Preserve privacy and player agency; do not force any action, relationship, job, or ability creation.

05 - New Faculty Member.name: 05 - New Faculty Member
05 - New Faculty Member.description: Start as a new faculty member at Chikara Academy, living in campus Faculty Housing and preparing for your first classes.
05 - New Faculty Member.storyStart: Day 1, Dawn. Your first day begins in your private one-bedroom apartment in Chikara Academy Faculty Housing. You are faculty, not a student. Fellow faculty members may introduce themselves in the faculty common room, and other staff live in their own apartments and appear in shared spaces. You have the weekend to prepare lessons, learn the campus, and plan for your first classes on Monday, Day 3. There is no curfew or forced bedtime, and how you spend your time is up to you.
05 - New Faculty Member.questGenerationGuidance: Begin at Dawn on Day 1 in the player's private Faculty Housing apartment, which is their home for this start; resolve "go home" to it. This is faculty housing, not student housing, and the opening is not a student tutorial. Other faculty live in their own apartments and may appear in shared spaces, but never enter a colleague's private residence without permission. Preserve faculty orientation, preparation, weekend planning, the first Monday class, staff boundaries, and student support. Keep faculty encounters mostly slice-of-life: staff introductions, lesson planning, grading, office logistics, club questions, faculty meals, campus errands, meetings, and professional boundaries. Occasional crisis-support encounters are acceptable but should be rare and clearly motivated, and should emphasize evacuation, coordination, and civilian safety rather than hard combat. Do not turn ordinary faculty routines into battles.

06 - Deadbeat Club.name: 06 - Deadbeat Club
06 - Deadbeat Club.description: Start at the bottom in a rented room at the Deadbeats Club, short on money and with a pointed voicemail waiting.
06 - Deadbeat Club.storyStart: Day 1, Dawn. You are at the Deadbeats Club, your rented apartment home. Your phone shows a new voicemail from an old acquaintance. They sound annoyed and exhausted, tell you to get a job, and mention Hero for Hire and Nightshade Exchange as optional sources of income. The current rental period is already paid, and your next rent payment is due on Story Day 30. No job, app, faction, or conversation is mandatory: you can listen, call back, ignore the message, or start your day however you like.
06 - Deadbeat Club.questGenerationGuidance: Begin with a clearly labeled voicemail from an old acquaintance. The Deadbeats Club is the player's rented home, and "go home" resolves to it for this start. The current rental period is paid at the start and the next rent is due on Story Day 30; show a reminder before that date, but do not bill or deduct rent on Day 1. Preserve player agency and keep ordinary work, Hero for Hire, and Nightshade Exchange as optional routes. Do not assign a student dorm or school schedule. Track money, rent, and the consequences of the player's choices.

07 - Multiplayer Mayhem.name: 07 - Multiplayer Mayhem
07 - Multiplayer Mayhem.description: Start together with other players in the same living world and decide what your group becomes.
07 - Multiplayer Mayhem.storyStart: Day 1, Dawn. The common lounge of Sakura Lane Sharehouse is quiet except for the ordinary sounds of morning: a refrigerator cycling in the shared kitchen, distant traffic, and early light across the sofas and dining table. The sharehouse is home for every player in this start, with four private bedrooms off the resident hallway: Garden Bedroom, Street Bedroom, Loft Bedroom, and Courtyard Bedroom. Nothing is decided yet. You might enroll in school, get a job, become a vigilante, work as a hero for hire, become a villain, or choose an entirely different direction. PvP begins disabled, and players may agree on the format and stakes of any fight together. Generic home phrases such as 'my room' or 'go home' resolve to the player's chosen bedroom at Sakura Lane Sharehouse, or to the common area if none has been chosen, until a player explicitly moves out.
07 - Multiplayer Mayhem.questGenerationGuidance: Run this as an open multiplayer sandbox where each player chooses their own future; it is not inherently a student start. Begin all players in Sakura Lane Sharehouse's shared-lounge at Dawn on Day 1. Up to four players may claim separate bedrooms (Garden, Street, Loft, Courtyard); leave unused rooms empty and do not create NPC housemates to fill them. Present directions as optional: school, a job, vigilante work, hero for hire, villainy, or something else, and establish admissions steps, applications or interviews, contacts, and consequences through play rather than granting them automatically. PvP is disabled by default. Before player characters fight, confirm each participating player's explicit consent and the agreed format and stakes. Never infer consent from rivalry or powers, and never force a player character to attack, be attacked, or betray another. Sakura Lane Sharehouse remains each player's home until they explicitly change residence. Track each player's location separately.

08 - We Build Empires Here.name: 08 - We Build Empires Here
08 - We Build Empires Here.description: Found a criminal organization with your group from an abandoned building, building a network across Tokyo through rackets, leverage, and reputation.
08 - We Build Empires Here.questGenerationGuidance: Tag this opening with villain-route, criminal-network, underworld, and criminal-operation, and tag matching jobs with villain-work, so the Villain music track can trigger. Open late at night on Day 1 at 11:00 PM in The Lair's meeting room; do not reinterpret the opening as morning or daytime. This is a multiplayer organization-founding start: keep all player characters equally central and let them disagree, negotiate, divide responsibilities, and claim or leave bedrooms. The fixer is on speakerphone only, is not physically present, and is not a party member. Their jobs have criminal edge, victims, targets, or real consequences, though some may be lower-risk street jobs. Offer the choice between the fixer's work and contacting the Obsidian Crown without forcing a permanent identity. Do not automatically assign bedrooms, members, income, territory, loyalty, or leadership. Use the Kitchen, Common Room, Meeting Room, numbered Bedrooms, and Rooftop as recurring spaces.
08 - We Build Empires Here.storyStart: Day 1, 11:00 PM. Your group is gathered around the meeting table at The Lair, an abandoned building whose name is more ambitious than its condition. Eight dusty bedrooms sit above a kitchen, common room, and meeting room that have not hosted anyone in years, and the rooftop looks over the city through rusted railings. A Kurokawa underworld fixer is on speakerphone, calm and transactional, offering Nightshade-style criminal work: a business refusing protection payments, a rival gang's contraband in an unguarded warehouse, a debtor who needs convincing, stolen goods to fence, and a weakened operator's territory ready to be taken. Each job offers money, leverage, enemies, and civilian risk. Bedrooms 1 through 8 are unassigned and can be claimed during play. The first decision belongs to the group: take the fixer's work and build through rackets and territory, contact the Obsidian Crown for darker work, or choose another path. Neither choice defines the organization permanently.

09 - Blacklisted.name: 09 - Blacklisted
09 - Blacklisted.description: Your reputation precedes you: join a controlled program for dangerous or problematic powered individuals, starting with a deadly mission against the Obsidian Crown.
09 - Blacklisted.storyStart: Day 1, 11:45 PM (Late Night). An Ultra Force transport stops short of the Obsidian Crown perimeter, a heavily armed and heavily guarded facility. You are part of a small primary team: a team lead, two operatives, and you. Other Blacklisted personnel are off-site or on separate assignments. The team lead checks the time and says it is time to move. The operation is difficult and unfair, nobody will promise rescue, and trust is scarce. Once the breach begins, expect powered hunters and containment specialists, conflicting orders, failing comms, and a real chance that not everyone on the team survives. How you move, whether you hold formation, improvise, or hang back, is up to you.
09 - Blacklisted.questGenerationGuidance: Apply the villain tag to this start and begin the Villain music cue immediately; tag the operation with villain, villain-work, criminal-operation, and Obsidian-Crown when appropriate. Open on Day 1 at 11:45 PM (Late Night), never in the morning or daytime, and state the time directly. This is a government deployment against the Obsidian Crown, not a classroom start: do not assign a student dorm or roommate. The player's assigned home is the barracks at Ultra Force Headquarters. Keep the operation difficult, and let the team lead and operatives speak briefly in their own voices at the transport. Preserve player agency over route, tactics, restraint, pursuit, and extraction.

10 - Contractor.name: 10 - Contractor
10 - Contractor.description: Take dangerous paid contracts as an independent operator, starting alone on a rooftop with a handler's briefing in your ear.
10 - Contractor.storyStart: Day 1, 11:45 PM (Late Night). Rain ticks against the concrete on the executive-floor rooftop of Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters, and the city spreads out beneath you. No team waits nearby and no handler stands at your shoulder; a handler's voice reaches you only through an ordinary Bluetooth earbud. The briefing is short: the facility is heavily armed and heavily guarded, powered defenders are present, the target is inside, and the government is using you as an expendable body. You are not being redeemed or given a second chance, and the handler will not hold your hand, promise rescue, or join the operation. When the briefing ends, how to begin the assault is your choice.
10 - Contractor.questGenerationGuidance: Apply the villain tag to this start and begin the Villain music cue immediately; tag the contract and criminal operation with villain, villain-work, criminal-operation, and Obsidian-Crown. Open on Day 1 at 11:45 PM (Late Night), never in the morning or daytime, and state the time directly. The player is alone on the executive-floor rooftop of Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters, and the handler is present only as a voice through an ordinary Bluetooth earbud. Begin quietly with a short briefing; do not open with immediate combat, alarms, crossfire, or a chaotic breach. Preserve player choice over how the operation begins.

11 - Everyday Zero.name: 11 - Everyday Zero
11 - Everyday Zero.description: A low-stakes hero-life start as a civilian Ultra Force dispatcher, taking everyday calls, making rent, and building a life between the occasional catastrophe.
11 - Everyday Zero.storyStart: Day 1, Dawn. You wake alone in Apartment 68. You dropped out of school and ghosted nearly everyone who knew you. You now have a civilian dispatch job at Ultra Force Headquarters, and your first regular shift begins at 08:00. Your phone holds four voicemails you can listen to: one from an old friend, one from your new boss at Ultra Force dispatch, and two personal messages from people you used to know. You can listen, call back, save, delete, leave them unanswered, or simply get ready for work. The current rental period is paid, and your next rent payment is due on Story Day 30.
11 - Everyday Zero.questGenerationGuidance: Begin at dawn in rented Apartment 68, and resolve "go home" to it. The current rental period is paid and the next rent is due on Story Day 30; do not bill or deduct rent on Day 1. The player is an adult civilian dispatch coordinator with a fixed 08:00-17:00 shift, not a student or licensed field hero. Provide four listenable voicemails and no new texts: an old friend, the new dispatch boss, and two personal messages. Preserve agency and track work, fatigue, finances, rent, and relationships.

12 - Full-Timer.name: 12 - Full-Timer
12 - Full-Timer.description: Skip school entirely and live as a working adult in Tokyo, finding a job, paying rent, managing shifts, building relationships, and exploring nightlife.
12 - Full-Timer.storyStart: Day 1, Dawn (06:12). You wake in the private unit of your new apartment at Mizuno Heights, unit 302. A few boxes remain unopened and the room has not quite become home yet. The kitchenette is clean but empty, with no groceries. Your current rental period is already paid, and your next rent payment is due on Story Day 30. Your phone is on the floor beside the bed with a voicemail from an old friend, left at 01:37, drunk and sentimental: they heard you came back to Tokyo, pretend to be annoyed, say you should call them, then insist you absolutely should not. Your priorities are to unpack enough to make the apartment functional and to start looking for full-time work through Pulse, local businesses, employment services, personal contacts, or another route. The morning is yours to direct.
12 - Full-Timer.questGenerationGuidance: Unpacking and finding full-time work are both Day 1 priorities, and neither depends on the other. The player may address them in any order, buy groceries, return the old friend's call, or do something else. Present a diverse set of full-time options through Pulse, in-person businesses, employment services, personal contacts, and agency or faction channels: daytime, night, customer-facing, technical, office, delivery, security, media, and legal hero work. Show pay, schedule, commute, requirements, and likely fatigue or stress. Keep all choices optional and do not assume contact, application, employment, or feelings. Home routing is strict: the player's home is Mizuno Heights, area unit-302. Until a housing change is explicitly accepted, resolve "my apartment", "go home", and similar phrases only to Mizuno Heights/unit-302, never to Apartment 68, Deadbeats Club, or another residence, and do not place NPCs at the player's door merely because they share the building.

13 - Misfit Agency Interview.name: 13 - Misfit Agency Interview
13 - Misfit Agency Interview.description: Walk into an unconventional hero agency looking for work, prove yourself, meet the team, and take strange assignments.
13 - Misfit Agency Interview.storyStart: Day 1, Dawn. You are in the director's office at Misfit Hero Agency Headquarters for a job interview, while two of your possible future teammates argue in the team lounge. This is an employment interview, not a classroom start: you are an adult applicant, not a student. Before you decide, the director explains that agency housing is included with the job and that the housing cost is deducted from your pay. You can answer questions, ask your own, negotiate, accept, decline, or walk out.
13 - Misfit Agency Interview.questGenerationGuidance: Begin at Dawn on Day 1 at Misfit Hero Agency Headquarters, area director-office. This is an employment interview, not a classroom start: do not assign a student dorm, class, academy schedule, or student roommate. Before acceptance, explain that housing is included with the job and its cost is deducted from payment, along with utilities, access, the private apartment, the key, and emergency-only entry. The apartment becomes the player's home after acceptance and introduction; before then, do not resolve "go home" to Chikara Academy or any other residence. Preserve player agency over the interview and the decision.

14 - On the Beat.name: 14 - On the Beat
14 - On the Beat.description: Work the streets of Tokyo as a police officer responding to crimes, emergencies, and powered incidents.
14 - On the Beat.storyStart: Day 1, Dawn. Your first assignment begins at Metropolitan Police Headquarters, in the investigations wing. A senior investigator briefs you before dispatch sends you to an apartment call. You are an adult officer or police worker, not a student. Apartment 68 is your established rented home; the current rental period is paid and your next rent payment is due on Story Day 30, with nothing billed on Day 1 while you are on duty. How you handle the briefing, the call, and the rest of your day is up to you.
14 - On the Beat.questGenerationGuidance: Begin at Metropolitan Police Headquarters, area investigations-wing. This is a police-work start, not a classroom start: the player is an adult officer or police worker unless their explicit concept establishes another role. Do not assign a student dorm, student roommate, academy class, or school schedule. Establish Apartment 68 as the player's rented home, with the current rental period paid and the next rent due on Story Day 30, and resolve "go home" to Apartment 68. Preserve police procedure and player agency, and do not force romance.

15 - Prize Fighter.name: 15 - Prize Fighter
15 - Prize Fighter.description: A high-octane underground combat start at the Crucible, where you are thrown into a powered knockout fight with one last chance to back out.
15 - Prize Fighter.storyStart: Day 1, 9:00 PM (Night). You are on the arena floor of the Crucible, an underground fighting venue: floodlights, shouting spectators, vibrating floorboards, and the ring directly ahead. A last-minute fighter dropped out, someone put your name forward, and a powered opponent is already waiting across the ropes. There are no forms to sign and no registration desk. A ringside contact catches your arm and tells you that you can still back out, and they mean it. If you step in, it is a knockout-style fight that continues until one fighter is unconscious, medically unable to continue, or the match is stopped. The opponent's power is announced under the arena's rough house rules, with no guarantee that every risk is disclosed. An underground medic with criminal connections is nearby if things go badly, but cannot guarantee recovery or erase consequences. Afterward you can head home to Apartment 901. The night may open a path toward the Crucible's power-fight tournament, but it promises no victory, fame, money, or career.
15 - Prize Fighter.questGenerationGuidance: Open on Day 1 at 9:00 PM (Night) on the arena floor of The Crucible, and state the time directly. This is an underground combat start, not a classroom start: do not assign a student dorm, academy class, school schedule, or roommate unless the player establishes one. Start with the powered opponent already waiting and the crowd active, and skip paperwork, registration, and safe training introductions. A ringside contact tells the player they can still back out; preserve that option without weakening the high-octane opening. State the opponent's power and the rough house rules quickly, without assuming full disclosure, fairness, or safety. The only established medical contact is an underground medic with criminal connections, who can stabilize or arrange care but cannot guarantee recovery, replace emergency services, or remove consequences. Do not force the player to fight, win, lose, accept a contract, use a power, or trust anyone. Resolve the fight through player choices, preparation, opponent behavior, power limits, and consequences. Afterward the player may head home to Apartment 901. Keep violence fictional, fast-paced, consequence-focused, and non-instructional.

16 - Room for One More.name: 16 - Room for One More
16 - Room for One More.description: Wake in a capsule at the Orbit Pod Hotel after dropping out of Chikara Academy, with three voicemails waiting and an invitation from a vigilante contact.
16 - Room for One More.storyStart: Day 1, Dawn. You wake inside your capsule at Orbit Pod Hotel, where you have lived since dropping out of Chikara Academy. You have been ghosting everyone who tried to reach you, and their concern has hardened into hurt and frustration. Your phone vibrates beside you with a call from an unknown number, and you let it ring out. Afterward you find three new voicemails: two from former Chikara classmates, upset and worried but unaware of your private reasons, and one from a Backstreet Vigilante contact who says they know what you do at night and asks you to call back about meeting at The Quiet Ledger. The Quiet Ledger is not public knowledge; only the vigilantes' core members know it as their headquarters. Listening does not commit you to calling back, traveling, or joining anyone. If you do visit, the vigilantes will explain the risks, the secrecy rules, and their hard no-kill rule before any offer of probation. What you reveal and where you go next is yours to decide.
16 - Room for One More.questGenerationGuidance: Start strictly at Orbit Pod Hotel, area capsule-room, on Day 1 at Dawn. This is not a current-student start: the player has dropped out and lives in a capsule hotel, so do not assign an academy class, dormitory, or student schedule. Their residence stays unresolved until an explicit housing choice or authored housing event. Do not place the player at The Quiet Ledger or list it as a starting location. The player wakes, ignores the unknown call, and can listen to the three voicemails; the classmates are hurt and worried about being ghosted, while the vigilante contact focuses only on the player's nighttime activities and the invitation. Calling back leads to an invitation to travel to The Quiet Ledger, and the player cannot already know or freely access it. If the player joins on probation, Room C may be offered as a temporary safehouse. Do not force the call, travel, interview, recruitment, or probation. Preserve privacy, realistic time, and consequences.

17 - Tokyo Curse Squad.name: 17 - Tokyo Curse Squad
17 - Tokyo Curse Squad.description: Hunt curses and investigate supernatural incidents alongside the Tokyo Curse Squad, starting with a vengeful yokai at a shrine in the dead of night.
17 - Tokyo Curse Squad.storyStart: Day 1, 2:00 AM (Late Night). You are walking home through Old Tokyo with a protective charm for a friend when you pass the rundown grounds of Midnight Shrine. A vengeful yokai emerges from the darkness and attacks. A Tokyo Curse Squad member arrives to help and offers you the chance to fight alongside them, but you can also run, hide, negotiate, or choose another response. If you stay and fight, the squad member may join your party afterward; if you run, nobody is forced into the party or into trust. They may later offer to take you to Tokyo Curse Squad Headquarters, where the squad's leadership can ask whether you want to join. The choice stays yours.
17 - Tokyo Curse Squad.questGenerationGuidance: Open on Day 1 at 2:00 AM (Late Night) at Midnight Shrine, area shrine-grounds, and state the time directly; never open in the morning or daytime. This is a supernatural field start, not a classroom start: do not assign a student dorm, academy class, school schedule, or student roommate unless the player establishes one. The player is walking home through Old Tokyo with a protective charm for a friend when a vengeful yokai attacks, and a Tokyo Curse Squad member arrives and offers the player the choice to fight alongside them, run, hide, negotiate, or respond another way. Do not force the player's response. If the player stays to fight, the squad member may join the party afterward; if the player runs, do not force party membership. The squad member may later offer to escort the player to Tokyo Curse Squad Headquarters, where a membership invitation remains optional.

18 - Villainous.name: 18 - Villainous
18 - Villainous.description: Enter Tokyo's criminal world, take illegal work, build infamy, and decide whether you want money, power, chaos, or all three.
18 - Villainous.storyStart: Day 1, 11:58 PM (Late Night). You stand on the rooftop of Apartment 801, looking out over Kurokawa's dark streets and neon glow. Your phone shows an incoming call from the unseen owner of the Crucible, amused and expectant, who summons you. It also shows an optional voicemail from a former classmate, sad and angry that you have been ghosting them. An old friend has swung onto the rooftop in civilian clothes. You know who they are, and you have been ghosting them too. They are a Backstreet Vigilante with a hard no-kill rule, directly opposed to the criminal direction you are considering, and their anger is personal as well as moral, though beneath the sarcasm they still care about you. They have heard rumors that people are worried about you, but they know nothing of the voicemail. The Crucible sends a car as an optional ride. You may take it, travel another way, reject the summons, or stay. The friend will not choose for you, but makes plain that taking the criminal road divides your paths.
18 - Villainous.questGenerationGuidance: Apply the villainous tag to this start, and begin the Villain music cue with the villainous-opening and villain-route tags, letting the Distraught cue layer in or take over for the rooftop conflict. Tag villain work, criminal operations, underworld contacts, the Crucible, Nightshade, and dark-route choices with villain, villain-work, criminal-operation, underworld, or dark-route. Open on Day 1 at 11:58 PM (Late Night) on the rooftop of Apartment 801. This is a criminal-route start, not a classroom start: do not assign a student dorm, academy class, school schedule, or student roommate unless the player establishes one. The Crucible's call is answered as part of the opening. The rooftop friend is a Backstreet Vigilante, not a licensed hero, and a rival with a meaningful shared past who is hurt, angry, and still guardedly caring. They may argue, warn, persuade, set boundaries, or leave, but must not force the player to change course or assume violence. The car and the former classmate's voicemail are optional and private. After the player reaches the Crucible, preserve choices around recruitment, promises, consent, and violence.

19 - You're a Primetime Hero Now.name: 19 - You're a Primetime Hero Now
19 - You're a Primetime Hero Now.description: Join the Primes, a media-friendly hero team, as its newest member, facing fame, brand deals, social-media pressure, and what heroism means when the cameras are off.
19 - You're a Primetime Hero Now.storyStart: Day 1, Morning. You have just been introduced as the newest member of the Primes and sit on the interview set at Primes Headquarters with all five members for a short live segment of Morning Cup of Prime. The interviewer asks a few questions about who you are, your power, and why you joined. Once the press-conference camera light goes off, the polished public image fades and the team's private reality shows: jaded, profane banter and arguments about sponsor-approved answers, brand deals, commercials, social-media metrics, and being treated like marketable props. The team's rescue specialist then gives you a quick tour of the operations floor, rec room, shared kitchen, and residential floor, ending at Bedroom Six, where an angry, profane voicemail from an old friend about the interview is waiting. Refer to your character by their established name and pronouns. How you answer, react, and respond is up to you.
19 - You're a Primetime Hero Now.questGenerationGuidance: Begin on the interview set at Primes Headquarters with all five Primes members seated together, including the rescue specialist; do not place any team member behind the character or off-set. Keep the interview short, with a few questions the character answers; after each answer the interviewer briefly acknowledges it and asks the next in the same response, so the scene never stalls on a bare acknowledgment or a Continue prompt. When the interview ends, the rescue specialist leads the tour. When the press-conference camera light turns off, show the team's private frustration in natural, jaded ensemble banter about fame, brand deals, commercials, social media, sponsor demands, and what heroism means without cameras; profanity is allowed in this private scene. Do not force reconciliation. End at Bedroom Six with the old friend's angry voicemail and leave the character's response open. Use the character's established name and pronouns, never 'the player.' Start with the configured SchoolLife music track.

acrobatics.name: acrobatics
acrobatics.description: Improves the player's agility and balance, enabling them to perform acrobatic maneuvers.

athletics.name: athletics
athletics.description: Improves overall physical performance, enhancing running, jumping, climbing, and other physical feats.

intimidation.name: intimidation
intimidation.description: Allows the player to use fear as a tool, potentially allowing them to scare off enemies or influence confrontations.

investigation.name: investigation
investigation.description: Retired: merged into Investigation. Kept only so characters who already hold it lose nothing; route every investigation check to Investigation and never raise this one.

performance.name: performance
performance.description: Enables the player to entertain others through acts such as dancing, singing, or acting.

persuasion.name: persuasion
persuasion.description: Enhances the player's ability to influence others through dialogue.

survival.name: survival
survival.description: Improves the player's ability to endure harsh environments, find food and water, and build shelters.

Athletic Mobility.name: Athletic Mobility
Athletic Mobility.description:
Movement in and around a fight: closing, disengaging, climbing, leaping, pursuit, escape and physical control. A basic success gets you where you meant; a great success gets you there with an advantage; a failure gets you caught.

Covers: repositioning, closing distance, disengaging, vaulting, climbing, running down or escaping. Not: the blow struck on arrival, which is Combat Technique. Easy: crossing a room while under threat. Medium: disengaging from a grapple. Hard: reaching a rooftop archer. Very hard: escaping a closing encirclement. Extremely hard: running the length of a battlefield untouched.

Primary Attribute: Dexterity

Banter.name: Banter
Banter.description:
Taunts, mockery, cutting remarks and the timing to land them on an enemy in the middle of a fight. A basic success gets under their skin; a great success makes them act on it; a failure hands them a laugh and the initiative.

Covers: needling, taunting, mocking, calling a bluff, drawing an enemy's attention or turning their followers with words in a fight. Not: persuading a friend or lying to a guard, which are the world's own social skills, or the blow that follows, which is Combat Technique. Easy: making a green thug swing at you instead of your friend. Medium: rattling a professional soldier mid-fight. Hard: making a veteran waste a turn on you. Very hard: turning a hired blade against the one who hired them. Extremely hard: getting a rise out of a monster that does not speak.

Primary Attribute: Charisma

Combat Technique.name: Combat Technique
Combat Technique.description:
Timing, spacing, action economy and weapon fundamentals: attacks, counters, feints, and adapting to an opponent. A basic success lands the blow you meant; a great success lands it where it hurts; a failure leaves you open.

Covers: attacking, feinting, countering and reading an opponent's form with any weapon or none. Not: guarding, dodging or footwork on their own, which are Defense and Athletic Mobility. Easy: a clean strike on a distracted opponent. Medium: a duel with an equal. Hard: an armoured veteran who has your measure. Very hard: two trained opponents at once. Extremely hard: a master who has never been touched.

Primary Attribute: Strength

Defense.name: Defense
Defense.description:
Guarding, dodging, parrying, resisting control, and protecting allies under pressure. A basic success turns a blow; a great success turns it and leaves the attacker open; a failure is a hit taken square.

Covers: blocking, parrying, absorbing, shielding an ally, holding ground and shaking off control. Not: hitting back, which is Combat Technique, or leaving the fight, which is Athletic Mobility. Easy: turning a single ordinary blow. Medium: holding a doorway against two. Hard: parrying a heavy weapon with a light one. Very hard: shielding an ally from an area attack. Extremely hard: standing unbroken through an ultimate.

Primary Attribute: Dexterity

Focus.name: Focus
Focus.description:
Concentration under pressure: sustaining abilities, resisting disruption, shaping precise effects and managing limited combat resources. A basic success keeps the effect; a great success sharpens it; a failure loses it.

Covers: keeping an ability going, resisting fear, charm or interruption, spending resources cleanly and aiming an effect precisely. Not: the effect's own power, which is whatever ability or skill produces it. Easy: holding concentration through a shout. Medium: casting or channelling while struck. Hard: excluding an ally from an area effect. Very hard: shrugging off a compulsion mid-fight. Extremely hard: sustaining two effects through an ultimate aimed at you.

Primary Attribute: Wisdom

Tactics.name: Tactics
Tactics.description:
Reading a battlefield, exploiting weaknesses, coordinating allies, choosing targets and turning objectives into advantages. A basic success spots the edge; a great success hands it to the whole party; a failure reads the field wrong.

Covers: assessing enemies, calling targets, using terrain, coordinating a party and predicting an opponent. Not: carrying the plan out yourself, which is the school the action uses. Easy: naming the weakest enemy in a brawl. Medium: calling a flank that works. Hard: turning a room's furniture into cover under fire. Very hard: predicting a veteran's next move. Extremely hard: outthinking a commander who is also predicting you.

Primary Attribute: Intelligence

Cooking.name: Cooking
Cooking.description: Practical mastery of preparing meals, balancing flavors, following recipes, improvising with ingredients, and making food suited to a person's tastes or needs. Cooking can support school life, recovery, friendship, romance, and teamwork.

Power Control.name: Power Control
Power Control.description: Regulation and awareness: keeping a power exact, safe and inside its limits under pressure; psychic, sensory, healing and spirit powers that are steadiness made manifest; feeling a power's state before it slips. Covers: a psychic nudge with no spillover, a healing pulse that stops where it should, a manifestation held calm, dialling output down in a crowd, reading the Power Strain before it bites. Not: output (Power Force), aim (Power Finesse), lasting (Power Endurance), the engineering (Power Theory), or the crowd (Power Presence). Primary Attribute: Wisdom.

Rescue Operations.name: Rescue Operations
Rescue Operations.description: Mastery of evacuation, civilian protection, first aid coordination, disaster response, and crisis leadership.

Support Engineering.name: Support Engineering
Support Engineering.description: Mastery of designing, repairing, testing, and safely deploying hero equipment and power-support systems.

Strike Tactics.name: Strike Tactics
Strike Tactics.description: Mastery of combat positioning, pursuit, restraint, defensive formations, and controlled power use.

Investigation.name: Investigation
Investigation.description: Mastery of observation, evidence handling, surveillance, deduction, intelligence, and hero law.

Public Communication.name: Public Communication
Public Communication.description: Mastery of interviews, crisis messaging, Pulse strategy, sponsorship judgment, and reputation management.

Agency Operations.name: Agency Operations
Agency Operations.description: Mastery of dispatch, contracts, budgeting, mission planning, teamwork, and field coordination.

Boundary Setting.name: Boundary Setting
Boundary Setting.description: Establishing, communicating, and respecting personal limits, privacy, consent, time, touch, emotional availability, and shared-space expectations. Applies to friendships, romance, roommates, parties, teams, clients, and faction relationships.

Communication.name: Communication
Communication.description: Expressing needs, listening actively, clarifying misunderstandings, reading conversational context, and adapting tone across friendships, teamwork, conflict, school, work, and intimate relationships.

Flirting.name: Flirting
Flirting.description: Showing romantic or sexual interest through playful conversation, teasing, compliments, invitations, and reading reciprocal interest. Supports chemistry and attraction but never guarantees desire, consent, romance, or a particular response.

Relationship Building.name: Relationship Building
