Relationship Building.description: Developing trust, familiarity, mutual support, repair after conflict, and durable connections through consistent attention and meaningful shared experiences. Applies to friendship, romance, rivalry, teamwork, clients, and faction ties.

Deception.name: Deception
Deception.description: Concealing truth, constructing believable lies, maintaining cover identities, disguising motives, manipulating impressions, and detecting when a conversation requires careful misdirection. Applies to investigations, undercover work, criminal negotiations, social conflict, secrets, and protecting allies. Deception does not guarantee that others believe the player and should be challenged by evidence, scrutiny, relationships, and consequences.

Close Quarters Combat.name: Close Quarters Combat
Close Quarters Combat.description: Mastery of unarmed fighting at close range, including punches, kicks, clinches, takedowns, holds, escapes, positioning, and nonlethal restraint.

Weapon Proficiency.name: Weapon Proficiency
Weapon Proficiency.description: Mastery of safely handling, aiming, maintaining, and fighting with a chosen weapon category. Each character must specify the weapon category they actually trained with; proficiency does not grant access to weapons or invent training.

Empathy.name: Empathy
Empathy.description: Recognizing, understanding, and responding appropriately to other people's emotions, needs, boundaries, and perspectives without assuming perfect accuracy or mind-reading.

Power Endurance.name: Power Endurance
Power Endurance.description: Sustaining and bearing: body-based powers, mutations, blood and flesh, barriers held for minutes, a curse's cost carried, strain pushed through without collapse. Covers: holding a ward through a whole fight, feeding a parasite and staying yourself, keeping a changed body working under damage, taking the recoil of a power and standing. Not: the burst itself (Power Force), the aim (Power Finesse), the design (Power Theory), the regulation (Power Control), or the audience (Power Presence). Primary Attribute: Constitution.

Power Finesse.name: Power Finesse
Power Finesse.description: Precision and speed: aiming, timing, threading a power through a gap, repositioning, portals and flickers placed exactly, a touch that does one thing and nothing else. Covers: a shot through a window, a blink to the right rooftop, a thread spun to a wrist, a cut that takes the cable and not the hand. Not: brute output (Power Force), holding it up all day (Power Endurance), designing it (Power Theory), keeping it from slipping (Power Control), or performing it (Power Presence). Primary Attribute: Dexterity.

Power Force.name: Power Force
Power Force.description: Raw output: putting the whole body and the whole power behind one expression. Blasts, impacts, lifting, bracing, breaking, holding a line by main strength, and powers that are muscle made strange. Covers: a full-power discharge, a thrown car, a wall of force, a charge that ends at the enemy. Not: aim, timing or subtlety (Power Finesse), lasting the distance (Power Endurance), understanding the mechanism (Power Theory), restraint (Power Control), or moving people (Power Presence). Primary Attribute: Strength.

Power Presence.name: Power Presence
Power Presence.description: Will, voice and bearing: powers that act through impression, sound, light, bargains, charms, faith, performance and the force of a self-defined identity. Covers: a note that turns a room, an illusion that convinces, a contract invoked with authority, a charm that holds, a god-label made real by being witnessed. Not: brute output (Power Force), precision (Power Finesse), bearing a cost (Power Endurance), the mechanism (Power Theory), or inner regulation (Power Control). Primary Attribute: Charisma.

Power Theory.name: Power Theory
Power Theory.description: Understanding the mechanism: constructs with working parts, elements shaped by knowing how they behave, technology, probability, nullification, improvising a new use from a known principle. Covers: a construct that is actually a working tool, an element bent by its physics, a device run past its spec on purpose, working out why a power failed. Not: output (Power Force), reflex (Power Finesse), stamina (Power Endurance), inner regulation (Power Control), or persuasion (Power Presence). Primary Attribute: Intelligence.

Bulwark.name: Bulwark
Bulwark.description:
You do not move. Things break on you, and you are still there when they have finished.

Primary Attribute: Dexterity
Bulwark.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as a Bulwark: the immovable point of a fight, the one allies stand behind. NPCs test them once and go around.

Channeler.name: Channeler
Channeler.description:
Your power is not the weapon in your hand. Whatever your world calls it, you channel it under pressure and shape it exactly.

Primary Attribute: Wisdom
Channeler.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as a Channeler: a wielder of the world's own power source, whatever that is, kept steady under pressure and shaped precisely. NPCs treat them as the ranged threat and try to break their concentration.

Duelist.name: Duelist
Duelist.description:
Placement over power. You read a fight one exchange ahead and answer the opening before it closes.

Primary Attribute: Strength
Duelist.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as a Duelist: precise, patient, deadly in a single exchange. NPCs who know fighting recognise the stance; braggarts underestimate it once.

Reaver.name: Reaver
Reaver.description:
Pain is fuel. The worse the fight goes for you, the worse it goes for them.

Primary Attribute: Strength
Reaver.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as a Reaver: reckless, hungry, strongest when hurt. NPCs step back from the grin; allies learn to stay out of the arc.

Skirmisher.name: Skirmisher
Skirmisher.description: A mobile role built around speed, opportunistic attacks, escape routes, and adapting under pressure.
Skirmisher.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors mobility, initiative, repositioning, and flexible tactics. It does not grant automatic evasion or immunity to danger.

Strategist.name: Strategist
Strategist.description:
You see the fight as a board. Your allies hit where you point and the enemy finds the ground already taken.

Primary Attribute: Intelligence
Strategist.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as a Strategist: the one who reads the field and calls it. Allies act better under their voice; clever NPCs try to silence them first.

Vanguard.name: Vanguard
Vanguard.description:
You go first and you go through. Guard breaks where you hit, and the line behind you moves because you moved.

Primary Attribute: Strength
Vanguard.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as a Vanguard: the front of every advance, a breaker of Guard and of lines. NPCs read them as the one to stop first; allies form up behind them without being told.

Warden.name: Warden
Warden.description:
Nobody gets past you to them. You hold the ground and you choose who the enemy is allowed to fight.

Primary Attribute: Dexterity
Warden.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as a Warden: a protector who controls where the fight happens. NPCs learn quickly that attacking anyone else means answering to them.

Marksman.name: Marksman
Marksman.description:
Distance is your weapon. You pick the moment, the angle and the target, and what you aim at you hit.

Primary Attribute: Intelligence
Marksman.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as a Marksman: the ranged threat who chooses targets from where the fight cannot reach. NPCs seek cover from them first; allies drive enemies into their line.

Provocateur.name: Provocateur
Provocateur.description:
Every fight is a conversation and you are the one they cannot stop answering. The enemy fights you because you made it personal.

Primary Attribute: Charisma
Provocateur.traitNarrativeEffects: The player fights as a Provocateur: the loud one, the one every enemy wants to hit first. NPCs with any pride cannot leave them alone; allies work in the space that opens.

Agency Trainee.name: Agency Trainee
Agency Trainee.description: You have early exposure to supervised hero work, client expectations, field procedure, and professional rescue standards.
Agency Trainee.traitNarrativeEffects: Offer legitimate contracts, agency mentors, civilian-protection tests, paperwork, payment negotiation, and reputation consequences. Do not assume fame or a license.

Self-Taught Hero.name: Self-Taught Hero
Self-Taught Hero.description: You learned to use your power outside formal institutions and rely on improvisation, caution, and personal judgment.
Self-Taught Hero.traitNarrativeEffects: Peers may find your practical experience impressive, while teachers, agencies, employers, and authority figures may question your methods. Informal hero circles can welcome you more quickly than official ones.

Elemental Power.name: Elemental Power
Elemental Power.description: A power that creates, shapes, transforms or controls one natural element or force: fire, water, ice, stone, wind, lightning, or another the player names. Its strength is reach and versatility, a burst, a wall or a tool from the same element; its limits are material (nothing to shape means nothing to use), scale, and the Power Strain that forceful shaping costs.
Elemental Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask which element, what it needs to draw on, how far it reaches, what it looks like when it works, and what the character cannot yet do with it. In play the element is visible and attributable: witnesses know what they saw, damage leaves evidence, and Legal Heat follows collateral. Resolve shaping through Power Theory by default (the element obeys its physics); a blast thrown with the whole body is Power Force, a precise shaping is Power Finesse, holding a wall of it is Power Endurance. Forceful use costs Power Strain; a shaping with no material fails cleanly. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Mutation Power.name: Mutation Power
Mutation Power.description: A body-based power: the character's form, senses, movement or capabilities are changed by one defined mutation that is always theirs. Its strength is that it cannot be taken away and costs no setup; its limits are that it is one mutation, it shows, and pushing it past its design hurts.
Mutation Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the mutation is, how visible it is in everyday life, what it costs the body, and what ordinary life it complicates (clothes, doors, food, sleep, dating). It is always on: NPCs notice, some stare, some are afraid, and the character cannot switch it off to pass. Resolve it through Power Endurance by default (the body bears it); a mutation used for a strike is Power Force, for precision Power Finesse. It cannot become a different mutation; growth deepens the one they have. Overuse causes Power Strain as pain, bleeding or exhaustion. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Psychic Power.name: Psychic Power
Psychic Power.description: A mental, emotional, sensory or perception-based power with clear boundaries and consent-aware use: reading, nudging, projecting, sensing. Its strength is that walls and distance mean less to it; its limits are resistance, distraction, mental fatigue, and the ethics the world holds it to.
Psychic Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Prompt for range, targets, consent boundaries, mental cost, failure modes, and the backstory of discovery. Psychic use leaves no physical evidence, so exposure comes from behaviour, witnesses who felt something, and the character's own tells; the law treats unconsented influence as assault. Resolve psychic use through Power Control by default (steadiness is the power); a crushing push is Power Force, a presence that commands a room is Power Presence. Resistance is real: a strong will, training, distraction or another psychic blunts or breaks the effect, and overreach costs Power Strain as headaches, nosebleeds and dulled senses. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Construct Power.name: Construct Power
Construct Power.description: A power that creates temporary objects, creatures, barriers, tools or environments from a defined substance or principle. Its strength is having the right thing at the right moment; its limits are durability, complexity, duration, and the Power Strain of holding a construct together.
Construct Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the constructs are made of, how long they last, how complex they can be, and what they cannot be (no living creatures, no working machines, no weapons, unless the player's definition allows). Constructs are visible, attributable and leave residue or vanish by the definition. Resolve construction through Power Theory by default (a construct that works is a design); holding one up under attack is Power Endurance, placing one in time to catch a fall is Power Finesse. Complexity costs Power Strain; a construct asked to do what it was not made for fails. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Mobility Power.name: Mobility Power
Mobility Power.description: A power of movement: speed, teleportation, flight, phasing, or changing position in a way the body alone cannot. Its strength is being where the fight is not; its limits are range, destination safety, momentum, and repeated use.
Mobility Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask which kind of movement, its range, what it needs (sight of the destination, a run-up, open air), and what happens on a bad arrival. Movement is the most witnessed power there is: cameras, crowds and Pulse clips follow it, and arriving where you should not be is a crime before it is anything else. Resolve movement through Power Finesse by default (placement and timing); a body-slam arrival is Power Force, a long flight or chase is Power Endurance. Repeated bursts cost Power Strain and Energy; a blind arrival is a risk, never free. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Energy Power.name: Energy Power
Energy Power.description: A power that emits, absorbs, redirects or transforms one distinct kind of energy: heat, light, kinetic, electric, or another the player defines. Its strength is output; its limits are control, range, what the energy is drawn from, and the Power Strain of a full discharge.
Energy Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what kind of energy, where it comes from (the body, the air, stored charge), what it does to the user, and what a full discharge costs. Energy powers are loud and bright: bystanders see them, property pays for them, and a hero's reputation rides on where the discharge lands. Resolve discharges through Power Force by default (output is the power); a precise beam is Power Finesse, absorbing and holding energy is Power Endurance, a dialled-down release in a crowd is Power Control. A full-power discharge costs Power Strain and Energy; a spent character sparks and nothing more. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Custom Power.name: Custom Power
Custom Power.description: Define an original power without selecting a preset category. Describe its name, effects, activation, visual expression, strengths, limitations, risks, starting mastery, and desired ultimate technique, and pick the Power Attribute it runs on; a custom power starts broad (+1 in every power skill) instead of deep (three attribute points), and the Power Attribute pick decides which lane it leans into.
Custom Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Treat the player's custom power description as authoritative. In Backstory, ask how the power was discovered, how it shaped the player's life, what early incident revealed its limits, and what goal or fear is connected to mastering it; never invent the player's answers or decisions. A custom power has no default lane: the player's Power Attribute pick names the power skill it resolves through, and without one read the description for the attribute it is most like and say which. Its strengths, limits, costs and visibility are exactly what the player wrote, applied in every scene. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Technological Hero.name: Technological Hero
Technological Hero.description: Your power comes from technology: a suit, device, implant, exosuit or support system you can explain. Its strength is that it can be repaired, upgraded and lent; its limits are battery, heat, maintenance, compatibility, and damage.
Technological Hero.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the technology is, who built it, what powers it, what it cannot do yet, and what happens when it fails. It is equipment: it can be damaged, hacked, run flat, left at home or taken at a checkpoint, and Support Engineering keeps it working. Resolve the technology through Power Theory by default (it works because you understand it); a suit-driven blow is Power Force, a long deployment is Power Endurance, a fine manipulation is Power Finesse. Battery, heat and damage are tracked in the scene; a function the device was not built for is an improvisation with a real failure chance. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Supernatural.name: Supernatural
Supernatural.description: Your power originates from a supernatural condition, lineage, curse, pact, transformation or other force beyond ordinary human ability. Its strength is that it answers to its own rules, not physics; its limits are the origin's own weakness, cost and activation.
Supernatural.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the condition is, where it came from, how it activates, what it costs, what weakens it, and how openly it can be revealed. The supernatural is known to exist in this world but not understood: NPCs react with fear, curiosity, faith or contempt by their background, and the law has no clean category for it. Resolve manifestations through Power Control by default (the condition answers to steadiness); a condition that acts through the body is Power Endurance, one that acts through presence is Power Presence. The origin's weakness is always real and always available to an enemy who learns it. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Vampire.name: Vampire
Vampire.description: A supernatural condition: heightened senses, unnatural recovery, predatory instinct and blood-related abilities, sustained by blood or synthetic blood. Its strength is the body it gives; its limits are hunger, exposure, and whatever the player defines as the condition's weakness.
Vampire.traitNarrativeEffects: Vampiric powers require meaningful boundaries and costs. The character must sustain themselves with blood or synthetic blood; the player defines the condition's origin, feeding rules, weaknesses, risks, access to synthetic blood, and how openly it is revealed. Hunger is a clock: a fed vampire passes, a hungry one shows it, and feeding is a scene with consent, secrecy and consequences. Resolve vampiric capability through Power Endurance by default (the condition is the body); a predatory strike is Power Force, a hunter's reading of a room is Power Control, a presence that unsettles is Power Presence. The defined weakness always works. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Cursed Item.name: Cursed Item
Cursed Item.description: Your power comes from a cursed object with unusual benefits and a meaningful cost. Its strength is that the item does what it does regardless of your talent; its limits are the curse it exacts, what it cannot provide, and the danger of losing it.
Cursed Item.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the item is, where it came from, exactly what it gives, exactly what it takes, and who else wants it. The item is real inventory: it can be seen, stolen, confiscated, broken or bargained for, and the curse continues whether or not the power is used. Resolve the item's use through Power Endurance by default (the bearer carries the cost); invoking its authority over someone is Power Presence, working out its rules is Power Theory. The curse is paid in the scene, every time, as the player defined it; the item never provides an unagreed benefit. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Compassionate.name: Compassionate
Compassionate.description: You notice suffering quickly and instinctively look for ways to help.
Compassionate.traitNarrativeEffects: Compassion supports rescue and trust-building but can make ruthless choices harder.

Ambitious.name: Ambitious
Ambitious.description: You set demanding goals and push yourself to achieve them.
Ambitious.traitNarrativeEffects: Ambition supports training, competition, and leadership, but failure and comparison may create pressure.

Guarded.name: Guarded
Guarded.description: You reveal little until someone proves they are trustworthy.
Guarded.traitNarrativeEffects: Guarded behavior protects private information but slows intimacy and cooperation.

Bold.name: Bold
Bold.description: You act decisively when others hesitate.
Bold.traitNarrativeEffects: Boldness helps confrontations but can encourage risky choices.

Analytical.name: Analytical
Analytical.description: You break complicated situations into patterns, evidence, and workable steps.
Analytical.traitNarrativeEffects: Analysis helps planning but may seem distant in emotional moments.

Child of a Hero.name: Child of a Hero
Child of a Hero.description: A famous or respected hero parent shaped your expectations and public first impression.
Child of a Hero.traitNarrativeEffects: Recognition supports social access but scrutiny makes covert work harder.

Child of a Villain.name: Child of a Villain
Child of a Villain.description: Your family name is associated with wrongdoing, creating suspicion or unwanted attention.
Child of a Villain.traitNarrativeEffects: Family connections may provide information but public trust is harder to earn.

Delinquent.name: Delinquent
Delinquent.description: A rebellious past gave you hard-earned street experience and a reputation that may precede you.
Delinquent.traitNarrativeEffects: You handle pressure and informal circles well but may face distrust in formal settings.

Ordinary Civilian.name: Ordinary Civilian
Ordinary Civilian.description: You begin without a famous legacy, institutional backing, or specialized reputation.
Ordinary Civilian.traitNarrativeEffects: You avoid inherited scrutiny but lack specialized contacts.

Legacy Family.name: Legacy Family
Legacy Family.description: Your family is known for influence, achievement, wealth, or public tradition.
Legacy Family.traitNarrativeEffects: Connections provide access but expectations can complicate sincere relationships.

Runaway.name: Runaway
Runaway.description: You left a former home or institution and built a life with limited support.
Runaway.traitNarrativeEffects: Independence helps adaptation but housing, records, and trust may be difficult.

Academic Student.name: Academic Student
Academic Student.description: You have structured study experience and know how to navigate formal education.
Academic Student.traitNarrativeEffects: Study habits support research but may leave less practical experience.

Part-Time Worker.name: Part-Time Worker
Part-Time Worker.description: Regular work taught you punctuality, customer service, and practical responsibility.
Part-Time Worker.traitNarrativeEffects: Work experience helps with schedules and service jobs but leaves less time for investigation.

Trade Apprentice.name: Trade Apprentice
Trade Apprentice.description: Hands-on training gave you practical knowledge of tools, materials, and repairs.
Trade Apprentice.traitNarrativeEffects: Practical training supports field improvisation but may not transfer to formal research.

Streetwise Self-Taught.name: Streetwise Self-Taught
Streetwise Self-Taught.description: You learned outside institutions by observing people, improvising, and surviving mistakes.
Streetwise Self-Taught.traitNarrativeEffects: Street experience supports reading situations but can leave formal gaps.

Support Technology Student.name: Support Technology Student
Support Technology Student.description: You study equipment, systems, and practical technology used to support heroes.
Support Technology Student.traitNarrativeEffects: Technical training supports investigation and troubleshooting but may reduce field instincts.

Power Instability.name: Power Instability
Power Instability.description: Your power can surge, misfire, or become difficult to control under pressure.
Power Instability.traitNarrativeEffects: Stress and intense use increase failure risk, Power Strain, and collateral consequences until control improves.

Low Stamina.name: Low Stamina
Low Stamina.description: You tire faster than most people during prolonged exertion.
Low Stamina.traitNarrativeEffects: Long scenes, training, combat, and travel drain Energy more quickly and make recovery more important.

Social Anxiety.name: Social Anxiety
Social Anxiety.description: Crowds, scrutiny, and unfamiliar social situations can overwhelm your confidence.
Social Anxiety.traitNarrativeEffects: Public speaking, introductions, dates, and high-pressure social scenes require extra care and may increase Energy drain.

Public Reputation.name: Public Reputation
Public Reputation.description: A visible past, rumor, or family connection makes strangers form opinions before meeting you.
Public Reputation.traitNarrativeEffects: Public reactions vary more sharply: reputation can open doors or create scrutiny depending on the situation.

Resource Dependence.name: Resource Dependence
Resource Dependence.description: Your effectiveness depends on a limited resource, supply, device, condition, or routine.
Resource Dependence.traitNarrativeEffects: When the required resource is unavailable, related abilities weaken or become impossible until the player addresses the shortage.

Optimistic.name: Optimistic
Optimistic.description: You look for hope and possible solutions even when circumstances are grim.
Optimistic.traitNarrativeEffects: Hope supports morale, but optimism can underestimate danger.

Cautious.name: Cautious
Cautious.traitNarrativeEffects: Caution improves preparation but can cost time and initiative.

Curious.name: Curious
Curious.description: You are drawn to mysteries and unanswered questions.
Curious.traitNarrativeEffects: Curiosity helps investigation but can lead toward danger.

Loyal.name: Loyal
Loyal.description: You stand by people who have earned your trust.
Loyal.traitNarrativeEffects: Loyalty strengthens teamwork but makes betrayal painful.

Independent.name: Independent
Independent.description: You prefer solving problems through your own judgment.
Independent.traitNarrativeEffects: Independence supports self-reliance but can make accepting help difficult.

Playful.name: Playful
Playful.description: You use humor and lightness to navigate daily life.
Playful.traitNarrativeEffects: Playfulness eases tension but may be poorly timed.

Disciplined.name: Disciplined
Disciplined.description: You rely on routines, practice, and deliberate follow-through.
Disciplined.traitNarrativeEffects: Discipline supports training but can become rigid.

Former Sidekick.name: Former Sidekick
Former Sidekick.description: You previously supported a hero or team.
Former Sidekick.traitNarrativeEffects: Field experience supports teamwork but former colleagues may complicate your life.

Underground Contact.name: Underground Contact
Underground Contact.description: You grew up around unofficial networks outside ordinary institutions.
Underground Contact.traitNarrativeEffects: Hidden routes and contacts help investigation but official trust is harder to establish.

Refugee.name: Refugee
Refugee.description: You rebuilt your life after leaving danger or upheaval.
Refugee.traitNarrativeEffects: Adaptability helps survival but records and belonging may take time to rebuild.

Foster Youth.name: Foster Youth
Foster Youth.description: You adapted across changing homes, adults, and expectations.
Foster Youth.traitNarrativeEffects: Adaptation helps social reading but asking for support can be difficult.

Celebrity Child.name: Celebrity Child
Celebrity Child.description: A famous family member makes you recognizable before people know you.
Celebrity Child.traitNarrativeEffects: Recognition provides access but public scrutiny makes privacy difficult.

Reformed Trouble-Maker.name: Reformed Trouble-Maker
Reformed Trouble-Maker.description: You are trying to leave behind a record of bad decisions.
Reformed Trouble-Maker.traitNarrativeEffects: A second chance can build trust, but others may watch for relapse.

Athlete.name: Athlete
Athlete.description: Sports training taught you conditioning, teamwork, and competitive focus.
Athlete.traitNarrativeEffects: Athletic experience supports physical challenges but creates injury and research pressures.

Artist.name: Artist
Artist.description: Creative practice taught you observation, expression, and patience.
Artist.traitNarrativeEffects: Artistic practice supports performance and perception but may not prepare you for physical strain.

Medical Trainee.name: Medical Trainee
Medical Trainee.description: You have introductory training in care and emergency response.
Medical Trainee.traitNarrativeEffects: Medical knowledge supports crisis response but does not replace professional treatment.

Mechanic.name: Mechanic
Mechanic.description: You have hands-on experience repairing machines and equipment.
Mechanic.traitNarrativeEffects: Mechanical experience helps maintain gear but may not transfer to social pressure.

Performer.name: Performer
Performer.description: Performance taught you presence, timing, and audience awareness.
Performer.traitNarrativeEffects: Performance helps hold attention but makes mistakes visible.

Research Assistant.name: Research Assistant
Research Assistant.description: You organize evidence, sources, experiments, or records.
Research Assistant.traitNarrativeEffects: Research helps investigation but requires time and reliable information.

Food Service Worker.name: Food Service Worker
Food Service Worker.description: Restaurant work taught you speed, service, and multitasking.
Food Service Worker.traitNarrativeEffects: Service experience helps in busy environments but leaves limited free time.

Short Temper.name: Short Temper
Short Temper.description: Frustration can push you toward heated reactions.
Short Temper.traitNarrativeEffects: Provocation makes restraint and negotiation harder.

Trust Issues.name: Trust Issues
Trust Issues.description: Past experiences make relying on unfamiliar people difficult.
Trust Issues.traitNarrativeEffects: Trust develops slowly and requires proof or consistency.

Perfectionism.name: Perfectionism
Perfectionism.description: You hold yourself to difficult standards.
Perfectionism.traitNarrativeEffects: Mistakes consume extra attention and Energy.

Fear of Failure.name: Fear of Failure
Fear of Failure.description: Disappointing others makes important choices feel dangerous.
Fear of Failure.traitNarrativeEffects: High-stakes tests and scrutiny increase pressure.

Chronic Pain.name: Chronic Pain
Chronic Pain.description: A persistent condition makes exertion and recovery unpredictable.
Chronic Pain.traitNarrativeEffects: Strenuous activity drains Energy faster and may require pacing or care.

Sensory Overload.name: Sensory Overload
Sensory Overload.description: Crowds, noise, light, or intense stimuli can overwhelm your focus.
Sensory Overload.traitNarrativeEffects: Busy scenes and intense power effects may drain Energy.

Protective Instinct.name: Protective Instinct
Protective Instinct.description: Threats to people you care about can override caution.
Protective Instinct.traitNarrativeEffects: Protection supports rescue but can cause reckless choices or extra strain.

Stubborn.name: Stubborn
Stubborn.description: You resist changing course even when advice suggests you should.
Stubborn.traitNarrativeEffects: Stubbornness supports endurance but makes compromise difficult.

Magical Power.name: Magical Power
Magical Power.description: A power drawn from spells, rituals, mystical study, contracts, inherited sorcery, spirits or curses. Its strength is breadth, with preparation; its limits are components, preparation, concentration, bargains, and carefully defined rules.
Magical Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what tradition the magic belongs to, what a working needs (words, components, time, a bargain), what it cannot do, and who taught it. Magic is slow where powers are fast: a prepared caster is formidable and an ambushed one has only cantrips. Resolve magic through Power Theory by default (a spell is a known procedure); a ritual held against interruption is Power Control, a curse borne is Power Endurance, an invocation that commands is Power Presence. Major magic without its requirements fails or misfires; a misfire is a scene. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Orphan.name: Orphan
Orphan.description: You grew up without one or both parents as an active part of your life.
Orphan.traitNarrativeEffects: Independence can help survival but family and trust topics may be difficult.

Cold.name: Cold
Cold.description: You keep emotional distance and reveal little of what you feel.
Cold.traitNarrativeEffects: Emotional reserve can support composure and intimidation, but may make empathy, reassurance, intimacy, and trust harder. Do not assume the character lacks emotion, empathy, or the ability to form bonds.

Sadistic.name: Sadistic
Sadistic.description: You may take pleasure in control, humiliation, fear, or another person's discomfort.
Sadistic.traitNarrativeEffects: This can aid intimidation but complicate trust and compassionate negotiation. It does not force violence or abuse; the player chooses how to manage it.

Emotional Detachment.name: Emotional Detachment
Emotional Detachment.description: You have difficulty recognizing, expressing, or tolerating emotional closeness.
Emotional Detachment.traitNarrativeEffects: This complicates intimacy and asking for help but does not make you emotionless.

Cruel Impulses.name: Cruel Impulses
Cruel Impulses.description: Under pressure, you may feel urges toward harsh, humiliating, or punitive responses.
Cruel Impulses.traitNarrativeEffects: This creates temptation, not forced behavior. Harmful choices have consequences.

Remorse Avoidance.name: Remorse Avoidance
Remorse Avoidance.description: You deflect, rationalize, or avoid confronting guilt after causing harm.
Remorse Avoidance.traitNarrativeEffects: This may delay repair and accountability without erasing responsibility.

Institutional Distrust.name: Institutional Distrust
Institutional Distrust.description: You are wary of authorities, official promises, and protective systems.
Institutional Distrust.traitNarrativeEffects: You prefer independent verification, which can help scrutiny but create official friction.

Psychotic.name: Psychotic
Psychotic.description: You experience altered perceptions, unusual beliefs, or difficulty distinguishing reality during episodes of severe stress or illness.
Psychotic.traitNarrativeEffects: This fictional characterization may complicate investigation and social certainty while encouraging unusual perspectives. Do not equate it with violence, and do not invent symptoms for the player.

Sociopath.name: Sociopath
Sociopath.description: You may display learned antisocial behavior, distrust of institutions, reactive aggression, rule-breaking, or selective loyalty shaped by experience.
Sociopath.traitNarrativeEffects: You may read power dynamics well, but ordinary trust can be difficult. This does not force violence or criminality.

Psychopathic Traits (Removed).name: Psychopathic Traits (Removed)
Psychopathic Traits (Removed).description: You show some combination of shallow affect, calculated behavior, low remorse, sensation-seeking, or instrumental relationships.
Psychopathic Traits (Removed).traitNarrativeEffects: This is a fictional behavioral characterization, not a diagnosis. It may affect risk assessment, attachment, manipulation, guilt, and responses to harm, but does not guarantee violence or remove agency. Do not assume the character is emotionless, incapable of loyalty, or destined to become a criminal. Show choices, learned behavior, personal values, and consequences.

Sociopathic Traits (Removed).name: Sociopathic Traits (Removed)
Sociopathic Traits (Removed).description: You may display learned antisocial behavior, distrust of institutions, reactive aggression, rule-breaking, or selective loyalty shaped by experience.
Sociopathic Traits (Removed).traitNarrativeEffects: This is a fictional behavioral characterization, not a diagnosis. It does not automatically mean violent, evil, or incapable of empathy. Let the player define the character's history, relationships, values, self-control, and capacity for change. Treat harmful actions as choices with social, legal, emotional, and relationship consequences.

Gravity Power.name: Gravity Power
Gravity Power.description: You manipulate weight, pull or directional gravity within defined limits: lightening, weighting, dropping, drifting. Its strength is that mass obeys you; its limits are area, duration, and the strain of moving more than you could carry.
Gravity Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask how large an area, how much mass, how long, and whether the user is inside their own field. Gravity work is visible in its effects (things fall wrong, people stumble, debris drifts) and dangerous to bystanders by default. Resolve gravity through Power Force by default (weight is force); a weightless zone held in place is Power Endurance, a lightened step placed exactly is Power Finesse, a field shaped to spare the people in it is Power Control. Moving more than the user could lift costs Power Strain in proportion; a dropped field drops everything in it. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Shadow Power.name: Shadow Power
Shadow Power.description: You shape, conceal yourself within, or move through shadows under defined limits. Its strength is being unseen and elsewhere; its limits are light, scale, and that a shadow is not a wall.
Shadow Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask whether the character hides in shadow, moves through it, shapes it, or all three; how much light breaks it; and what the shadow cannot do. Light is the counter: a lit room, a flare, a flashlight held steady, and the power is ordinary darkness. Resolve shadow use through Power Finesse by default (concealment is placement and timing); a shadow made solid to strike is Power Force, a darkness held over a room is Power Endurance, a terror in the dark is Power Presence. Being unseen is not being undetectable: sound, heat, cameras and dogs still work. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Sound Power.name: Sound Power
Sound Power.description: You create, shape, suppress or sense sound and vibration. Its strength is that it fills a space and passes walls; its limits are volume, your own ears, and that it cannot shatter what it cannot reach.
Sound Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask whether the character makes sound, shapes it, silences it, or hears through it; what their own ears can take; and what the loudest thing they have done was. Sound is public: everyone in range is affected, allies included unless the player defines a way to spare them, and a shout in a city is a report to the police. Resolve sound through Power Presence by default (a sound acts on everyone who hears it); a focused shockwave is Power Force, listening through a wall is Power Control, a note placed exactly is Power Finesse. Overuse costs Power Strain as ringing, bleeding ears and temporary deafness. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Time Power.name: Time Power
Time Power.description: You alter personal speed, delay brief events, or affect limited temporal windows. Its strength is the moment nobody else has; its limits are duration, scope, and the strain of borrowing time.
Time Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the character can do with time (speed themselves, slow a space, hold a moment), how long a window lasts, who or what it affects, and what borrowing time costs them afterward. Time powers are hard to witness and easy to doubt; they do not undo what has happened. Resolve temporal use through Power Finesse by default (a moment used exactly); holding a window open is Power Endurance, reading what a window will do is Power Theory, keeping it from slipping is Power Control. Every borrowed second is paid back as Power Strain and Energy; a window held too long collapses on the user. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Probability Power.name: Probability Power
Probability Power.description: You influence the likelihood of possible outcomes without guaranteeing success. Its strength is that it works where nothing else can be aimed; its limits are that it nudges, never decides, and the debt of improbability comes due.
Probability Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what kind of outcomes the character can lean on, how strongly, and what the world does to balance the books. A nudge shifts a step of success, never a certainty; important outcomes resist, and a run of luck is followed by its bill (a coincidence that costs, a delayed misfortune, an engine that drifts). Resolve probability through Power Theory by default (knowing which outcome to lean on); a blind push of luck is Power Presence, riding a long streak is Power Endurance. Nobody can prove a probability power was used, which is its own kind of exposure problem. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Barrier Power.name: Barrier Power
Barrier Power.description: You create protective, blocking or containing fields. Its strength is that others live because of it; its limits are size, duration, what passes through, and that a barrier held is a barrier paid for.
Barrier Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the barrier is made of, how big, how long, what passes through it (air, sound, allies, the user), and what happens when it breaks. Barriers are the rescue power: civilians, crowds and teammates look to them first, and a barrier that fails under people is the worst thing that can happen to this character. Resolve barriers through Power Endurance by default (a field lasts as long as you do); a barrier thrown to cover an ally in time is Power Finesse, one shaped to stop a specific power is Power Theory. Every hit a barrier takes costs the user Power Strain; a broken barrier stuns them. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Portal Power.name: Portal Power
Portal Power.description: You create linked openings between locations or points within strict limits. Its strength is that distance stops mattering; its limits are range, size, line of sight or knowledge of the far side, and what may not pass.
Portal Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask how far a portal reaches, how large, whether the character needs to see or know the far side, how long it stays open, and what it refuses to carry. A portal is a door: things come through it both ways, it can be seen, and opening one into a place you have no right to be is burglary. Resolve portals through Power Finesse by default (a gate placed exactly); holding one open under load is Power Endurance, calculating an unseen destination is Power Theory. A portal closing on something is a scene; a bad destination is a consequence, never a free escape. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Illusion Power.name: Illusion Power
Illusion Power.description: You alter one or more senses without changing physical reality. Its strength is that a convinced enemy acts on what is not there; its limits are that illusions do no harm themselves, break on contact, and fail against a mind that knows.
Illusion Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask which senses, how many targets, how large and detailed an illusion can be, and what breaks it. An illusion is a performance: it convinces or it does not, and a target who touches it, is told, or has reason to doubt sees through. Resolve illusions through Power Presence by default (an illusion is a performance); a sustained scene is Power Endurance, one aimed at a single sense exactly is Power Finesse, one built on a correct read of what the target expects is Power Theory. Illusions never cause damage directly; using one to make someone hurt themselves is the user's act. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Nullification Power.name: Nullification Power
Nullification Power.description: You suppress or disrupt powers under strict contact, range, duration and resistance limits. Its strength is that it answers any power; its limits are reach, resistance, and that it stops nothing ordinary.
Nullification Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask whether nullification needs touch, how long it lasts, how it feels to the target, and what it does to the user's own power if they have one. Nullifiers are feared and wanted: agencies, police and villains all have a use for them, and powered NPCs react to their presence. Resolve nullification through Power Control by default (feeling a power to still it); understanding an unfamiliar power before suppressing it is Power Theory, holding a suppression is Power Endurance. A stronger or stranger power resists; nullification does nothing to a gun, a fist or a fall. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Healing Power.name: Healing Power
Healing Power.description: You restore, stabilize or accelerate biological recovery within defined limits. Its strength is that it undoes harm; its limits are that it cannot restore what is gone, reverse death, or heal faster than the body can bear.
Healing Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the healing needs (touch, time, the user's own vitality), what it cannot fix, and what it costs the healer. A healer is never off duty: every injury in a scene is a request, hospitals and agencies want them, and the one thing they cannot heal will arrive. Resolve healing through Power Control by default (knowing where to stop); a long triage is Power Endurance, a steadying word that keeps a patient alive is Power Presence, understanding an unfamiliar injury is Power Theory. Healing is paid in Power Strain and Energy; serious injuries, death and lasting conditions stay beyond it. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Demonic Contract.name: Demonic Contract
Demonic Contract.description: Your power comes from a negotiated pact with a demon or infernal entity: defined benefits, defined terms, a price. Its strength is what the other party can do; its limits are the terms, the price, and the other party's own interests.
Demonic Contract.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask who the other party is, what the contract grants, what it costs and when it is collected, what the sign of it is, and whether the other party can be spoken to. The contract is a relationship with an NPC who has interests; it is exact, it never gives an unagreed benefit, and the price is paid in scenes. Resolve contract powers through Power Presence by default (an invocation is authority exercised); bearing the pact's price is Power Endurance, reading its small print is Power Theory. Faith, consecrated places and people who know the signs react; so does the entity when the user overreaches. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Powers Only.name: Powers Only
Powers Only.description: Rely primarily on established powers rather than mundane weapons or unarmed combat. Every exchange starts from the power; fists and tools are what is left when the power is spent, and the fighter knows their meters better than anyone.
Powers Only.traitNarrativeEffects: Power use follows the character's authored abilities, limits, resources, cooldowns and Power Strain; do not invent weapons or combat training. Narrate this fighter as opening every exchange with the power and reading the fight through it: range, Energy, Power Strain and cooldowns are their real position. Resolve their power actions through the lane the action uses (Power Routing); their Power Attribute pick is the tie-break. When the power is spent they are ordinary and exposed, and a good opponent waits for exactly that. Full Commitment is theirs alone: once an encounter, one expression a band harder at the cost of extra Power Strain.

Power and Hand-to-Hand.name: Power and Hand-to-Hand
Power and Hand-to-Hand.description: Combine established powers with punches, kicks, grappling, movement and close-range tactics. The power rides the body: a strike carries its effect, a grapple holds with it, and closing the distance is the plan.
Power and Hand-to-Hand.traitNarrativeEffects: Mundane close combat does not cause Power Strain by itself; applying a power to an attack follows its authored costs, limits, resources and cooldowns. Narrate this fighter closing, clinching and striking with the power woven into the contact; resolve the physical half through Close Quarters Combat and the power half through its lane (Power Routing). They are at their best inside arm's reach and at a disadvantage against anything that keeps them out. Charged Strike is theirs: a close blow that delivers the power's effect on contact.

Hand-to-Hand.name: Hand-to-Hand
Hand-to-Hand.description: Rely primarily on unarmed fighting: punches, kicks, grappling, takedowns and restraint. No power, no weapon, nothing to confiscate; the fighter is always armed and always nonlethal by default.
Hand-to-Hand.traitNarrativeEffects: Use Close Quarters Combat for meaningful uncertainty; do not assume formal training, guaranteed hits, or immunity to weapons. Narrate this fighter controlling distance, grip and the ground: restraint, takedown and escape are their answers, and their fights end in holds and unconsciousness, not blood, unless they choose otherwise. They cannot be disarmed and are never caught without their weapon; against reach, armour or a power that keeps them off, they need an opening. Takedown Chain is theirs: a sequence that takes a standing opponent to the ground and holds them.

Blades.name: Blades
Blades.description: Rely primarily on edged weapons: knives, swords or other established blades. The blade is quick, quiet and serious; every cut is a decision about how much harm this fight deserves.
Blades.traitNarrativeEffects: Require a specific established blade, training, Weapon Proficiency, and attention to injury, legality, concealment and escalation. Narrate this fighter working angles, tempo and the opponent's hands; a blade turns a nonlethal intent into careful work and a lethal one into a short fight, and the law and witnesses read a drawn blade as escalation. Precision Cut is theirs: one cut placed to disable (a weapon hand, a strap, a cable, a tendon) rather than to wound broadly.

Blunt Weapons.name: Blunt Weapons
Blunt Weapons.description: Rely primarily on clubs, batons, hammers, staffs or other established impact weapons. Reach, leverage and mass; the fighter stops people and breaks things without needing to cut anyone.
Blunt Weapons.traitNarrativeEffects: Require a specific established weapon, training, Weapon Proficiency, and attention to injury, reach, legality and escalation. Narrate this fighter using reach and leverage: parries, sweeps, strikes that stagger, and the option to end a fight without a wound that bleeds. Against speed in close they need their footwork. Staggering Blow is theirs: one hit that leaves the target staggered and open for the next exchange.

Smoker.name: Smoker
Smoker.description: A habitual tobacco user who gains familiar short-term stress relief from cigarettes but carries ongoing health and resource costs.
Smoker.traitNarrativeEffects: Cigarettes may provide slightly more reliable short-term Stress relief for this character, but smoking costs money, uses one cigarette from a pack, creates odor and social consequences, can reduce stamina, worsen coughs and colds, impair long-term health, and create habit pressure. Never force smoking, withdrawal, dependence, or use of cigarettes without player choice.

Fast Healer.name: Fast Healer
Fast Healer.description: A character whose body recovers from ordinary fatigue and minor injuries faster than usual.
Fast Healer.traitNarrativeEffects: Recovery from minor injuries, soreness, and ordinary illness may be faster, but this does not prevent injury, restore full health instantly, reverse death, erase lasting damage, or bypass hospitalization. Severe injuries and supernatural conditions still require appropriate care.

Iron Constitution.name: Iron Constitution
Iron Constitution.description: A robust constitution that resists ordinary illness, fatigue, and environmental discomfort better than most people.
Iron Constitution.traitNarrativeEffects: The character gains resilience against common colds, minor sickness, and fatigue, but can still become ill, exhausted, injured, or affected by serious disease, toxins, powers, and supernatural conditions.

Poor Sleep.name: Poor Sleep
Poor Sleep.description: A recurring difficulty getting restful sleep, including possible trouble falling asleep, waking during the night, or being unable to return to sleep.
Poor Sleep.traitNarrativeEffects: Poor sleep can reduce Energy, increase Stress, impair concentration, slow recovery, and sometimes interrupt or shorten a rest period. Sleep disruption should remain contextual and player-directed, not a forced condition in every scene. Establish routines, safe environments, support, treatment, accommodations, or coping strategies when relevant; these can make recovery habits meaningful without guaranteeing perfect sleep.

Chronic Condition.name: Chronic Condition
Chronic Condition.description: A player-defined ongoing health condition that requires accommodations, management, treatment, or periodic care.
Chronic Condition.traitNarrativeEffects: The player defines the condition, symptoms, triggers, treatment, limits, privacy, and accommodations. Do not invent a diagnosis, symptoms, disability, medication, or medical history. Benefits may include planning, support access, self-knowledge, or resilience developed through management; costs may include appointments, fatigue, expenses, restrictions, or flare-ups.

High Metabolism.name: High Metabolism
High Metabolism.description: A body that burns energy quickly, requiring more frequent meals and creating both useful recovery and practical costs.
High Metabolism.traitNarrativeEffects: Food can restore Energy somewhat efficiently, but hunger arrives sooner, meal costs increase, and missed meals can cause fatigue, irritability, or concentration problems.

Sensitive Lungs.name: Sensitive Lungs
Sensitive Lungs.description: A vulnerability to smoke, pollution, respiratory illness, and strenuous exertion.
Sensitive Lungs.traitNarrativeEffects: Smoke, poor air, colds, and intense exertion can reduce Energy or worsen symptoms, while clean air, rest, and medical care help. Do not invent a diagnosis or force symptoms without context.

Adrenaline Seeker.name: Adrenaline Seeker
Adrenaline Seeker.description: A strong attraction to high-intensity activity that can improve performance under pressure but makes calm recovery difficult.
Adrenaline Seeker.traitNarrativeEffects: During danger, competition, or urgent action the character may resist hesitation or fatigue briefly, but reckless choices, poor rest, injury risk, and difficulty settling down can create consequences. Never override player decisions.

Slow Healer.name: Slow Healer
Slow Healer.description: A character whose body heals more slowly than normal but ultimately recovers more completely from ordinary injuries and illness.
Slow Healer.traitNarrativeEffects: Recovery begins slowly and may require more rest, treatment, rehabilitation, and missed obligations than usual, but the character can recover more thoroughly over time from minor and moderate injuries or ordinary illness. This does not prevent injury, reverse death, erase lasting damage automatically, or bypass appropriate medical care.

No Power.name: No Power
No Power.description: You have no supernatural power and rely on training, equipment, planning and ordinary skills. Its strength is that nothing about you can be nullified, drained or exposed, and every skill you own is one you earned; its limits are reach and scale against powered opponents, which preparation, allies, terrain and gear have to make up.
No Power.traitNarrativeEffects: Present non-powered solutions, practical preparation, equipment, social tactics and environmental advantages without treating the character as helpless; a trained, prepared human beats an unprepared power often enough to matter. Do not invent supernatural abilities for them, ever. Their checks run through Close Quarters Combat, Weapon Proficiency, Strike Tactics and the ordinary skills, never a power skill. The world reads them as either an underdog or a professional, by conduct. Ask what they trained in, what they carry, and why they do this without a power. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Power and Weapons.name: Power and Weapons
Power and Weapons.description: Combine established powers with trained weapon use, tactical positioning and practical combat judgment. The weapon is the conduit: the power travels down the blade, the barrel or the haft, and the fighter picks the ground.
Power and Weapons.traitNarrativeEffects: Using a weapon requires an established weapon category, access, training, and attention to legality, injury, concealment and escalation; applying a power to a weapon follows its authored costs, limits, resources and cooldowns. Narrate this fighter choosing position first and striking with the weapon and the power as one; resolve the weapon through Weapon Proficiency and the power through its lane (Power Routing). Disarmed, they fall back to the power alone. Conduit Strike is theirs: one weapon attack that carries the power's effect to the target.

Ranged Weapons.name: Ranged Weapons
Ranged Weapons.description: Rely primarily on ranged weapons: bows, guns, firearms, thrown weapons and other established projectile equipment. Distance is the fighter's armour and the shot is a decision made before the target knows it.
Ranged Weapons.traitNarrativeEffects: Require a specific established ranged weapon, appropriate ammunition or recoverable projectiles, training, Weapon Proficiency, lawful access or consequences where applicable, and attention to collateral risk; this style covers bows, guns, firearms, thrown weapons and similar equipment without granting access to any particular weapon. Narrate this fighter choosing lines of fire, cover and the moment; ammunition, reloads and bystanders are real. Caught at arm's length they are in the wrong fight. Called Shot is theirs: one aimed shot at a declared target point (a hand, a weapon, a strap, a leg) that resolves as that choice.

Hero Operations.name: Hero Operations
Hero Operations.description: You studied coordinated hero deployment, rescue logistics, and field leadership.
Hero Operations.traitNarrativeEffects: Agency obligations, formal reporting, and public accountability follow you into early work.

Combat Academy.name: Combat Academy
Combat Academy.description: You focused on practical combat training and controlled engagements.
Combat Academy.traitNarrativeEffects: Your direct approach brings higher collateral scrutiny and pressure to solve conflicts visibly.

Power Research.name: Power Research
Power Research.description: You studied power theory, testing, limits, and controlled application.
Power Research.traitNarrativeEffects: You begin with less field experience and must adapt when situations become chaotic.

Support Engineering.name: Support Engineering
Support Engineering.description: You trained in support equipment, maintenance, and practical hero technology.
Support Engineering.traitNarrativeEffects: You depend more heavily on functioning equipment, replacement parts, and repair access.

Medical and Rescue.name: Medical and Rescue
Medical and Rescue.description: You focused on stabilization, emergency care, and extracting people from danger.
Medical and Rescue.traitNarrativeEffects: Teams expect you to prioritize stabilization and civilian safety before pursuing threats.

Investigation and Law.name: Investigation and Law
Investigation and Law.description: You studied evidence, procedure, criminal investigation, and hero law.
Investigation and Law.traitNarrativeEffects: Mandatory reporting, evidence rules, and procedural limits shape your available choices.

Media and Public Relations.name: Media and Public Relations
Media and Public Relations.description: You trained in public communication, interviews, reputation, and crisis messaging.
Media and Public Relations.traitNarrativeEffects: Image management, interviews, and agency publicity obligations compete with field work.

Independent Hero Studies.name: Independent Hero Studies
Independent Hero Studies.description: You built a self-directed education around the skills most relevant to your own hero identity.
Independent Hero Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: You have less institutional support and a weaker professional network at the start.

Emergency Management.name: Emergency Management
Emergency Management.description: You studied large-scale crisis coordination, evacuation, and disaster logistics.
Emergency Management.traitNarrativeEffects: You are expected to prioritize civilians, evacuation, and stabilizing the scene over pursuit.

Hero Ethics and Mediation.name: Hero Ethics and Mediation
Hero Ethics and Mediation.description: You studied de-escalation, negotiation, hero ethics, and conflict resolution.
Hero Ethics and Mediation.traitNarrativeEffects: Supervisors and civilians expect you to attempt negotiation before using force when practical.

Forensics and Crime Analysis.name: Forensics and Crime Analysis
Forensics and Crime Analysis.description: You studied crime scenes, evidence patterns, and investigative reconstruction.
Forensics and Crime Analysis.traitNarrativeEffects: Field response can slow while you secure evidence and preserve chain of custody.

Agency Management.name: Agency Management
Agency Management.description: You studied leadership, scheduling, administration, and the systems behind hero agencies.
Agency Management.traitNarrativeEffects: Paperwork, scheduling duties, and responsibility for team failures follow you into the field.

Community Hero Studies.name: Community Hero Studies
Community Hero Studies.description: You studied neighborhood trust, outreach, and long-term public safety relationships.
Community Hero Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: Local visibility and ongoing neighborhood obligations make it harder to disappear after a case.

Covert Operations.name: Covert Operations
Covert Operations.description: You studied infiltration, concealment, intelligence gathering, and discreet intervention.
Covert Operations.traitNarrativeEffects: Oversight and secrecy requirements limit what you can reveal, while covert work receives limited public recognition.

International Hero Studies.name: International Hero Studies
International Hero Studies.description: You studied cross-border hero work, cultures, languages, and jurisdictional differences.
International Hero Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: Travel demands, jurisdiction issues, and unfamiliar legal systems complicate assignments outside your home area.

Hero Technology and Communications.name: Hero Technology and Communications
Hero Technology and Communications.description: You studied agency networks, field communications, and technical coordination.
Hero Technology and Communications.traitNarrativeEffects: You rely more heavily on functioning networks, devices, and agency support.

Adaptive Field Studies.name: Adaptive Field Studies
Adaptive Field Studies.description: You pursued a broad practical education instead of specializing in one hero discipline.
Adaptive Field Studies.traitNarrativeEffects: You have no deep specialization and may face inconsistent expectations from institutions and teammates.

Alien.name: Alien
Alien.description: Your power originates from extraterrestrial biology, technology, lineage, training or a connection to a civilization beyond Earth. Its strength is that it was never meant for human limits; its limits are what Earth lacks that it needs, and the attention it draws.
Alien.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the connection is (biology, device, lineage, training), what it needs that Earth may not provide, what gives the character away, and who on Earth already knows. Alien origin draws government, media and faction attention the moment it is suspected. Resolve alien power through Power Force by default (a body or core built for more); a precise application is Power Finesse, an alien device understood is Power Theory, holding a transformation is Power Endurance. Earth's conditions set the limits: what the power needs and cannot get here is the ongoing cost. Preserve agency: never force a form, a use, a victim, a morality or a loss of control; the player defines the power and decides its use.

Flunked Out.name: Flunked Out
Flunked Out.description: You entered higher education but failed to complete the program, leaving with unfinished training, damaged confidence, or unresolved obligations. You may still use what you learned, return to study, pursue work outside the field, or build a new path without being defined by the failure.
Flunked Out.traitNarrativeEffects: This character may face incomplete credentials, lost opportunities, academic debts, strained faculty relationships, or gaps in formal training. Their unfinished education can also provide practical knowledge, contacts, self-taught skills, and a reason to prove themselves. Do not assume the cause, shame, finances, disability, discrimination, burnout, misconduct, or personal history behind leaving; establish it through player choice or authored backstory. Flunking out does not determine intelligence, morality, competence, or future success.

Bruiser.name: Bruiser
Bruiser.description: A close-range role built around force, endurance, and staying in the fight.
Bruiser.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors direct pressure, physical resilience, and close-quarters problem-solving. This is a starting emphasis, not a requirement to be violent or to use only blunt weapons.

Ranged Specialist.name: Ranged Specialist
Ranged Specialist.description: A precision role built around distance, timing, mobility, and accurate equipment use.
Ranged Specialist.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors positioning, precision, and projectile or ranged-power decisions. Ammunition, collateral risk, line of sight, and lawful access remain meaningful.

Support Specialist.name: Support Specialist
Support Specialist.description: A team-oriented role built around protection, recovery, coordination, and practical problem-solving.
Support Specialist.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors keeping people safe, enabling allies, treating injuries, managing equipment, and finding nonviolent solutions. Support does not require self-sacrifice or obedience.

Defender.name: Defender
Defender.description: A protective role built around resilience, positioning, shielding, and controlling danger near allies.
Defender.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors absorbing pressure, protecting civilians, and creating safe openings. Defense does not require the character to accept harm without limits.

Controller.name: Controller
Controller.description: A tactical role built around battlefield shaping, timing, disruption, and managing risks.
Controller.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors analysis, awareness, planning, and effects that limit danger or create opportunities. It does not guarantee that powers work or that opponents surrender control.

Investigator.name: Investigator
Investigator.description: A problem-solving role built around observation, evidence, deduction, and careful questioning.
Investigator.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors noticing inconsistencies, preserving evidence, interviewing, research, and patient reasoning. It does not guarantee correct conclusions or access to restricted information.

Support Class.name: Support Class
Support Class.description: A wisdom-focused class built around protection, recovery, coordination, and practical care.
Support Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors keeping people safe, enabling allies, treating injuries, managing risk, and finding nonviolent solutions. Support does not require self-sacrifice or obedience.

Strike Class.name: Strike Class
Strike Class.description: A dexterity-focused class built around precision, timing, and decisive attacks.
Strike Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors accurate attacks, quick reactions, and exploiting openings at close or long range. It does not require violence when restraint is safer.

Vanguard Class.name: Vanguard Class
Vanguard Class.description: A constitution-focused class built around endurance, initiative, and remaining effective under pressure.
Vanguard Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors stamina, sustained action, frontline reliability, and entering uncertain situations prepared to endure consequences. It does not grant immunity to injury.

Defense Class.name: Defense Class
Defense Class.description: A constitution-focused class built around resilience, shielding, positioning, and protecting others.
Defense Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors absorbing pressure, protecting civilians, and creating safe openings. Defense does not require accepting harm without limits.

Control Class.name: Control Class
Control Class.description: An intelligence-focused class built around tactics, battlefield shaping, timing, and disruption.
Control Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors analysis, planning, systems, and effects that limit danger or create opportunities. It does not guarantee control over opponents or powers.

Command Class.name: Command Class
Command Class.description: A charisma-focused class built around leadership, coordination, authority, and motivating a team.
Command Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors clear communication, social leverage, planning, and maintaining group cohesion. Command does not grant authority over NPC choices or force obedience.

Bruiser Class.name: Bruiser Class
Bruiser Class.description: A strength-focused class built around close-range pressure, physical force, and taking space.
Bruiser Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors grappling, striking, lifting, breaking obstacles, and direct physical problem-solving. Strength does not guarantee success or require violence.

Powerhouse Class.name: Powerhouse Class
Powerhouse Class.description: A strength-focused class built around overwhelming force, heavy impacts, and exceptional physical output.
Powerhouse Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors feats of force, powerful attacks, carrying capacity, and physically imposing solutions. It does not grant invulnerability or unlimited exertion.

Skirmisher Class.name: Skirmisher Class
Skirmisher Class.description: A dexterity-focused class built around speed, mobility, repositioning, and opportunistic action.
Skirmisher Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors movement, initiative, escape routes, and adapting under pressure. It does not grant automatic evasion or immunity to danger.

Tech Class.name: Tech Class
Tech Class.description: An intelligence-focused class built around engineering, equipment, research, and technical problem-solving.
Tech Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors understanding devices, repairing systems, designing solutions, and using technology responsibly. It does not grant instant expertise or unrestricted equipment access.

Recon Class.name: Recon Class
Recon Class.description: A wisdom-focused class built around awareness, observation, scouting, and reading situations before acting.
Recon Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors noticing danger, tracking context, gathering information, and making careful decisions. Recon does not guarantee accurate conclusions or hidden information.

Diplomat Class.name: Diplomat Class
Diplomat Class.description: A charisma-focused class built around negotiation, trust-building, de-escalation, and navigating competing interests.
Diplomat Class.traitNarrativeEffects: Favors persuasion, mediation, reading social boundaries, and finding agreements without assuming consent or cooperation. Diplomacy does not guarantee trust or compliance.

Natural.name: Natural
Natural.description: The character's power emerged as a natural part of who they are: it was always there, grew with the body, and needs no trigger, device or bargain. The body is built around it.
Natural.traitNarrativeEffects: The power is as familiar to the character as a hand; they have never not had it, and their childhood, family and school records show it. Ask when it first showed, who noticed, and what they were told about it. It cannot be revoked, hacked or argued with, but it also has no one to blame and no manual: its limits were learned by living with it.

Inherited.name: Inherited
Inherited.description: The character received or developed the power through family, lineage or ancestry. The name came with it, and so did the expectations, the relatives, and the people who remember what the last one did.
Inherited.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask who in the family has or had the power, what the family expects, and what the character owes or refuses. Relatives with the same power are NPCs with opinions; the family's reputation precedes the character with institutions, factions and the press. The power's known family limits are public knowledge among those who know the name.

Accident.name: Accident
Accident.description: The character's power began through an accident, exposure, disaster, experiment or malfunction. They survived something, and what they carry out of it is the power and the memory.
Accident.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what happened, who else was there, what was lost, and whether anyone is responsible. The accident is a matter of record somewhere: medical files, a news item, a company that would rather it stayed quiet. The character knows what an emergency feels like from the inside, which is why they move first when one happens; the power may still be unstable in the ways the accident was.

Artificial.name: Artificial
Artificial.description: The character's power was created, implanted, engineered or enabled through technology or cybernetics. Someone built it, someone can maintain it, and someone has the schematics.
Artificial.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask who made it, why, what it needs (power, maintenance, parts, updates), and whether the maker still has a say. The power has documentation and dependencies: it can be serviced, upgraded, damaged, remotely affected or legally contested. The character understands their own mechanism better than most people understand their phone, and other engineers notice.

Training.name: Training
Training.description: The character developed the power through disciplined practice, study, ritual or specialised instruction. Nothing about it was free; every edge was drilled, and the teacher's voice is still in their head.
Training.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask who taught them, what the discipline forbids, what the next lesson would be, and what they still cannot do. A trained power is deliberate: the character knows their limits exactly, rarely overreaches by accident, and reads other people's powers as a practitioner. Their school or master is an NPC with standards and a reputation that attaches to the student.

Contract.name: Contract
Contract.description: The character gained the power through an agreement with a person, being, artifact, faction or force. The terms exist, the other party exists, and the price is still being paid.
Contract.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask who the other party is, what the terms say, what was promised in return, and what happens if the character breaks them. The other party is an NPC with interests and a way to collect; the contract's terms are exact and known to the character. People who deal in agreements recognise a contractor, and the character has learned to read a bargain.

Cursed.name: Cursed
Cursed.description: The character's power was imposed or awakened through a curse, relic, ritual or supernatural event. They did not ask for it, cannot give it back, and have learned to live with what it costs.
Cursed.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the curse is, what it takes from the character, what eases it, and who or what laid it. The curse has a cost that is paid regardless of whether the power is used; the character is good at enduring, improvising and making do, because they have had to be. Those who know curses can see the marks; a cure or a lifting is a quest, never a line.

Alien Origin.name: Alien Origin
Alien Origin.description: The character's power is connected to extraterrestrial biology, technology or an astral source. Earth is not quite where it belongs, and the character has spent their life working out what that means.
Alien Origin.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what the connection is, what gave it away, who on Earth knows, and what the power needs that Earth may not provide. Government, agency and faction attention follows the suspicion of an off-world origin; the character has learned to investigate, because nobody else could tell them what they are. The power's needs and vulnerabilities are unlike human ones.

Transformation.name: Transformation
Transformation.description: The character's power began through a permanent or recurring transformation of body or state. The body is not the one they were born with, or not always, and it is stronger for it.
Transformation.traitNarrativeEffects: Ask what changed, whether it recurs or holds, what triggers it, and what of the old self remains.
